items.body:
Remastered from the original tapes by Robin Guthrie and reissued on vinyl for the first time, 'The Moon and the Melodies' is one of the Cocteau Twins' most sublime sets, a blissful marriage of horizontal piano-laced ambience and glistening dream pop.

"It's not Cocteau Twins, and it's not me," Budd said in a 1986 interview, "it's an odd combination peculiar to the mixture." He'd never heard the band until bassist Simon Raymonde reached out to cover 'Not Yet Remembered' from his 'Ambient 2: Plateaux of Mirror' collaboration with Brian Eno. Although the cover never materialised, Budd was struck by the trio's music and after a meeting in Los Angeles, they began to consider a full collaboration. 'The Moon and the Melodies' appeared at a good time, Budd had recently released his syrupy masterpiece 'The Pearl', and Cocteau Twins had sailed further into abstraction with their beatless oddity 'Victorialand'. The album also marked the end of an era for Guthrie, Raymonde and Liz Fraser, catching them on the cusp of their later shift towards more identifiable pop, and integrating Budd's signature languid piano worked seamlessly. Just check 'Memory Gongs', still one of the most pristine entries in either act's repertoire - seven and a half minutes of rubbery, tremolo piano reverberations and muggy, billowing soundscapes. 

But the big draw will no doubt be opener 'Sea, Swallow Me', a more recognisable Cocteaus cut that's had a new lease of life since it became a viral hit on TikTok, of all places. It's now one of the band's most recognisable (and most streamed) songs, and Budd's serene arpeggios take on a slightly different form when they're balanced with Guthrie's shimmering riffs, Raymonde's driving basslines and Fraser's soaring voice. The four alternate between proper songs and ambient reflections, as if they're each paying attention to each other's strengths while attempting to experiment. "It turned out like four songs that sounded like us and four songs that sounded like him, which wasn't really the plan," remembers Guthrie. And it's interesting that when it was originally released, the album was credited to each musician, rather than being listed as a Cocteau Twins album; indeed, Raymonde recalls that the sessions were enjoyably un-premeditated. "It captured a moment in time between friends that are enjoying making music together," he explains. "Really, that's the essence of it."

Elsewhere, Dif Juz's Richard Thomas plays sax on two of the album's most crushing tracks: the jangly, anthemic 'She Will Destroy You' and the cloudy 'The Ghost Has No Home'. The latter is one of the Budd-forward tracks, and stretches into the abyss with his piano fainting into Thomas's echoing horns and Guthrie's tempered, chiming guitar phrases. It's hardly surprising that the album marked the beginning of a collaboration between Guthrie and Budd that would eventually give us the iconic 'Mysterious Skin' soundtrack in 2005.

'The Moon and the Melodies' has never sounded better; it's aged well, pulling away from the expectations that caused some critics to misunderstand it when it emerged almost four decades ago, gradually establishing itself as a stylistic milestone in the years since.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Cocteau Twins与极简主义钢琴家Harold Budd的合作产物，重新混音并首次以黑胶形式再版。作品将横向铺展的钢琴氛围与闪烁的梦幻流行交织，Budd慵懒的钢琴音色与Guthrie的颤音吉他、Raymonde的低音线以及Fraser空灵的嗓音形成对话。专辑在结构上交替呈现完整歌曲与氛围化片段，Richard Thomas的萨克斯出现在两首较沉重的曲目中。制作过程被描述为无预设的即兴交流，捕捉了朋友间共度创作时光的瞬间。这一合作也开启了Guthrie与Budd后续的电影配曲之路。整体而言，这是一次跨界融合的实践——梦幻流行的质感与现代古典的克制手法相互渗透。

items.body:
Returning after a decade-long break with none other than Isis/Sumac frontman Aaron Turner at the helm, Neurosis move into a new era with their sickest album since the iconic 'Through Silver in Blood'. Tipped!

It would have been easy to assume that Neurosis would have folded after guitarist and vocalist Scott Kelly, one of the band's founder members, was dismissed following domestic abuse allegations. Indeed, as late as in January last year, it looked like things were fizzling out when drummer Jason Roeder claimed he was ready to sell his music equipment and retire from touring. And it would have made sense, too; Neurosis have been active since the mid-1980s and defined a sound that would evolve into "post-metal", pulling influence from hardcore, prog, industrial music, ambient and sludge and inspiring a legion of followers. They never really lost their mojo, either - even their last album, 2016's Steve Albini-recorded 'Fires Within Fires' was pretty universally regarded as one of that year's best metal releases. But truth be told, they'd started to repeat themselves; locked into Kelly's grim, agonized lyrics, they were starting to sound like their own gloomy tribute act. If it was the end, they'd had a good run.

So 'An Undying Love...' is in many senses a total surprise Not only is the band back, re-energised, but they have a new vocalist and guitarist in tow: Turner, whose old band Isis were arguably the most important members of post-metal's second wave. You might consider the new Neurosis lineup as the ultimate post-metal supergroup, then, and 'An Undying Love...' is the record that proves the credentials of everyone involved. Unlike its tight, almost too brief predecessor, this album is a return to the epic, sprawling songwriting that both Neurosis and Isis perfected at their respective peaks. And it's incredibly expansive, too; anyone who's been following Turner in recent years will already know how open-minded he is, whether it's with his work with Moor Mother and Keiji Haino as Sumac or his various genre-bending collaborations. Here, there's an extra layer to the Neurosis sound that fills out their sludgy, lurching epics with the meticulously engineered haze of Isis's milestone 'Oceanic'.

Where Neurosis's last few albums had been shaped by their long-time collaboration with Albini, this one sounds like a clean break, mixed and recorded by Oakland's Scott Evans, who worked on Turner's Sumac records. It's still Neurosis, with those slow, almost symphonic atmospheres and the unmistakably tight rhythm section, but there's even more going on here, whether it's the unsettlingly effective breakdowns that often replace the band's usual instruments with synths and pounding drum machines, or the stacked feedback loops and scratches that fill their riffs with even more tension. Turner's lyrics, too, offer the band a new dimension to explore. "The separation that burns our hearts / is the root of all our disease," he bellows on the opener 'We Are Torn Wide Open' over radio interference. "We've forgotten how to live so we suffer." Self-referential in their own way at first, they move on as the band does, rolling through themes of environmental collapse, division and redemption. 

It's worth it just for the payoff delivered by the album's side-long finale 'Last Light', shifting from hi-BPM dark gabber into pure symphonic sludge, using its hefty runtime to properly display what this nu-Neurosis (NeurIsis?) is capable of. Really, it's not just the band's most vital record in years, it's one of the best metal albums we've heard in way, way too long.
items._cn_summary: Neurosis在经历十年沉寂与主创离队后，邀请Isis/Sumac主唱Aaron Turner加入，以全新阵容回归。专辑被乐评视为乐队自《Through Silver in Blood》以来最出色的作品，彻底告别了与Steve Albini长期合作形成的紧致短促风格，回归史诗级、绵长铺陈的作曲路线。Turner的开阔视野为乐队带来新层次，将Isis里程碑《Oceanic》中精细雕琢的氛围迷雾融入Neurosis沉重的sludge riff。制作人Scott Evans（曾操刀Sumac专辑）为这张作品带来干净的断裂感，大量合成器、鼓机、反馈循环与噪音碎片取代传统器乐，制造出不安的爆发段落。Turner的歌词也开辟了新的探索维度，与乐队一贯的黑暗沉重内核形成互补，构成一张兼具传承与革新的后金属巨作。

items.album: Parallel Worlds :: Explorer (Neo Ouija)
items.excerpt: Explorer is a richly detailed journey through melodic ambient electronics and progressive textures, where Parallel Worlds transforms the mystery, beauty, and endless motion of deep space into nine immersive sonic voyages. Our journeys into space remind us to look up and stay curious Explorer by Parallel Worlds   Strange prog rock tinged ambient electronic music that captures much of the experience of being in space, each track is a unique haunting melody, a jeweled glass music box to explor
items.body: Explorer is a richly detailed journey through melodic ambient electronics and progressive textures, where Parallel Worlds transforms the mystery, beauty, and endless motion of deep space into nine immersive sonic voyages. Our journeys into space remind us to look up and stay curious Explorer by Parallel Worlds   Strange prog rock tinged ambient electronic music that captures much of the experience of being in space, each track is a unique haunting melody, a jeweled glass music box to explore. Space travel is glamorous. The feeling of floating and bouncing around without gravity captures much of the imagination, there are nine journeys into the dark infinity of space, covered with distant star clusters and galaxies. I hear a very idiosyncratic language of unmistakable electronic beeps, tocks and ticks, constructed of weaving intricate nimble rapid cyclic interactions. A clockwork of multiple interacting moving parts, with engaging craftsmanship and a polished presentation. Here on Earth, our journeys into space remind us to look up and stay curious. World creating music makes cosmic galactic travel go smoothly, the machines are built to run forever, in pursuit of intimate lunar mysteries, to break through the light barriers, and search for life among the stars. Our universe is a wide and wonderful place. The cover design is by LoMo, and the sound was mastered by Lorenzo Montana, all Parallel Worlds Explorer tracks were composed, arranged and produced by Bakis Sirros during 2025 using Eurorack modular (including modules by Qu-Bit, Synthesis Technology, Make Noise, Instruo, Xaoc Devices, Frap Tools, Doepfer, 4ms company, Noise Engineering, Buchla Tiptop Audio, Befaco, Neuzeit, Strymon, Steady State Fate, Cosmotronic, Hexinverter, Industrial Music Electronics, Endorphin.es, Behringer and others), Analogue Systems RS-Integrator modular, Roland System-8, korg Prologue, Wavestate, Opsix, SQ64, MS2000R, ASM Hydrasynth, Novation Peak, Kodamo EssenceFM mk2, Yamaha TG77, Waldorf Microwave, Behringer Model-D. Opening with a melody from outer space, bearing a melodic easy tempo, mysterious, fast and pleasant, “Bendophonic” (7:15) builds into upbeat frisky and color-rich flocks of electronic birds, the speed of lots of voices combines as one message, slowly things are starting to get dark. The bright blue sky quickly turns pitch black as we climb higher. The orchestra awakens in a new galaxy :: The bass brings us in slow and low, followed with electronic snaps and buzzy drones, the layers build, a keyboard sets up the framework and away we go, “Phase” (5:18). Tricky percussion percolates in like cocoa, I hear sinister steps behind me, casting long gloomy shadows haunting desolate and dark, I am enjoying the ride, now it ends. The orchestra awakens in a new galaxy, “Still Unknown” (4:26), always calling out,  seeking a signal in return, forming a jammin’ bass percussion line revealing visions from outer space, an old ceremonial contemplative ritual that takes centuries to repeat. Perhaps a strange question hangs in the melody. Engines shut off and you instantly float, moving in several dimensions like flying. Opening like an almost forgotten television series, “Persistence” (5:17) brings lots of moving parts that fit together and create a cyclic pattern that evolves and adds new dimensions as it goes. The immense spiral gyre comes overflowing into the shoreline, with lots of details and layered repetition, humans are learning how to live and work in space. “Patience” (6:30) starts slow, a spider web of moonlight, playing on spiral glass bowls dark with roses and silver, genty struck ringing bell glass objects, a dance finish, very sparse and swooning in places. Astronauts often spend extended amounts of time in space, always to pave the way for even longer, future exploration missions. After riding across the night sky forever, “Fullmoon” (7:02) paints a picture. The moonlight now has more colors than just silver, but the picture started with silver, honoring the children of the night. Here there are all kinds of colors and a choppy moist energetic beat holding strong all through the track. It seems that they come from the sky, with complex weaving layers of beat and melodic themes being ground quite finely. These repeating cycles add new beeps and buzzing strangesounds that change, new strangesounds held on the same rhythm as one flow, slowly turning in the hall of mirrors, “Soundwise” (5:17). We are making some dreamy dark distance as the machine beats and bips along, weaving its patterns with plenty of mysterious electronic atmospheric details. With many a light-year to go tonight, tonight feels different. “Tonight” (5:22) breaks out with chimes followed by a strong bass, a triumphant journey into percussive synergy, with some tight jams and electronic voices answering and calling. Now I hear little dancing robots with period costumes, perhaps telling another story about another night in another place and it fits tonight here at last. The climax, “Octo” (7:08) opens with a question posed by an electronic voice. I do not know what it is saying in the icy darkness. I hear a buzzy beat box click in, which takes the ever cycling helix pattern in a strong new direction, into another new hall of mirrors. Somehow, midway things drop out. We drift for a moment, but ultimately the ride continues forever, nothing changes anymore, we just cycle and look into infinity all around.​ Explorer is available on Neo Ouija. [Bandcamp] Explorer by Parallel WorldsThe post Parallel Worlds :: Explorer (Neo Ouija) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 这是希腊裔制作人 Bakis Sirros 以 Parallel Worlds 名义发行的专辑《Explorer》，以深空旅行为核心意象，通过九首曲目构建沉浸式的环境电子音景。制作上完全依赖 Eurorack 模块化合成器系统及 Roland System-8、Korg Prologue/Wavestate/Opsix、Waldorf Microwave 等硬件设备，强调模拟信号的物理质感与声音设计的实验深度。评论描述其音乐语言充满怪异的电子嗡鸣声、滴答声与精密交织的节奏循环，呈现出类似钟表机械般的多层互动结构。在旋律与渐进式音墙之间，作品既保留了流畅的太空主题旋律线，又通过键盘框架和层次叠加引入渐进摇滚式的张力展开。评论特别指出每首曲目都拥有独特的旋律个性，从色彩丰富的电子音簇到阴郁的低音脉冲，呈现丰富的情绪光谱。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — The album "An Ambassador in Bonds" is as good (and atmospheric) as the first one. The same turns and twists, the same "Petersburg" mood of the Silver Age of Russian poetry. Poetic images are felt in every note. If the poets of this era could clothe their words in music, then it would be just like that. The alternation of light and dark sections of musical constructions reminds me of Russian periods in general, without which they do not exist. Either wandering in search of the meaning of existence, then the joy of finding it run like a red thread through the tracks and lead the audience out of any dead end that prevents them from reaching the heights of flaming optimism. Listen to this! And you will have an even greater desire to learn, to work and to make yourself. Further wishes to this collective: "move" their works towards symphonic ones. And there it is not far from ready-made requiems.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张延续首张专辑氛围气质的RIO/前卫摇滚作品。乐评将音乐比作俄罗斯白银时代诗歌的声响化呈现，认为每段旋律都浸透着诗意思象。光暗交替的结构类似于俄罗斯文学中的经典转折手法——既有对存在意义的漫长求索，也有顿悟时刻迸发的喜悦。专辑通过多重情绪转换引导听众穿越低谷，抵达乐观之境。乐评建议乐队在未来的创作中进一步靠向交响化方向，认为其作品距离成熟的安魂曲式结构并不遥远。作为俄罗斯厂牌发行的前卫摇滚专辑，其将诗歌意象转化为器乐叙事的手法体现了独特的文化视角。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — I hear a voice from a beautiful Canterbury far-away? It plunged me into memories of seemingly unlike each other things ? 1) of course, the bands of "Canterbury periods", and 2) music of the Soviet time ? for films, tales, etc. Now then ? it would seem evident ? Russia and England are similar in spontaneously natural musical feeling. This is even so. I hope that this experience will not be lost, and we will hear its numerous incarnations further ? everywhere. The album abounds in "natural", that is, sounds-of-nature-imitating instruments. There are not only classical "multi-orchestral" opuses, but also sounds of raindrops, knock of twigs on roof, and other spontaneously planetary sonorities. As well as we can hear typical for this group "entries" into the other countries ? for example, Japan (tracks 3 and 4), England (tracks 7 ? 9), Spain, etc. And that is good! Requests ? I would like to listen to more depth and precision of each instrument's sound. In all other respects, Patience of Hope (my nickname Naida in Russian almost implies Hope in English) has been satisfied. I rate 5, first of all, for "primary nature" of the stuff.
items._cn_summary: 俄罗斯前卫摇滚乐队ROZ VITALIS的专辑将坎特伯雷流派的优雅旋律与苏联时期电影音乐的自然情感相融合，在传统前卫摇滚框架中注入多国文化色彩。专辑运用模拟自然声响的乐器——雨滴敲击、树枝轻叩屋顶等环境音色，与管弦乐编制交织，营造出跨地域的声音旅行。日本、英国、西班牙等不同地域的音乐元素在曲目中各占段落，形成色彩丰富的拼贴结构。评论者指出演奏层次尚可深化，希望各乐器音色更为精准，但整体认可其自然质朴的艺术取向。独立厂牌RIO发行保证了小众实验空间，作为来自俄罗斯的坎特伯雷风格尝试，在地域文化融合方面具有独特价值。

On the cornfields of progressive rock ? so far ? there is an abundance of both yield gathered from past harvests and new richly ear-forming implantations. The first part of the album ? including 5th track ? reflects it with all moods of joys and sorrows in days of old. Starting with 6th composition Christian outlook prevails over. Thinking about the meaning of life ? listen to track 10 ? is the very explicit validation of it. The brief description of songs according to their mood:Track 1: urge towards the cognizance of the world.Track 2: rest from vain world.Track 3: pure psychedelia.Tracks 4-6: medieval epos.Track 7: Renaissance era.Track 8: thoughtful Russian field.Tracks 9-11: the conclusion is that you have cognized the world nevertheless ? to the ingratiating sounds of hearts of every instrument sounding here. It is not enough nevertheless. To be continued?
items._genre: avant-prog / progressive rock / psychedelic / folk fusion
items._cn_summary: 乐评以斯拉夫民间叙事为框架，将ROZ VITALIS这张作品置于前卫摇滚的语境中审视。开篇即引入丰收意象与古斯拉夫部族迎朝阳的比喻，将乐队与Steven Wilson及Van Der Graaf Generator进行比较。整张专辑被视作一部贯穿中世纪、文艺复兴至俄罗斯田园的史诗，前五轨承载喜怒哀乐等古典情绪，第六首起基督教哲思逐渐主导，第十轨构成对生命意义的直白追问。器乐层面，乐评强调每件乐器的交相鸣响，竖笛与小号等古朴音色与前卫编制交织，呈现认知世界、休憩尘世、纯粹迷幻等多重段落。整体气质融合前卫摇滚的结构感与斯拉夫民间传说的文化视角。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — The album QNQF has a more expressed harmonic-melodic component of the musical canvas of the band titled Roz Vitalis. It's like a narrative author's work, a fantastic epic for the film. The prologue, climax and epilogue of the narrative are clearly audible. We read music like a book, the letters of the notes will sound in our memory for a long time. The echoes of low whistle, flute and clarinet sound very natural and spontaneous. The harpsichord adds the harmonic thought of the Renaissance to the general background. The eastern rubab and doira in track 8 are an echo of the desert. It is pleasant to listen to the album in any mood. It both soothes and evokes a bright sadness at times that are pleasant for everyone to remember. For some, this is the period of childhood, for others - love for people and circumstances. This is a message to humanity in principle. It does not have to be pathos-heroic, it also happens to be lyrically romantic, like the next wonderful creation of this collective given to us.
items._cn_summary: Roz Vitalis 这张专辑呈现出鲜明的叙事性结构，从序曲到高潮再到尾声如同一部听觉史诗。和声与旋律线条突出，乐器编制丰富且跨文化：竖琴带来文艺复兴时期的和声思维，低音口哨、长笛与单簧管的音色自然流动，第八轨中东方鲁巴琴与手鼓则唤起沙漠意象。整体编排兼具抒情浪漫与戏剧张力，既可安抚情绪也能唤起明亮的忧伤，适合不同心境下反复聆听。专辑融合了前卫摇滚的复杂性、室内乐器的精致质感以及世界音乐的色彩，呈现出一种面向人类情感的普遍讯息。

items.album: Albumin

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由 Jim O'Rourke 与 Jos Smolders 合作完成，以即兴创作为核心，强调录音过程的即时性与不可预测性。评论者特别指出其封套设计中的红色意象与音乐内部的张力相呼应，暗示作品在色彩与声音之间建立了视觉化的隐喻。两位音乐人的合作延续了实验音乐领域跨界对话的传统，将电声处理、现场即兴与电子媒介相融合，形成一种介于作曲与偶发事件之间的结构。文章反复强调该专辑具有强烈的自发性，这种特质使得听者每次聆听都能获得不同的体验层次。整体而言，乐评聚焦于作品如何突破预设框架，在即兴与电声美学之间寻找平衡点，是面向实验音乐爱好者的值得关注之作。

items.body: Baltimore-based quintet Crying Laughing will release its debut album, Talking, on Tape, CD and digital formats on September 10, 2026, through Hausu Mountain. The band fuses saxophone-led minimalism in the Steve Reich, Terry Riley and Philip Glass tradition with post-punk energy and the rhythmic sensibility of Moondog’s street recordings. Talking by Crying Laughing “Talking” runs eight tracks: “Toppled Column,” “Bass Alarm,” “Tato,” “When They Come to Town You Must Exile,” “Ricemeat,” “Inner Life,” “Crocodopolis Theme” and “Geese Six.” Crying Laughing recorded the album in one day in a basement studio outside Baltimore, tracking each song as a live performance through a network of microphones and isolation booths set up by engineer Chris Freeland. Crying Laughing’s line-up and Baltimore connections Crying Laughing formed in 2024 around saxophonists Christian Best and Rose Hammer Burt, drummer Jen Kirby and bassist Marc Miller, joined by keyboardist Steve Strohmeier. Kirby and Best’s prior work together in the duo Smoke Bellow, which released albums on Trouble in Mind and Moon Glyph before ending in 2024, formed the group’s starting point. Miller founded the math-punk band OXES in 1998 and the experimental ensemble Microkingdom in 2006, while Strohmeier has recorded or toured with Beach House, Dan Deacon, Daniel Higgs and Lower Dens. Hammer Burt participates in Baltimore collectives connected to the venue The Red Room and its High Zero improvised-music festival. Hausu Mountain first became aware of the band through mutual friends in Horse Lords, whose line-up includes label artist Andrew Bernstein. Hausu Mountain describes “Talking” as a fusion of polymetric saxophone composition with the energy of post-punk and the rhythmic sensibilities of Moondog, calling it “head music as much as body music.” Saxophonist Christian Best described the band’s writing process: “Each song begins its life as a seed of an idea: a whole arrangement, specific rhythms, melodies, or sometimes just a theory of interaction. The band then collaboratively expands and later condenses those ideas down into their most concise form. Compositionally we aim to not encroach on each instrument’s space. All of us contribute to the overall rhythm and melody of each piece, trading roles and interweaving with each other.” Drummer Jen Kirby, who plays a modified kit with a small snare and tuned rototoms, described her own approach: “a response to the people I’m playing with and my natural technical limitations due to total hackery of technique.” About Crying Laughing Crying Laughing is a quintet based in Baltimore, Maryland, formed in 2024 by musicians who had already spent years in the city’s experimental music scene. Saxophonists Christian Best and Rose Hammer Burt lead the group’s dual-sax arrangements, with drummer Jen Kirby and bassist Marc Miller forming the rhythm section and Steve Strohmeier adding keyboards, harmonium, piano and marimba. Kirby and Best previously played together in Smoke Bellow, which released records on Trouble in Mind and Moon Glyph before the band ended in 2024. Miller’s other projects include the math-punk band OXES, formed in 1998, and the experimental ensemble Microkingdom, formed in 2006. Strohmeier has recorded or toured with Beach House, Dan Deacon, Daniel Higgs and Lower Dens, and Hammer Burt performs in Baltimore’s Red Room and High Zero improvised-music circles. Crying Laughing joins Hausu Mountain with “Talking,” its debut album, recorded live in a single day at a basement studio outside Baltimore with engineer Chris Freeland.
items._cn_summary: Crying Laughing 是一支来自巴尔的摩的五重奏乐队，首张专辑《Talking》以萨克斯为核心，将极简主义作曲手法（Steve Reich、Terry Riley、Philip Glass 传统）与后朋克的能量及 Moondog 街头音乐的节奏感融为一体。专辑共收录八首作品，所有录音在一天之内于巴尔的摩郊外的地下室工作室完成，采用现场同期录音方式，通过分布于各隔离间内的麦克风网络进行捕捉。乐队成员背景多元：成员此前活跃于巴尔的摩实验音乐圈，分别来自 Smoke Bellow、OXES、Microkingdom 等乐队，并曾与 Beach House、Dan Deacon、Daniel Higgs 等合作。作品强调乐手间的即兴互动与节奏互换，追求在编曲层面不侵占彼此的声部空间，呈现出兼具头脑性与身体性的复合质地。

items.body: About two years after the EP “Love Me Now (Not)”, American artist Azul Far returns with the debut album from her sonic alter ego, The True Union. Production duties were handled by Travis Bacon and Sebastian Komor, with additional contributions on selected tracks from Jamie Cronander (Combichrist), Hellhammer (Mayhem), and Tony Särkkä (Abruptum/Ophthalamia). If you were already familiar with the EP, this album will hit you with even greater intensity. A palpable sense of rage runs throughout the record, fueled by personal experiences and emotional turmoil. Call the result Metal, Industrial, or simply a fusion of both—occasionally enriched with symphonic arrangements. Dark, aggressive, EBM-infused basslines further reinforce the album’s power, while Azul Far’s vocal versatility proves equally impressive. She effortlessly shifts between ferocious outbursts and more melodic, almost Pop-oriented passages, even as the music charges forward like a runaway train. The songs are short, uncompromising, and explosively powerful, giving the album the impact of a sonic blitzkrieg—it is over almost before you realize it. The True Union is a relentless listening experience that leaves little room to catch your breath. It is a fierce and uncompromising debut that is sure to claim plenty of victims—or rather, devoted new fans. (Rating:8). Side-Line first reported on the album’s Alfa Matrix release in April 2026, when “Sleepwalk” arrived as an 11-track digital album produced by Sebastian Komor. Listen to “One By One feat. Komor Kommando”: One By One (feat. Komor Kommando) by The True UnioN About The True Union The True Union is the industrial metal and dark electro project of American singer and composer Azul Far, founded in 2009. A 2022 Side-Line report on the act joining Alfa Matrix listed The True UnioN as a Dallas-based act in its opening line, while the same article’s detail section placed the project in Denver, Colorado; Side-Line has not resolved which city applied at the time of founding. The project was originally conceived as a studio-only outlet, with Far beginning to recruit musicians for live performance from 2017 onward. The True UnioN joined the Belgian label Alfa Matrix in 2022, first appearing on the label’s “Sounds From The Matrix 023” compilation with the track “Purousthai”. The same year, the project released the EP “Love Me Now (Not)” on Alfa Matrix, produced by Sebastian Komor with additional work from Siggi Bemm, Travis Bacon and guitarist Jamie Cronander (Combichrist). The EP also featured Azul Far’s guest vocals on “One By One”, a track written for the Komor Kommando EP of the same name, after Komor worked on production and mixing for The True Union. In March 2023, Azul Far discussed the project in a Side-Line interview titled “An order amongst the chaos!” The True Union’s debut full-length, “Sleepwalk”, followed in April 2026 on Alfa Matrix as an 11-track digital and CD album, again produced by Sebastian Komor, with additional contributions from Travis Bacon, Jamie Cronander, Hellhammer of Mayhem, and the late Tony “IT” Särkkä of Abruptum and Ophthalamia, who died in 2017.
items._cn_summary: 美国艺术家Azul Far以The True Union之名推出的首张专辑，由Travis Bacon和Sebastian Komor联合制作，另有Combichrist吉他手Jamie Cronander、Mayhem鼓手Hellhammer等客座参与。专辑延续此前的EP路线，情感驱动的愤怒贯穿始终，融合金属、工业与EBM元素，间或加入交响化编配。深沉的贝斯线构成骨架，人声在暴烈嘶吼与近乎流行化的旋律段落间自由切换。歌曲短促凌厉，整体如闪电战般密集轰炸。Alfa Matrix作为比利时独立厂牌为专辑发行提供了地下工业场景的归属感。专辑将个人经历转化为强烈的情绪宣泄，在类型框架内展现出一定的融合意识与执行力度。

items.album: Mikkel Rev / Evocation (ASIPV057)
items.body:
Enter the Magnetic Heliosphere. 

 Mikkel Rev returns to A Strangely Isolated Place with Evocation , his third full-length album shaped deep within the forests of Norway. 

 Since Mikkel’s debut, The Art of Levitation first arrived in 2023, Mikkel has been quietly building his own corner of the ASIP catalogue. Last year's Journey Beyond expanded that vision further, revealing an artist increasingly comfortable balancing the emotional pull of early trance with a more reflective, ambient-leaning approach. While his work elsewhere naturally gravitates towards the dance floor through his own collective, Ute Recordings and other club-focused outlets, his ASIP releases have always evolved differently. Beginning with a larger body of material that’s gradually shaped together, each album seeks to find a narrative without a dancefloor in place; one that moves naturally between momentum and stillness, carrying something of the spirit found in those early-'90s records that drifted effortlessly between peak-time energy and the quiet hours in room two. 

 astrangelyisolatedplace · Mikkel Rev / Evocation (ASIPV057) [Previews] 

 Long-form compositions like "Step Inside" and "MRI" favor gradual development over immediate impact, while "Dream Sand" introduces shimmering rhythms that subtly shift the album's momentum and pace. The piano-led "The Infinite" offers a definitive nod to the enduring emotional pull of classic trance before "Sanitorium" closes the record with one of Mikkel's most restrained and affecting pieces to date.

 Evocation continues Mikkel Rev's remarkable run on ASIP, extending a catalog where echoes of trance's formative years find new expression through the communal energy and natural surroundings of the Nordic forest gatherings that have become an integral part of his world.

 Ventral Is Golden returns on artwork duties, with Lupo handling the mastering and cut. Released on August 28th as a gatefold double LP on dusty purple smoke and digital.

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比两个小岛在1970至80年代非洲黄金时期录制的音乐Puxa。Puxa是一种融合了葡萄牙语非洲殖民地各种元素的复合节奏，融合了merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等风格，葡萄牙殖民历史和大西洋对岸加勒比的地理位置影响了其声音形成。乐评详细介绍了当地的音乐生态背景，指出由于缺乏大城市和录音厂牌，许多音乐未能得到充分记录。合辑展示了多把吉他交织盘旋的编制，主唱与和声交替呼应，节奏部分放手让鼓和吉他推动律动，呈现出适合长时间现场演奏的流动感。Pedro Lima的乐队以闷音吉他和鼓组的对抗充满张力，Africa Negra的作品则体现了人声让位于器乐展开的处理方式。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 厂牌第44号发行，收录贝宁传奇乐队 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 与作曲家兼巫毒教祭司 Antoine Dougbé 1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé 以其独特的 Cavacha 节奏闻名——一种源自列车节拍、由鼓手 Belobi Meridjo 开创的律动，曾在70年代中期席卷刚果流行乐坛。专辑融合古巴 son 与刚果伦巴元素，合成器与电吉他音色具有鲜明的80年代初质感，高帽主导的律动贯穿始终。与厂牌此前发行的 Poly-Rythmo 合辑相比，本作更突出 Afro-Cuban 影响的痕迹，且因 Dougbé 巫毒背景而带有独特的精神文化维度。录音生涯虽短暂——仅三张专辑与少量单曲——但密度极高，展现了一位非裔音乐人对节奏与宗教仪式的独到理解。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威Camilla Hole Trio的最新作品，相比前作将科幻合成器与传统素材结合的星际探索，此次选择回归大地，但仍将目光投向本国以外的民间音乐领域。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，爵士影响明显，首曲《Springleik》取材于挪威西部的传统舞蹈音乐。乐队成员角色并非固定不变——Egil Kalman与Knut Kvifte Nesheim起初在低音提琴和鼓上提供节奏支撑，随后Kalman的模块合成器与Nesheim的颤音琴被叠加进来增加色彩。乐曲进行中各乐器不断流动，Kalman的低音提琴接过旋律线与萨克斯齐奏，Nesheim进一步拓展节奏层次，整首作品呈现出强烈的即兴特质，最终由Hole再次吹响旋律收束。这种不拘泥于传统角色分配的方式，以及爵士、民谣与电子音色之间的自由对话，构成专辑的核心吸引力。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威演奏家组成的三重奏演绎，素材源自斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲，但呈现方式远离常规舞蹈音乐，更接近室内乐式的亲密对话。三位音乐家均长期致力于模糊流派边界，将民谣素材解构重组，挖掘旋律表层之下的暗流与隐喻。开篇选用的挪威塞特斯达尔地区小调暗含水妖传说与小提琴被视为魔鬼乐器的历史暗示，赋予作品一层不安的底色。演奏中旋律常在推进途中瓦解、碎裂并戛然而止，文本化的伴奏与稀疏的打击点缀取代了常规节奏铺底，整体倾向于对传统调式的深层探索而非简单复现。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._genre: experimental jazz / improvisation / world fusion / solo piano
items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家Omar Sosa在意大利Fazioli钢琴厅完成了一场长达两小时的独奏即兴录音，后期加入人声采样、打击乐、循环段和实地录音等稀疏元素，形成《Sendas》这张专辑。Sosa强调'不重复自己'的创作哲学，刻意回避风格归类，将爵士、拉丁、非洲节奏与古典传统融于一体，保留第一遍即兴的真实感。对他而言，创作是综合所有影响的全新方式，音乐旨在引导听众进入未知领域而非迎合既有分类。专辑以对琴弦的拨弦与抚摸开场，挖掘钢琴共鸣体的深层泛音，展现出冥想式的探索状态。作品反映了疫情封锁时期的精神反思，艺术家强调人类需要'扎根的音乐'与脉轮共振般的低频泛音。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / sound art / spoken word / documentary / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥枪支暴力幸存者社区实地录制的口述声音档案。录制地点选在南城一栋九十多岁老人家的前廊下，毗邻中途机场降落航线，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，二十五位受枪支暴力影响的人自发参与讲述。整张作品没有任何添加的音乐，只有现场环境声与人物独白，包括一位失去两个儿子的老人反复道歉的哽咽片段。项目恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥当日完成，所有收益捐给反暴力公益组织。作为田野录音与声音艺术的跨界实践，专辑将社会现实以原声方式保存，编辑在文中坦言无法以常规乐评方式处理，故直接呈现录音师本人批注与录音片段，让被遗忘的社区声音本身成为作品主体。

items.body: Saudade is usually a backward-facing feeling, a longing for what has passed. Matu Miranda points it the other way. On “Céu Azulzin” the Brazilian singer and guitarist treats that longing as forward motion, a pull toward somewhere rather than a mourning for something lost. Miranda’s own writing pulls MPB together with jazz, soul and the music of the Northeast. He shares “Céu Azulzin” with Josyara, who comes from Juazeiro in Bahia, the town that raised João Gilberto, and plays with a percussive right hand rooted in the Afro-Brazilian music of the Bahian Recôncavo. Producer Leonardo Marques recorded it at his Ilha do Corvo studio, keeping the sound warm and organic, the two guitars and voices held close together. “Céu Azulzin” is the second single from Apuama, out 4 September, an album built as a travel diary about making a home while staying in motion. The single holds one piece of that journey: the kind of home you carry with you instead of returning to. Stream and listen to “Céu Azulzin” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Matu Miranda – Céu Azulzin (Featuring Josyara) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: MPB / Brazilian jazz / folk fusion / Afro-Brazilian
items._cn_summary: Matu Miranda 的单曲《Céu Azulzin》将 MPB 与爵士、灵魂乐及巴西东北部传统音乐融合，邀请来自巴伊亚州的 Josyara 合作，以右手拨弦的打击感致敬非洲-巴西音乐根源。制作人 Leonardo Marques 在 Ilha do Corvo 工作室录制，音色温暖有机，两把吉他与人声紧密交织。这首歌是专辑 Apuama 的第二首单曲，整张专辑以旅途日记的形式展开，探讨在流动中构建家园的主题。歌曲将 saudade 重新解读为向前的牵引力而非对失去的哀悼，传递出随身携带的归属感。发行渠道独立，整体呈现兼具地域色彩与现代融合质感。

items.body: Review by D0BR0 — As a huge Van Der Graaf Generator fan this album blew my mind. My favorite. There was somethingabout the spatial mixing of sound in this album. It was like the music was all around in 3D. Adifferent sounding experience for me from already stellar music and sound from just about everyother album. The lyrics took on a different meaning for me at the time personally. The pale personfor example.Guy Evans is easily one of my favorite drummers. I may like him even more than Carl Palmer now whoused to be my favorite drummer. The King Crimson like sounding songs were great with Fripp evenhelping them.A personal story. As some kind of strange correspondence with the album title I decided to go for mypersonal World Record of altered state. Left was right and right was left and I fought some dwarf atthe top room of a tower. Album got me through and became utterly personal for me. The last song title "Wondering" is a question by the band. And my answer is resounding YES!. Increation, we are creating ourselves in a contradiction that is a sure sign of God.
items._cn_summary: 这张1976年的专辑延续了Van der Graaf Generator一贯的实验性前卫摇滚路线。评论者特别强调了唱片在空间混音上的独特处理，音乐仿佛以三维环绕的方式包围听者，营造出沉浸式听觉体验。Guy Evans的鼓击被赞为极具表现力，甚至可与Carl Palmer比肩。专辑邀请Robert Fripp参与，使部分曲目呈现出King Crimson式的张力与棱角。评论者以个人化的方式描述聆听体验，将专辑与自身的精神探索联系起来，歌词在特定时刻承载了私人意义。整体而言，这是一张在声音设计、演奏技艺和情感深度上均有所突破的前卫摇滚作品，适合对实验性乐队音乐感兴趣的听众深入聆听。

items.body: Swedish dark synthpop trio Priest will release the single “Python” on August 21 via Blue Nine, the first taste of their fifth studio album, “Altered State Police,” due October 23 on the same label. The announcement follows the band’s US tour supporting Stabbing Westward. “Python” turns surveillance and data collection into subject matter, built around relentless electronics, industrial textures and flashes of ’90s big beat. The track includes a spoken sequence cataloguing a listener’s data: “Terms accepted. Surveillance initiated. Facial data: stored. Iris response: logged. Voice patterns: catalogued. You are now a consumer profile. Thank you for agreeing.” Priest describe it as one of their most direct and danceable songs to date, addressing “what happens when we’ve accepted being watched without even noticing.” “Altered State Police” is designed as a continuous listening experience rather than a loose collection of songs, built around surveillance, political distrust, technological dependence and the boundary between human and machine, with songs written to answer questions raised elsewhere on the record. Neither the single nor the album has surfaced yet on Bandcamp, YouTube or Spotify; Priest’s official site, priestnexus.com, currently carries the “Python” and “Altered State Police” announcement and upcoming tour information. The single follows Priest’s run on the Wither ReWired Tour, the 2026 US trek on which Stabbing Westward re-recorded “Wither Blister Burn + Peel” for its 30th anniversary, with Priest and Acumen Nation as support. Priest ‘Python’: release details “Python” arrives August 21 via Blue Nine as the first single from “Altered State Police,” out October 23 on the same label. No tracklist, credits or formats for the album have been confirmed at the time of writing. About Priest Priest is a dark synthpop trio from Stockholm, Sweden, formed in 2017 by former members of Ghost: vocalist Mercury (previously the bassist known as Water in Ghost) and keyboardist Salt (previously the keyboardist known as Air in Ghost), later joined by keyboardist and programmer Sulfur. The band’s sound draws on 1980s sci-fi synth textures, gothic soundscapes and industrial and cyberpunk elements, distinct from Ghost’s horror-rock theatrics. Priest released its debut album, “New Flesh,” in 2017, followed by the “Obey” EP in 2019 and the album “Cyberhead” in 2020. The band signed to Cleopatra Records in 2021 and released the single “A Signal in the Noise” that December. Further releases include the “Chaos EP,” the live album “Live in Hollywood,” the studio album “Dark Pulse” and, in March 2026, “Body Machine.” Priest has since moved to the label Blue Nine, which issues “Python” and the forthcoming “Altered State Police.” Priest has toured internationally in support of its releases, most recently opening for Stabbing Westward’s Wither ReWired Tour across the United States in 2026. “Python,” out August 21, and “Altered State Police,” out October 23, mark the band’s next chapter under Blue Nine.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典暗潮合成器三人组Priest即将发布第五张专辑《Altered State Police》，先行单曲《Python》以监控与数据采集为主题，将不间断的电子节拍、工业质感音色与九十年代big beat元素交织，并嵌入一段口语化的数据清点序列，构成对当代数字监控社会的直接回应。专辑被构想为连续聆听体验，围绕监视、政治不信任、技术依赖以及人机边界等议题展开，歌曲之间相互呼应而非松散拼凑。乐队成员曾参与Ghost项目，音乐风格以八十年代科幻合成器质感、哥特声景与赛博朋克元素为基底，与Ghost的恐怖摇滚戏剧化路线形成区别。该文本为新闻发布性质的报道，侧重发行信息与背景介绍，对音乐本身的深度评论有限，但题材与声音设计取向与暗潮工业领域契合。

items.excerpt: Diego Romo’s Are The Lovers moves with the heavy, deliberate gait of something crawling out from beneath a nightclub after closing time, wearing somebody else’s leather jacket and carrying a grin that suggests the evening went either very well…or catastrophically wrong. items.body: Diego Romo’s Are The Lovers moves with the heavy, deliberate gait of something crawling out from beneath a nightclub after closing time, wearing somebody else’s leather jacket and carrying a grin that suggests the evening went either very well…or catastrophically wrong. The 24-year-old Chilean artist drags alternative rock, post-punk, synthwave, and gothic excess into the same dim room, then lets them eye one another suspiciously over the bassline. The opening seconds establish a pace somewhere between a stalk and a crawl, allowing each low note to land with the authority of a hostile bouncer. The sinister bass is the song’s center of gravity: thick, slow, and almost indecently physical. Around it, guitars grind without turning the track into a blunt-force exercise, while electronic textures give the production a futuristic chill. Strange sucking sounds appear between phrases, an inspired bit of studio mischief that makes the song feel as though it might latch on to your neck while you are busy admiring the chorus. Romo’s voice hangs above the arrangement in sheets of echo, cool enough to seem composed yet close enough to carry an unmistakable sense of appetite. “This song is what I imagine would happen if Queens of the Stone Age and Nine Inch Nails decided to write a song for sex in the year 2079,” he says. One suspects the year 2079 will involve worse rent, smaller apartments, and considerably less flattering latex wear. Are The Lovers shares Queens of the Stone Age’s narcotic strut and Nine Inch Nails’ industrial unease, but Romo also reaches toward Depeche Mode’s decadent electronics, Type O Negative’s funereal sensuality, and the sleek night-drive menace associated with the late Kavinsky. The Horrors hover nearby in the track’s smeared textures, while the Arctic Monkeys comparison surfaces through its slow, knowing posture. Seduction becomes more interesting when a little spice enters the room. Are The Lovers plods forward with purpose, leaving enough space for every drum hit, vocal echo, and unidentifiable mouth-like noise to register. Listen to Are The Lovers below: Are The Lovers presents Diego Romo as an artist with a firm grasp of atmosphere and a healthy suspicion of daylight. His mix of rock mythology, cyberpunk imagery, vampiric desire, and electronic menace could easily collapse into costume drama, yet the song maintains a sharp sense of control. It is sensual, strange, and slightly ridiculous in precisely the right proportions, which is often where rock music starts behaving properly again. items.body:
2nd wave dub techno staple Stephen Hitchell meets new wave producer Federson in a back ’n forth of timeless originals and versions.

San Francisco’s Chris Kelly, aka Federsen’s Alt Dub label hosts this passing of the baton/torch with CV313 and Echospace figure Hitchell a sits 2nd release after the ‘Positive Charge’ EP  christened the vessel in earlier ’24. Federsen fronts the session with a smoky, night-driving dub of CV313’s ‘Skycrossing’ in properly classic Maurizio style, especially that scooping bassline, whilst shutting it down with the more air-stepping levity of his dusted congas and distant dub chords to ‘Skyway’.

CV313’s original ‘Skycrossing’ places his mastery of constantly shifting, ever the same, dynamic within its unfurling envelopes, alongside a remix of ‘Skyway’ that plunges upward, outward into billowing electro-acoustic dub techno dimensions.
items._genre: dub techno / deep ambient / minimal electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是底特律/芝加哥系深层 dub techno 传统的当代延续，由 Echospace 核心人物 Stephen Hitchell 与旧金山制作人 Federsen 共同完成。Hitchell 的原创作品延续了他一贯的缓慢展开手法，在层层递进的合成器音墙中维持极简律动，'Skycrossing' 以不断变化却始终如一的动态结构铺陈，'Skyway' 混音版则向更宽广的电声融合维度延伸。Federsen 贡献的版本以烟雾感的夜行 dub 风格重组原作，参考 Maurizio 经典美学，低频饱满、混响深远，conga 与远距 dub 和弦交织出漂浮感。整体维持了该流派的高度内省气质，音色考究但风格上并未突破既有范式，适合深夜聆听的氛围型电子乐爱好者。

items.body:
DJ Sprinkles' classic Midtown 120 Blues, self-released by Terre Thaemlitz through their Comatonse imprint and finally available again.

Bringing deep house back into contact with its club culture roots, Terre Thaemlitz created one of the most essential house albums of the last two decades with 'Midtown 120 Blues'. Terre was originally working as a DJ under her Sprinkles alias in the gay clubs of midtown Manhattan and New Jersey in the late 80's when deep house began to blossom. It's this early period of House history which Terre has beautifully recreated over 10 tracks, making a pointed comment with the intro track taking shots at Strictly Rhythm for becoming 'Strictly Vocal' and pulling no punches towards "Most Europeans who think deep house means shitty hi-NRG vocal house".

With the intentions made clear, Terre develops a masterpiece of serene melancholy and sublime deep house crafted with the skill and dedication of someone who you know lived this music through every fibre of their being. From the rich subbass driven tones of 'Midtown 120 Blues' with plaintive pianos slowly encircling one another, to drag queen monologues over the deepest ambient brushed rhythms on 'Ball'r (Madonna-Free Zone)' or head-meltingly warm chords and caressed percussion of 'Brenda's $20 dilemna' - this will suck in and swallow you whole -  transporting you to another place, another time.

A total pleasure.

please remember that we support Terre and Comatonse Recordings' efforts to keep projects offline, minor, and acting queerly. When purchasing this item, we ask you to refrain from uploading and indiscriminate sharing in any form. <3
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以深度浩室为根基，融入环境氛围元素与酷儿文化语境，试图将浩室音乐拉回其俱乐部文化根源。制作人Terre Thaemlitz早期在曼哈顿中城与新泽西的同性恋俱乐部担任DJ，亲历了深度浩室兴起的年代，专辑以十首作品重现彼时的场景，序曲即对Strictly Rhythm厂牌的商业转向及欧洲听众将深度浩室等同于低质人声浩室的现象进行了直接批判。音乐呈现沉静忧郁的气质，丰富的次低音音色与缓慢交织的钢琴音型构成核心声响层次，部分曲目以变装皇后的独白叠加在最深层环境节奏之上，另一些曲目则展现温暖的和弦与细腻的打击乐触感。整体制作精良，带有明确的个人视角与文化立场，但作为浩室舞曲的变体，其与纯粹实验或前卫电子的边界仍有距离。

items.body:
Following 2024's avant-prog-Americana song cycle 'Viewfinder', guitar deity Wendy Eisenberg goes chamber pop on their self-titled latest, tipping their hat to Judee Sill, Gillian Welch, Van Dyke Parks and Joanna Newsom.

When they relocated from rural Western Mass to Brooklyn in 2020, Eisenberg was hit with a wave of longing for the open landscape they'd left behind. They were drawn to classic country and folk records, perfectly poised offerings from Willie Nelson and John Hartford and lavish pop-folk records from Jimmy Webb and Van Dyke Parks as well as the weirdo fare of Richard Dawson et al. So when 'Viewfinder', a way of deconstructing the experience following eye surgery in 2011, was finished, Eisenberg started writing "genuinely folk songs" and swapping out their usually showy, complex performance for a form of relative simplicity that they explain is inherently strange all the same. Prog becomes folk, basically. And they're not on their own; more eaze handles the lush string arrangements, playing pedal steel and synthesizer, and a loose band forms around that axis, with drummer Ryan Sawyer and bassist Trevor Dunn.

But despite the personnel, it's resolutely Eisenberg's album. Their voice sounds unrestrained, capturing the era they're referencing and their own emotional (and physical upheaval). It's fragile but strangely warm on the country-tinged Jim O'Rourke-like 'Will You Dare' and hypnotic on the baroque 'Meaning Business', a track they wrote in the wake of David Lynch's death as the antithesis of the "Lynchian" aesthetic. And they should really get their flowers for this one; Americana, especially now, is teetering on a precipice, almost knocked off the edge by half-assed, churned attempts and underwritten pastiches. Eisenberg's an attentive listener and someone who's surrounded themself with similarly sensitive ears, people who are able to fill their heart and their sound so what we hear is as byzantine as a Gastr del Sol record but sounds as effortless as John Prine's 'Angel From Montgomery'. If you loved Joanna Newsom's 'Ys' and have never found anything quite as satisfying, this is the one.
items._cn_summary: 吉他手Wendy Eisenberg在2024年完成前卫乡土作品《Viewfinder》后，转向室内流行风格，推出同名专辑。2020年从马萨诸塞乡村搬到布鲁克林后，对开阔地貌的思念促使他们回归经典乡村与民谣素材，融合Willie Nelson的简约与Van Dyke Parks的精致弦乐编排。Eisenberg主动放弃以往华丽复杂的演奏方式，转而追求一种本质上仍然陌生的简洁性。more eaze负责弦乐编配与钢 pedal和合成器，Ryan Sawyer与Trevor Dunn组成松散节奏组。人声呈现出不设防的状态，在乡村色彩的曲目中脆弱而温暖，在巴洛克风格的曲目中则带有催眠感。评论指出，这张专辑是对当下美式音乐领域粗制滥造模仿风潮的有力回应，以细致入微的聆听态度与精致编曲为基础，将前卫思维注入民谣传统。

items.body:
The unstoppable LIV.e finds her groove alongside Stones Throw mainstay Karriem Riggins on 'The Pleasure is Yours', breathing life into a set of big hearted contemporary avant-soul/hip-hop experiments that'll hit anyone into Erykah Badu's 'New Amerykah' tomes.

Riggins is an old hand at this stage. The bandleader for Common's old band, he's produced alongside Dilla, worked with The Roots and Ye, collaborated with Madlib and kept it fresh by breaking bread with Kaytranada, Denzel Curry and Earl Sweatshirt. And if you're used to poring through the liners, you'll realize it was his mind behind Badu's 'Soldier', one of the highlights from her second-wind classic 'New Amerykah Part One'. It's this hiccuping sound - a rougher, more defiantly hip-hop inspired take on what became sold as "neo soul" - that roots 'The Pleasure is Yours', the first record from Riggins' self-styled supergroup alongside young prodigy Hailee Olivia Williams, aka LIV.e. 

Working with his trusty LinnDrum and playing bass and piano, Riggins orchestrates a backdrop that's knowing (he was there, after all) but oddly relevant - and twice as wonked as anything from his younger rivals. For her part, LIV.e adds the charm and the warmth. We already know she's good - it's not just hype - and her songs crackle, purr and flicker alongside Riggins' skittering beats. On one level, it's pure psych - tune into the rattly, swirling 'TGD' and tell us it ain't - but what makes this one stand out is that it never takes itself too seriously. So we're treated to brash Prince-style belters like 'This is so Crazy', the waved Motown-like 'DoobieDooWew' and the levitational 'You've Outdone Yourself Today, Huh?' all on one record.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是制作人Karriem Riggins与年轻歌手LIV.e的合作产物。Riggins以LinnDrum为核心，亲自演奏贝斯与钢琴，搭建出带有粗粝质感的节律骨架，延续了他在Erykah Badu《New Amerykah》中的那种打破常规、放克味与嘻哈骨架交织的手法。LIV.e的声线在碎裂的节拍中时而低沉、时而高昂，与跳脱的制作形成有趣对话。曲目跨度大，既有神经质的迷幻段落，也有Prince式的放克宣泄，更有Motown式的旋律与轻盈律动，整体不拘泥于单一氛围，强调即兴与不可预测感。作为Stones Throw厂牌出品，定位偏向独立地下场景，对喜爱打破类型边界的听众有一定吸引力，但在实验维度上并未完全脱离neo-soul框架。

items.body:
Their third album, ‘Treasure’ also debuts Simon Raymonde on bass and finds the band scaling new heights in the most emotionally raw way imaginable. Impossible to overstate just how influential and well loved this album is - from the quietly anthemic Pandora (For Cindy) - probably played in every bedroom by every teenager in 1984, to the sublime 'Beatrix' and 'Otterley' - tracks that were played on Autechre’s Disengage Kiss FM show in the early 90’s and which gave us our first introduction to one of the most magical and timeless albums ever made.

"The band returned to being a trio in 1984 with guitarist Simon Raymonde joining their ranks in time for third album, Treasure. Produced by Robin Guthrie and featuring tracks ‘Lorelei’, ‘Ivo’ and ‘Persephone’, Treasure is often celebrated as one of the band’s finest works. As Pitchfork put it when including the album in their Top 100 Albums of the 1980s, “Treasure was titled simply enough. An adjective for the endlessly inventive melodic lines you'd find buried in these songs, and a verb for what you'd do with them for years to come.”

items._cn_summary: Cocteau Twins 1984年发行的第三张专辑《Treasure》是乐队以三人阵容完成的标志性作品，吉他手Simon Raymonde的加入强化了低音线条与和弦织体的层次。制作人Robin Guthrie延续了乐队标志性的回授吉他处理与人声混响美学，将Elizabeth Fraser近乎无词义的人声漂浮在密集的音墙之上，创造出情感浓度极高的氛围空间。专辑收录了《Lorelei》《Persephone》《Ivo》等曲目，旋律线被嵌入层层延迟与混响之中，形成既亲密又疏离的听觉体验。该作被Pitchfork列入1980年代百佳专辑榜，其影响延续至九十年代的电子音乐场景，曾被Autechre等艺术家选播，证明了其在声音美学上的持续启发性。

items.body:
This National Day, StarHub and Bandwagon are inviting Singaporeans to experience home through a different lens — or rather, through a different listen.

Launched on 30 July, the two homegrown brands have unveiled Sounds of Home, an original music project that transforms the familiar sounds of everyday Singapore into a heartfelt soundtrack celebrating the people, places and moments that connect us.

Created as part of StarHub's ongoing The Power of Pause initiative, the collaboration encourages people to take a break from constant scrolling and reconnect with the sounds that often fade into the background of daily life. Rather than focusing on grand National Day spectacles, Sounds of Home shines a spotlight on the small moments that quietly define what it means to call Singapore home.

Produced by acclaimed Singaporean producer, artist and composer Fauxe, the track is built entirely from authentic field recordings captured across the island. The sonic palette draws from bustling hawker centres, neighbourhood playgrounds, MRT stations and everyday conversations, weaving these familiar sounds into an original composition that reflects the rhythm of life in Singapore. Joining the project are homegrown artists RENE, Krysta Joy, YAØ and Akeem Jahat, who bring the soundtrack to life with an accompanying visual film inspired by everyday moments shared across the country.

The collaboration also marks an intersection between technology, music and wellbeing. While StarHub connects millions of people every day through digital services, The Power of Pause serves as a reminder that meaningful human connection often begins when people put their devices down and become fully present.

"National Day is a time to reflect on what brings us together as Singaporeans. While we often celebrate the big moments, it's the everyday sounds around us, from familiar voices and neighbourhoods to shared experiences, that remind us what home feels like," said Lin Liangmin, Head of Brand and Communications at StarHub.

"Through Sounds of Home, we hope to encourage Singaporeans to pause, listen a little more closely, and reconnect with the moments that matter most."

For Bandwagon, the project also represents an opportunity to explore music in one of its purest forms: storytelling through sound.

"At Bandwagon, we've spent years championing Singapore's music scene, so we're always thinking about how sound can tell stories and create meaningful connections," said Clarence Chan, Founder & CEO of Bandwagon.

"Working closely with StarHub, we saw the potential in the everyday sounds we often take for granted, yet instinctively associate with home, and set out to reimagine them as an original piece of music. Every rhythm, bassline and melody is crafted from the sounds of Singapore. We hope people have fun spotting the familiar sounds woven into the song, while being reminded that, much like music, it's the many small moments of connection that come together to make Singapore feel like home."

As Singapore celebrates its 61st National Day, Sounds of Home offers a fresh way of reflecting on identity and belonging. Instead of commemorating the occasion through spectacle alone, the project celebrates the ordinary sounds that accompany everyday life — reminding listeners that home is found not only in familiar places, but also in shared experiences and fleeting moments that often go unnoticed.

The project premieres today via StarHub's LinkedIn page and Bandwagon's social media channels. The full soundtrack will also be available on Spotify, Apple Music and other major streaming platforms.

items._genre: field recording / ambient / electronic / experimental / world
items._cn_summary: 这是StarHub与Bandwagon合作推出的国庆主题声音项目《Sounds of Home》。制作人Fauxe以新加坡日常生活中的实地录音——小贩中心、邻里游乐场、地铁站、街头对话——为素材，将其编织成原创音乐作品。RENE、Krysta Joy、YAØ与Akeem Jahat等本土歌手参与伴唱，并配以视觉短片。项目属于StarHub"暂停的力量"倡议的一部分，呼吁人们放下手机、从熟悉的环境声中重新感受"家"的含义。文章整体偏向品牌新闻稿而非深度乐评，对声音设计、制作技法及音乐结构的讨论极为有限，但田野录音作为创作基础的思路本身就带有实验性与世界音乐色彩，与传统商业流行路线形成差异。

items._cn_summary: Abul Mogard 与 Rafael Anton Irisarri 的合作作品游走于静默与重力之间，音色缓慢浮现而非刻意编排。整体以循环、扭曲、空间感和记忆为线索塑造声响，呈现出近乎建筑般厚重的质感，却仍保留着脆弱的呼吸感。两人均长期活跃于氛围与无人机领域，此番合作延续了各自的美学脉络，将模块合成器的绵延音层与磁带质感融为一体。专辑《Where Light Pauses in the Silence of the...》指向一种对安静环境与时间延展的探索，作品不急于抵达任何终点，而是邀请听众进入声音自身的物理空间。适合深度聆听与沉浸式播放，其氛围构造手法展现了当代实验电子对空间与质感的持续关注。

items.body: This Daily Discovery isn’t the usual kind… These features normally just point you towards something worth hearing and watching; this one also asks you to help. Alice in WonderBand are Ana Vrbaški and Marko Dinjaški, a Serbian duo who have been together on stage and off it for 28 years. They live out near the Fruška Gora National Park in the north of the country and make all their music from the body: hands clapping and snapping, feet stamping the floor, chests and thighs slapped for the low end, tongues and mouth clicks filling the gaps, Ana at the piano, Marko on didgeridoo and darbuka, and the tunes carried in their voices. Most of what they sing began as Balkan folk song, which they take apart and rebuild in the odd, uneven rhythms of the region. On 11 July, Ana was seriously injured as a passenger in a car accident, and she now faces a long period of treatment and rehabilitation. The couple had a full summer of concerts ahead of them, and all of it has fallen through, their income with it. Friends have set up a fundraiser to help meet the cost of her care and steady the months to come. You can donate HERE, or give directly through PayPal at THIS LINK. If a donation isn’t possible, sharing it helps just as much. The song in the video is one of theirs. “Dokonanje”, which roughly means being idle, is a track from their new album, The Courage to be Afraid. They recorded it in May with their daughter, Alisa Dinjaški, alongside “Vrbice, Vrbo Zeljena”, a Gorani song from Kosovo. It is an old piece, written almost twenty years ago, and the words still read like a motto. “Dokonanje” means being idle, but the song argues the opposite: the refrain insists “We’re not being idle”, then lists the digging, mowing and carrying of water that fills the day. The video was filmed at Slovenia’s Kavč festival, a travelling event that for ten years has staged concerts in living rooms, bookshops and town squares under Matija Solce. Alice in WonderBand played the Fragmenti bookshop in Kranj. This year Ana and Marko, together with Julia Lewandowska and Łukasz Malok from CISI, also brought Slavyk to life, a quartet that sets Silesian and Serbian folk traditions to English lyrics. Their debut, 11 Songs of Love and Suffering, was released this June on CPL Music. If you can, stand with Ana and Marko by giving or sharing THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Alice in Wonderband – Dokonanje (Live @ Kavč Festival, Fragmenti Bookstore) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: folk / world music / experimental vocal / body percussion
items._cn_summary: 塞尔维亚二人组Alice in WonderBand以身体作为核心乐器，通过拍手、跺脚、拍击胸膛与大腿发出节奏声响，辅以钢琴、迪吉里杜管、手鼓和人声，构建出融合巴尔干民谣的独特声响。他们的创作取材于地区民间歌谣，将其拆解并以不规则、错综的当地节奏重新编织。文中重点介绍的现场录音《Dokonanje》来自新专辑《The Courage to be Afraid》，歌词以反讽手法描绘日常劳作，蕴含朴素而坚韧的生活哲学。文章同时介绍了他们在斯洛文尼亚Kavč音乐节的演出，以及与波兰音乐家合作将西里西亚与塞尔维亚民歌传统融入英语歌词的新项目Slavyk。由于歌手遭遇车祸，文章呼吁读者通过捐款或分享链接支持这对合作二十八年的音乐伙伴。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — Listen up! If the stars are lit, it means? they burn too brightly for this world. Unfortunately, the genius "psychedelic" wrote a little, but his works are immortal. Good works, which include a unique transparent sound, which is typical, however, for many English performers and bands. Transparent, like the air of their homeland, inhaled by the instrument and blown into our ears. Some of the compositions are English fantasy fairy tales (Matilda Mother, The Gnome, Scarecrow), and the main action is a great cosmic journey through which this "star gentleman" travels. He gives the light of these stars to us and his group, who set off on a more distant earthly journey. And he stayed on the other side of the moon. My assessment is not accidental. I'd like to thank you for the innovation of transparent sound and cosmically ethereal vocals, born (not in pain). The only band, in my opinion, where there is such a combination is Yes. But that's another story.
items._cn_summary: 这张1967年的专辑以透明清澈的音色著称，吉他与键盘编织出英式幻想般的音景。曲目取材于英式童话与宇宙意象，从小妖精、稻草人到星际漫游，叙事跨越尘世与天际。评论者特别提到其音色具有独特的透明感，并将其与Yes乐队在声乐与宇宙氛围上的相似性相比较。整体上，专辑通过新颖的音色运用和空灵的人声处理，开创了迷幻摇滚与太空摇滚融合的早期范式，对后世前卫摇滚的声景美学产生了影响。
