items.body: Review by Naida Regent — The album "Narrow is the Road" is more coherent than the previous two. It feels the spirit of the present time, the ongoing difficult events that have affected Ukraine and Russia in 2022. In every note, one can feel personal involvement of the performers and the transfer of this to the listeners. "He who has ears to hear, let him hear." This gospel saying best fits the theme of the album. There are fewer things that are heavy in perception and in mood than on previous albums; rather there is a certain mood that awakens all the best inside the human mind, inside our understanding on the path of searching for the truth. The titles of the compositions are also united by one goal - the awakening of reason and mercy. Here is a musical example that shows that it is possible to speak about difficult things in a very simple language. It is not difficult to be a humanist and it is not too late to become; while you're still alive, do it faster so the world doesn't fall apart. The composer Jenkins has an oratorio titled "A Mass for Peace". The album "Narrow is the Road" can safely be called its continuation.
items._cn_summary: COMPASSIONIZER 的第三张专辑《Narrow Is the Road》展现出比前两张更高的内聚性，乐评人 Naida Regent 认为其精神内核呼应了 2022 年俄乌冲突背景下的时代情绪。专辑以简朴的音乐语言探讨沉重命题，传递人道主义关怀与对真理的追寻。作曲家 Jenkins 此前曾创作清唱剧《A Mass for Peace》，本专辑被视作该作品的精神延续。曲目标题统一指向理性与慈悲的觉醒，整体氛围不再沉重压抑，而是唤起人性中向善的力量。音乐在表达严肃议题的同时保持平易近人，呈现出以简单方式承载深意的特点。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — After listening to "Daybreaking Live" album I had discovered for myself new Roz Vitalis, although previously I listened to this band time and time again. At the present moment compositions are perceived as more mature and "grow" with musicians both physically and mentally. The sound became more heavy and dense. Due to more heavy guitar and more heavy rhythm-section "approach" of the band comes closer to progressive metal. But, at the same time, Roz Vitalis's style remains true to oneself and recognizable. Evidently, the group wants to take from prog a little bit of everything and, at the same time, to be distinctive and original. As before, there are baroque-and-medieval motives. In "Nepsis" and "Psalm 6" motives of dancing heaviness transform into tranquil transcendence. In each composition there are memorable and hit melodies. "Mother of All Rain" remains the most melodic one. The flute sounds remarkably, but I would like to hear more winds like in "The Hidden Man of the Heart" album. In general, in the future it would be better to increase quantity of wind instruments (clarinet, saxophone, trumpet, French Horn). The same wishes concern use of string instruments (violin, cello, double bass, viola). The main recommendation is to move to symphonic style of music.
items._genre: avant-prog / progressive rock / progressive metal / neoclassical
items._cn_summary: 这是Roz Vitalis乐队现场专辑《Daybreaking Live》的乐评。评论者认为相比此前作品，乐队在创作上更加成熟，音色更厚重密集，吉他与节奏组的力量感将风格推向前卫金属边缘，但乐队标志性的个人风格依然可辨。评论指出乐队试图从前卫摇滚中广泛汲取元素，同时保持独特性与原创性，其中巴洛克与中世纪动机贯穿始终。在《Nepsis》和《Psalm 6》中，舞蹈性的沉重动机逐渐转化为宁静的超脱氛围，每首作品都包含记忆点旋律，《Mother of All Rain》被认为最具旋律性。长笛表现突出，评论者建议未来增加单簧管、萨克斯、小号、法国号等管乐器以及小提琴、大提琴、低音提琴、中提琴等弦乐器的运用，整体向交响化风格发展。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — This album is the first release in the history of the project dedicated to a specific person, alas, who left us, the talented producer Nikolai Bogaichuk. I heard in this album a reverent appeal to the addressee, echoes of the past, good, bright communication. The musicians seem to be continuing a dialogue with a person who already exists in another reality, and he responds to them. It's as if they can hear each other in the musical canvas of the works. A roll call of instruments is created - keyboards, wind instruments, etc. The first tracks are like the intro to a peculiar symphony of mystical roll call. The middle is active, vital, because a person lives in us as long as the memory of him is alive. And the ending is an epilogue, completing the journey on earth and looking into another future, an unknown world. Everyone "applies" the ease of perception to herself/himself. Everyone carries the weight of loss within herself/himself. When listening to this album, the effect is "opposite", where grief should not be boundless, and happiness should not be fleeting. It is not the first time that we have heard Ivan Rozmainsky's symphonic "approach", which is always inherent in him, and we hope that he will develop this to the level of the immortal classics.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是俄罗斯前卫摇滚乐团首次以纪念特定人物为主题的作品，献给已故制作人尼古拉·博加伊丘克。乐评将其结构比作一部交响曲：开头如同神秘召唤序曲，中段充满活力与生命力，结尾则作为尾声收束整段旅程。乐队延续了伊万·罗兹曼斯基一贯的交响化编曲手法，键盘与管乐器在音画中交织，营造出与逝者持续对话的意象。评论者期望乐团在此方向上继续深化，最终达到不朽经典的境界。

items.body: Review by Naida Regent — In the cold Spring time I was very sad. I felt blue due to the dominance of musical culture promoted by mass media. I had made decision to listen to new album of the band which is known and loved by me for a long time because of the originality. The album "The Hidden Man of the Heart" is much darker than previous, "Lavoro d'Amore", but in the process of listening to the feeling of depression does not appear. If to take technical sides that this album sounds more professionally than previous ones. If to make comparisons with other artists then it the band "combines in one flacon" early Pink Floyd, King Crimson, and ELP. It also reminds exercises of Robert Fripp and Brian Eno. If to give characteristics of the style then it is progressive-psychedelic-electronic format with elements of German classical music, for example, Wagner. Recommended to listen to for those who want quickly to move from the state of sadness to the state of joy.
items._cn_summary: 这是俄罗斯前卫乐队ROZ VITALIS 2018年发行的专辑《The Hidden Man of the Heart》。乐评人将其风格描述为将早期Pink Floyd、King Crimson、ELP的特质融合于一处，并带有Robert Fripp与Brian Eno实验性练习的气质，定位为"progressive-psychedelic-electronic"格式，同时融入德国古典音乐（如瓦格纳）的元素。相比前作《Lavoro d'Amore》，这张专辑整体色调更暗，但聆听过程并不产生压抑感，制作上更为专业成熟。整张专辑在结构编排和氛围营造上展现出乐队一贯的原创性，融合古典、电子与迷幻元素，适合希望从前卫实验中寻找情感转换体验的听众。

items.body: Review by OlyaBeginner — I have just listened to An Ambassador in Bonds. This work has raised a bunch of emotions. There were positive feelings like magic and wonderfulness and uncertain ones like humility, fearness, searching and curiosity. A work like this can create any kind of atmosphere and change the mood of listeners. It can be both calm and pacifying or stress and tension. All instruments play their own role and they are laconic together. A listener can find episodes in their life which can be accompanied by the compositions from the album. It is a big and worth-listening work that can make your passion for progressive rock stronger.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张题为《An Ambassador in Bonds》的前卫摇滚专辑，乐评者描述其能唤起多层次情绪——既有魔法般的惊奇感，也有谦卑、恐惧、探索与好奇等不确定感受。作品在氛围营造上极具弹性，可安静安抚，也可制造紧张张力。各乐器分工明确，相互克制而不抢戏，整体呈现出内敛而统一的声响质地。乐评强调这是一种可伴随听众个人经历的作品，适合在特定生活片段中聆听，并有助于加深对前卫摇滚这一领域的热情。专辑归属Avant-Prog与RIO谱系，体现出小众前卫圈子对结构与情绪实验的持续探索。

items.body: Review by OlyaBeginner — I won't describe the quality of musical instruments, I will just tell you, what feelings this work has evoked. Day breaking makes you feel despair, acceptance, peace. Your thoughts are being stopped and focus on the fact where and when you are. This composition makes you accept life as it is, the rules it has.Fountain makes you remember about hurt, tears you have in your life but it reminds that there is always hope that everything is gonna be ok.Se camminiamo Nella Luce evokes anxiety, fear and again hope. It tells you we can overcome difficult period, but we should try and work in order to contribute to making things better.Premonition - starting gradually, like growing. Brutal, strong and determined, with pauses to respite and rethink. Maybe you were doing something wrong. Maybe there are important things you weren't paying attention.Walking - is brutal too, changing to cute. Sometimes people need to stop being strong and show their weaknesses, have some rest and after that again get into a diligent rhythm of life in order to get what you want.Wides - the idea of taking an oath of fighting unfairness and cruelty runs through the entire album. Here in particular. In the beginning you don't know what to do, maybe feel confused. But then you realise that the only right thing is you never gonna give up. Bustle of hard work will fix troubles. But of course you have to take breaks when you feel tiredness, which is pleasant. You keep doing your thing following your oath.The man whose wings were cut off - hurt and shock, confused and uncertain, sadness and brutal.Beautifulness - admiration with beautifulness, but this beautifulness consists of kindness and love for other people.Nocturne - makes you remember people you stop being close with and feel thankful for all time you spent together and unforgettable experience they gave you. You are just thankful that they were in your life. Light sadness and love fill the soul, even it's not mutual.So this album has the great power to make a listener feel a bunch of emotions and immerses him/her in a different sorts of atmosphere. Sometimes it comforts, sometimes it inspires to go forward.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以器乐为主，每首曲目围绕特定情绪主题展开：从黎明破晓的绝望与接纳，到面对伤害时的希望与疗愈，再到宣誓对抗不公的坚定。评论者没有分析乐器或演奏技术，而是从感受出发，记录每段音乐所唤起的情感氛围与人生感悟。曲式上呈现由渐进展开到强烈爆发、再回归平静的弧线，体现出叙事性的器乐编排逻辑。整体制作注重情绪层次与沉浸感，试图让听众在音乐中经历从困惑到释然的完整旅程。这种以情感为线索的写法本身就是一次有意识的实验，用音乐作为情绪载体，而非传统结构化作品。

items.body: Nolwenn Boyet and Ronni Gauderat make up the French duo Buzzkill. Active since 2024, Buzzkill previously released an EP on Ganache Records. For their debut album, “Wasteland”, they joined forces with Manic Depression Records, a move that will help expand their audience. “Wasteland” blends Cold-Wave and Minimal-Electro influences, with a raw, uncompromising sound driven by icy synth textures and deep, brooding basslines. Nolwenn Boyet’s cold, detached vocal delivery complements the music throughout. I spoke with both Buzzkill musicians about the making of “Wasteland”. (Courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) Buzzkill interview Q: Let’s start with the origins of Buzzkill. When and how did the band come together, and what are your individual musical backgrounds? How did those experiences inspire you to form Buzzkill? Nolwenn: We created a band shortly after meeting Ronni. At first, the project was very different from what it is today. We didn’t have the ambition to make something professional out of it, we just wanted to make music and spend time together. At the time we were a trio, with Ronni on bass and vocals, Axelle on synths and me on drums. When Axelle left the band, we wanted to try something else. We started experimenting with a duo setup where I took over the vocals and synths, and the drums became electronic. We quickly felt that something was working. We compose together quite naturally and found a good balance as a duo. At the end of 2024, we wrote our first EP, which was a starting point for us. It really captured the beginning of Buzzkill and helped define our identity. Ronni: I started playing music at 15, as a drummer in a Grunge band, which later became a Rock’n’roll band that I still play in today. At the same time, I taught myself guitar and started several other projects, including a Shoegaze band and a swamp Garage band with which I toured for eight years and released two albums. Today, I’m also working on a Synth-Punk duo alongside my other projects. My musical background is quite eclectic, maybe even a bit chaotic, but I’ve always liked moving from one style to another. The creative process is what motivates me the most. I just like writing music and exploring different directions. Nolwenn: My journey as a musician actually started with Buzzkill. I had never sung, played synths or composed music before. I had only played a bit of drums when I was a teenager. Meeting Ronni is what pushed me to get into music. I like this kind of unexpected path and I’m still learning as I go. Ronni and I come from very different musical backgrounds, but we share the same approach. Keeping things simple and raw. Q: Earlier this year, you released the debut album of Buzzkill, “Wasteland”. Looking back on the entire creative process, what stands out to you most? What was your vision for the album in terms of its sound and production? Ronni: What probably stood out the most to us were the conditions in which we recorded the album. We did it in a garden shed, during a heatwave. It was a strange feeling to create such cold music while being in 40 degree heat. Maybe that’s what naturally led us towards the atmosphere of “Wasteland”. Nolwenn: Like for our EP, we recorded everything ourselves. We used pretty much the same equipment, but we had improved a lot in the way we used it and knew more clearly where we wanted to go. With “Wasteland”, we wanted to create something that felt more like a complete album, with a stronger overall atmosphere. We also wanted to lean further into the Electronic side of the project. We spent more time working on synth textures, drum sounds and the atmosphere of each track. I also discovered my voice more and found the way I wanted to use it. For the bass, we wanted to keep that raw and upfront feeling, with a sound that doesn’t feel overproduced. It was already part of the EP’s identity, and I think it defines a big part of what Buzzkill sounds like. We were also careful about which songs we wanted to include. That’s why the album only has seven tracks. It felt complete that way, and we liked the idea of keeping it short and intense. For the mastering, we worked again with Mathis Kolkoz (Blind Delon), who also mastered the EP. We really like his work and trusted him for this. Q: “Wasteland” is a bleak and evocative title. What does it represent to you, and which emotions shaped the music and inspired the lyrics? Nolwenn: “Wasteland” represents our vision of an apocalyptic future. It’s a deliberately exaggerated and pessimistic vision, but deep down it doesn’t feel that unrealistic today. We wanted a strong title that would immediately evoke an empty and hopeless landscape. We were quite inspired by the post-apocalyptic and desert aesthetics of movies like “Dune” and “Mad Max”, as well as games like “Fallout” and “Borderland”. The lyrics came from our anger and anxiety about the current ecological and social crises, but also from the feeling of injustice around the fact that the most vulnerable people are always the first to suffer the consequences. Through “Wasteland”, we imagine a future where no one can escape the collapse, not even the most privileged. It’s a sad thought that maybe the only moment when these inequalities could disappear is when we’re all facing the end of the world. Q: In a way, “Wasteland” feels like the soundtrack to a world in decline – a place where people are struggling with both themselves and the reality surrounding them. How personal is this album, and what is your perspective, both as artists and as individuals, on the state of the world today? Nolwenn: This album is very personal because it comes from the way we experience the world today and the anxiety it creates in us. But I think it speaks to a lot of people, especially younger generations who know they’ll grow old in this world, or at least in what will be left of it. As I’m answering this interview we’ve reached 42°C in our city. There are major forest fires happening in our country and people are dying because of the heat, while political responses still seem completely disconnected from the reality we’re facing. It’s become impossible not to think every day about what the world will be like in 10, 20 or 30 years, and under what conditions we’ll be living. “Wasteland” is our cathartic way of putting words and sounds to the distress we’re feeling lately. Q: I’ve always found it fascinating that some of the darkest, most nihilistic themes can inspire such compelling and even danceable music. There seems to be an intriguing contradiction between despair and movement. How important is that contrast to Buzzkill, and what role does music play for you as a means of expression? Ronni: This contradiction is very much part of the DNA of Post-Punk. We’ve always liked that contrast in bands like Joy Division. We like the idea that music can make you want to dance while talking about very dark subjects. We also felt that fast tempos and repetitive rhythms were the best way to express tension and urgency. If we have to live in a world that’s falling apart, we might as well dance through it. Q: Let’s talk about the live Buzzkill experience. What can audiences expect from a Buzzkill performance, and what atmosphere or emotions do you hope to create on stage? How do your songs evolve in a live setting compared to their studio versions? Ronni: Live we try to keep things intense and direct. We don’t talk much, sometimes not at all. We like to step back and let the music take the lead. We try to build a set where the atmosphere can evolve naturally. We like playing almost without breaks because we enjoy the feeling of a 45 min set that keeps moving, with very little time to come back down. It’s a way to convey that overwhelming feeling we have. The bass also brings something very organic and physical to the live experience. I play it through both a bass amp and a guitar amp. Q: Finally, what are your expectations and ambitions for Buzzkill following the release of “Wasteland”? What can listeners look forward to in the near future? Nolwenn: We didn’t really expect “Wasteland” to get much attention at the beginning. We just told ourselves: let’s do our thing and see what happens. We were lucky to meet our friend and manager Stephy just before its release, and she really helped us give the album more visibility. Our main goal now is to keep defending the album on stage, in France of course, but also to start playing in other European countries. We’d like to keep developing the project, see where this album can take us, and keep writing because it’s what drives us in life. We also want to keep surrounding ourselves with people we appreciate, discover new projects from the underground scene, and share the stage with artists we love. We’re already thinking about the next album and we’ve started writing again. We want to explore new directions, maybe something a bit more Electro-Punk, with more repetitive and hypnotic structures, while still keeping what defines Buzzkill. To finish, we just want to say to everyone reading this: keep supporting the underground scene and independent artists. Keep going to concerts in dark and humid caves, discovering local bands and getting lost on Bandcamp. This counterculture only survives because people choose to support it. Thanks for that. And thank you, Stéphane and Side-line for the interview 🙂 Nolwenn and Ronni – Buzzkill
items._cn_summary: Buzzkill 是法国二人组合，成立于2024年，首张专辑《Wasteland》由 Manic Depression Records 发行。乐队将 Cold-Wave 与 Minimal-Electro 元素融合，冰冷合成器纹理与低沉贝斯线条构成核心声音骨架，主唱 Nolwenn Boyet 以冷峻疏离的人声演唱贯穿全作。创作过程以自发性为特点，从最初的三人配置转变为二人电子编制，通过简化与粗砺化确立乐队身份。专辑被视为二人对当下情绪压抑的宣泄出口，在制作上保持了原始且不妥协的态度。作为 Manic Depression Records 发行的作品，厂牌背景为其扩展受众提供了支持。整体风格契合暗潮与电子暗色音乐的脉络，但在创新性与跨类型融合层面并未展现出显著的突破，仍属于该流派框架内的稳健制作。

items.body: UK trio Holy Tongue will release their second album, Basilikum, on LP and digital through AD 93 on October 9, 2026, catalog number WHYT106. The record moves between dub, ritual percussion and cinematic psychedelia, and features vocalist Dali De Saint Paul on two tracks. Holy Tongue recorded “Basilikum” as a series of improvisations in the Swiss Alps and London, built on vintage drum machines and what the label describes as “instinctive interplay.” AD 93 describes the album as combining dub techniques with ritual percussion, hypnotic pulse and Popol Vuh-style landscapes, with the trio treating playing, recording, editing and transformation as part of the same creative act. ‘Basilikum’ tracklist and featured vocals “Basilikum” runs eight tracks: “I’ve Stood in This Room for a Long Time Before,” “Coca” (feat. Dali De Saint Paul), “Orange 28,” “Bloom in D Minor” (feat. Dali De Saint Paul), “Vuoto 25,” “ROSEROOT,” “Single~Eyed” and “Nature.” The lead track “Coca” carries De Saint Paul’s vocal alongside the band’s dub-rooted rhythm section. About Holy Tongue Holy Tongue formed in London in 2018 as a studio project between producer Al Wootton and percussionist Valentina Magaletti, also a member of Moin, before expanding into a full trio with the addition of Susumu Mukai of Vanishing Twin. The group’s music draws on dub reggae, free improvisation and post-punk, referencing labels and artists such as On-U-Sound and Muslimgauze alongside post-punk bands like Liquid Liquid and 23 Skidoo. Following a trilogy of EPs, Holy Tongue released their debut album, “Deliverance and Spiritual Warfare,” in 2023, and followed it in 2024 with a collaborative album, “The Tumbling Psychic Joy of Now,” made with dub producer Shackleton. “Basilikum” is the trio’s second album, due October 9, 2026, on AD 93, the London label formerly known as Whities.
items._cn_summary: 英国三人组Holy Tongue即将在AD 93厂牌发行第二张专辑《Basilikum》。整张专辑在瑞士阿尔卑斯山和伦敦两地以即兴方式录制，使用复古鼓机作为节奏基础，融合dub技巧、仪式感打击乐、催眠式脉冲以及带有Popol Vuh气质的电影化迷幻音景。人声仅出现在两首曲目中，由Dali De Saint Paul担纲，整体偏向器乐氛围的沉浸式建构。乐队将演奏、录音、编辑与变形视为同一创作行为的不同阶段，强调直觉式互动而非预设编排。成员包括制作人Al Wootton、打击乐手Valentina Magaletti（同时活跃于Moin）和Susumu Mukai（Vanishing Twin），此前已与dub制作人Shackleton合作完成一张专辑。

items.body: London post-punk trio Black Doldrums will release a new album, “Repetition Compulsion,” on November 13, 2026, through Fuzz Club Records. The band shares the first single from the record, “Repetition,” alongside a video, out now. “Repetition Compulsion” completes Black Doldrums’ “State of Mind Trilogy,” a three-album exploration of the psychological forces that shape identity, memory and human connection that began with the band’s 2022 debut, “Dead Awake,” and continued on 2024’s “In Limerence.” The title refers to the psychological concept first explored by Sigmund Freud, and the album, according to Fuzz Club, “examines the unconscious tendency to recreate familiar emotional patterns, destructive behaviours and inherited cycles from the past” across its eleven tracks. ‘Repetition’ explores an unconscious cycle At the core of “Repetition Compulsion” is the creative and personal partnership between founding members Kevin Gibbard and Sophie Landers. “The songs are either about Sophie, for Sophie, or inspired by her,” Gibbard says. On the new single, he explains: “The song came from an idea to challenge ourselves to write something around one riff and something dirge-like. It also fit the theme of the album and the topic of repetition by literally experimenting with repetition in the musical sense. The opening line – ‘is your mind split in two’ – is something taken from our conversations on our many long walks around London where Sophie was talking about the psychological term splitting. It seemed to fit the feel of the song and theme of the album so much so it now opens up both the album and our live shows. I consider it very much Sophie’s song because she was the source of inspiration and that’s why we have her backing vocals fairly prominent to create a dual vocal effect. I also had the after-thought to have Sophie mime the first line in the video which is actually her line anyway.” On the album as a whole, Gibbard adds that “the album invites listeners to confront the echoes of the past while questioning whether those patterns can ever truly be broken.” Black Doldrums draw on 80s gothic post-punk, synth-pop and darkwave, alongside the film scores of John Carpenter and Vangelis, building songs from layered analogue synths, chorus-soaked guitars and driving rhythms. Repetition Compulsion by Black Doldrums The eleven-track “Repetition Compulsion” runs “Repetition,” “The Uncanny,” “Waiting,” “Beat The Rain,” “Echoes,” “Compulsion,” “No One’s Talking To Me,” “Bat Bomb,” “No Words Can’t Lie,” “Die With Me” and “Eulogy.” About Black Doldrums Black Doldrums is a post-punk trio from London, UK, built around the creative and personal partnership of Kevin Gibbard and Sophie Landers. The band released its debut album, “Dead Awake,” in 2022, followed by “In Limerence” in 2024, both through Fuzz Club Records. “Repetition Compulsion,” out November 13, 2026, closes the “State of Mind Trilogy” that runs across all three albums, arriving after heavy UK and European touring.
items._cn_summary: Black Doldrums 即将发行的专辑《Repetition Compulsion》标志着其「心灵状态三部曲」的完结，前两张分别是2022年的《Dead Awake》和2024年的《In Limerence》。整张专辑围绕弗洛伊德提出的「强迫重复」心理学概念展开，探讨无意识中重演熟悉情感模式与破坏性行为的主题。全辑十一首曲目从首单《Repetition》出发，创作者Gibbard透露该曲围绕单一riff构建怨曲式段落，并通过音乐层面的重复手法呼应主题。乐队在创作上受到80年代哥特后朋克、合成器流行和暗潮的影响，同时融入John Carpenter与Vangelis的电影配质感，编曲以层叠模拟合成器、合唱吉他与驱动型节奏为基础。核心创作源于Gibbard与Sophie Landers之间紧密的私人合作关系，使得歌词带有人格解离式的对话感，并采用双声部人声构筑内在张力。

items.body: New York darkwave duo R. Missing will get a limited clear-white transparent vinyl LP of its album “Like the Sound of Injured Love” on October 2, 2026, alongside a regular digiCD edition, through the Italian label Young & Cold. The album originally came out digitally in December 2025 and combines darkwave, coldwave, dream pop and electronic elements. The LP is limited to 444 copies, while the digiCD comes in a Digipak sleeve limited to 250 copies; both carry the same eleven tracks. Young & Cold describes the record as an atmospheric album that opens with a mysterious, captivating tone from its first track, driven by electronic sounds that give the music a modern, dreamy quality alongside calm, distinctive vocals. The label singles out “Dreamletting” and “Let in the Night Outside” as highlights of R. Missing’s style, and calls “Telepolartears” memorable for its “fascinating sound.” Tracklist for ‘Like the Sound of Injured Love’ The LP spreads its eleven songs across two sides: side one holds “Like the Sound of Injured Love,” “Telepolartears,” “Dreamletting,” “Let in the Night Outside,” “Dear Contests” and “Supermuted,” while side two holds “Ola Tremble,” “infinifalls,” “Pony Yeah,” “Shadowist” and “Cloud Without Tear.” The digiCD carries the same eleven tracks in a single sequence. A video for the title track, “Like the Sound of Injured Love,” is available online. About R. Missing R. Missing is a darkwave duo based in New York City. Side-Line previously covered the project in August 2023 for a cover of Siouxsie and the Banshees’ “Spellbound.” “Like the Sound of Injured Love” was released digitally in December 2025 and combines darkwave, coldwave, dream pop and electronic production. Young & Cold, the label behind this physical edition, now brings the album to a limited clear-white transparent vinyl LP and a digiCD, distributed through Audioglobe.
items._cn_summary: 本文介绍纽约暗潮二人组R. Missing通过意大利独立厂牌Young & Cold发行专辑《Like the Sound of Injured Love》实体版本的消息。专辑融合暗潮、冷潮、梦幻流行与电子制作元素，以神秘氛围和冷静人声为标志，营造出既现代又梦幻的听觉质感。实体版采用限量透明白胶和Digipak数字CD两种形式，分别限定444张和250张，配以双面曲目排列。厂牌特别推荐《Dreamletting》《Let in the Night Outside》与《Telepolartears》作为专辑亮点，并释出同名曲目的影像作品。该组合此前以翻唱Siouxsie and the Banshees的《Spellbound》引发关注，整体风格延续了后朋克与暗潮的阴郁气质。

items.body: South African musician and vocalist Mia van Wyk has spent the past decade recording as Hunter As a Horse, or HAAH, releasing a varied succession of electronic dark-pop singles and EPs from her base in the Western Cape. Her songs have often carried the scale of miniature films: private crises placed against large backdrops, with synthesizers, programmed rhythms, and van Wyk’s coolly controlled voice providing both the setting and its unsettled central presence. After signing with Metropolis Records earlier this year, HAAH has released her long-awaited debut album, Paradise Lost. The record moves between alternative pop, indie electronics, dream-pop, dance music, and nu-goth, shifting from propulsive tracks to slower, more spacious pieces without losing its sense of internal unity. For an artist whose earlier releases frequently operated as independent worlds, the album represents a considerable change in scale. Its songs belong to the same emotional period and circle a connected set of concerns: death, addiction, CPTSD, astral visions, magical thinking, and the uneasy business of examining the parts of oneself that polite society recommends keeping out of view. “This album deals with my shadow, my transformation and my inner architecture,” says van Wyk. “I have tried to show what is deep inside myself. I discovered that the things I was taught to bury were never my enemies, but are actually my power.” The language of Paradise Lost is grand without becoming remote. Van Wyk thinks in terms of ruins, crowns, monsters, resurrection, and revenge, yet these images remain tied to recognizable psychological experience. The record’s supernatural vocabulary offers a way of discussing survival without reducing it to a tidy lesson or a reassuring conclusion. Propelled by a taut dance beat, the darkwave-driven title track coils through the album’s broad dynamic range. The video places Hunter as a Horse in a garage workshop, singing directly into the camera with rows of tools behind her. Grainy black-and-white footage of Appalachian serpent-handling worship cuts through the performance, showing congregants praying, dancing, raising snakes, and collapsing in religious ecstasy as temptation, danger, faith, and salvation converge. Watch the video for the title track below: Styles change, tempos contract and accelerate, but the songs on Paradise Lost appear to share the same architecture, as though each opens onto a different room in a vast, faintly dangerous house. Van Wyk’s interest in misunderstood figures also supplies the album with its moral logic. She looks toward people and creatures traditionally cast as threats, studying the injuries and adaptations concealed inside their reputations. “A lot changed for me during that time personally and I went through a kind of integration process where I started confronting things more,” she elaborates. “Writing the album felt like a natural expression of that. In the past, I often struggled to bring songs together because they felt too different, but this time everything came from a similar emotional place and period in my life.” With her inspiration often stemming from unusual sources, van Wyk reveals that “I have always been drawn to the villains in stories, the ones who were feared and misunderstood, and I have often found beauty in places other people are afraid to look – the strange, the haunted, the macabre. Some people see monsters. I see stories. I see what survived. I see how it transformed. This album is resurrection, obsession, desire, revenge, surrender, love and my shadow. I don’t believe darkness is always something to be destroyed. Sometimes it’s the only part of you strong enough to save you. This album isn’t about conventional ‘healing’. It’s about walking out of the ruins wearing the crown.” Listen to Paradise Lost below and order the album here. Paradise Lost by Hunter As a Horse The foundations of Paradise Lost can be traced to Anathema, the 2025 EP on which van Wyk first began treating separate songs as parts of a larger design. That release encouraged her to think beyond the single as an isolated statement and toward the album as a sustained act of disclosure. “It was the first time I really started thinking in terms of a connected body of work, so it felt natural to take that further with ‘Paradise Lost’, she explains. “It is designed to be heard as one piece, even though the songs are quite different individually.” HAAH’s music has already appeared in American Horror Story, Riverdale, and Elite, as well as the film Wander Darkly and several international advertising campaigns. With Paradise Lost, van Wyk finally gathers the breadth of that work into a full-length record, finding order among obsessions that once seemed too unruly to occupy the same space. Follow Hunter As A Horse: Instagram Facebook TikTok YouTube Bandcamp The post Hunter as a Horse Confronts Serpents and Salvation in Video for “Paradise Lost” — Debut Album Out Now! appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 南非音乐人Mia van Wyk以Hunter As a Horse之名在开普敦创作多年，首张全长专辑《Paradise Lost》在Metropolis Records厂牌下发行，将另类流行、独立电子、梦幻流行与nu-goth等多种风格编织成统一的情感架构。专辑围绕死亡、成瘾、复杂性创伤后应激障碍、星象异象等内心议题展开，合成器音景与冷峻控制的人声构筑出不安的精神图景。她借用废墟、王冠、怪物、复活等夸张意象讨论生存体验，拒绝给出安慰性结论。标题曲的MV混合暗潮律动与阿巴拉契亚山区蛇礼崇拜的黑白影像，将诱惑、危险、信仰与救赎并置呈现。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: Los Cenzontles 的这张专辑源于十九世纪加州牛仔前往夏威夷牧牛的历史脉络，呈现出墨西哥与夏威夷两种被刻板印象化的音乐文化的深度对话。16 首曲目以西班牙语、夏威夷语和英语演唱，包含老夏威夷歌曲配新西语歌词、老墨西哥歌曲配新夏威夷语歌词，以及全新创作和美国传统曲目。专辑在加州旧金山湾区的一间录音室五天内基本同期录制完成，保留了即兴与现场感。Taj Mahal 和 David Hidalgo 作为核心催化剂参与编曲与演奏，与夏威夷本地音乐人及学院学员同台合作，呈现出语言、文化、年龄和性别上的多元协作。尤克里里、墨西哥竖琴、手风琴与滑弦吉他交织出独特的跨太平洋声音谱系，翻唱 Woody Guthrie 的《Deportee》更将音乐引向移民劳工的社会现实议题。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，由北欧民间场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统素材，融入成员各自视角与原创作品。开场曲以粗犷奔放的节奏展示Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口簧琴与风笛推动节奏律动。匈牙利扬琴为传统民谣曲目增添细腻层次，口簧琴与长笛、弦乐交织的器乐终曲展现出弹簧般弹跳感和些许失衡的惊喜。整体笼罩着古老、质朴的氛围，乐队虽初出茅庐却显得成熟老练，为传统北欧民谣带来现代诠释的雏形。

items.body: Photo: Hilary Scott   Nordic Boomers at Tanglewood Festival of Contemporary Music July 27, 2026 Published in Sequenza 21 By Christian Carey   LENOX – The annual Festival of Contemporary Music concludes with an orchestra concert by the Tanglewood Music Center Orchestra. This year, the festival was curated by Esa-Pekka Salonen, and featured themed programs spotlighting emerging composers, Gen X creators, and Monday’s concert, “Nordic Boomers,” dedicated to fifty and sixty-something Scandinavian composers. Most were colleagues of Salonen from his early days as a student composer. These connections were fruitful, but each composer forged their own path, as was evidenced by the FCM concert. Magnus Lindberg’s Serenades (2020) was curiously named, as it had a muscular demeanor that seemed at odds with its title. Salonen conducted, bringing out details of its vivid orchestration and soaring lines. The piece contained a small quote from Beethoven’s Opus 111. The same source reference point would play a large role in a piece later on in the program. Hans Abrahamsen’s let me tell you (2013), in a libretto crafted by Paul Griffiths, is a setting of the words spoken by the character Ophelia in Shakespeare’s Hamlet. One of Abrahamsen’s best known works, it contains a challenging, wide-ranging and expressively intricate part for solo soprano. Alexandra Henderson sang its demanding and declamatory lines with thoughtful interpretative skill, and displayed plummy low notes and a well-supported upper register. Lauren Smith conducted with nuanced attention to dynamics and phrasing. Anders Hillborg’s Kongsgaard Variations (2006) used the aforementioned quotation, from the arietta movement from Beethoven’s Opus 111 piano sonata, as the basis for a series of variations that he considered meditations rather than the often found developing trajectory of the form. A string orchestra piece, its expert writing was deployed in a variety of playing demeanors. A particularly attractive section featured solo violin, viola, and cello trading folk style melodies in a manner reminiscent of the music played on a Hardinger fiddle, Norway’s national instrument. Elsewhere were neoclassical, minimal, pastoral and modernist variations of the Beethoven theme, some allowing it center stage if slightly morphed, with it instead being submerged in others. Julian Gilewski conducted an effusive, shimmering version of Hillborg’s abundantly attractive piece. The concert concluded with Salonen’s Cello Concerto (2016), conducted by the composer. Written for Yo-Yo Ma, the piece has an extraordinarily challenging solo part. Senja Rummakainen played it with impressive virtuosity and admirable commitment. Cello concertos are notorious for balance issues, but Salonen’s comprehensive knowledge of the orchestra made space both for multihued and powerful orchestral passages and vivid solo writing. The second movement included electronics, with looping of seagull glissandos, an extended technique, interweaving into knots of sound. The third movement features something of a second soloist, with percussionist Patrick Sorah playing bongos, sharing center stage with Rummakainen, his syncopated performance ricocheting in mercurial duets with the cellist. The Festival Orchestra was well-prepared and performed the formidable program with musicality and consummate professionalism. Salonen’s curation of the whole FCM was inspired, and one hopes that he remains a part of Tanglewood’s activities for many years to come. Christian Carey The post Tanglewood Festival of Contemporary Music – Nordic Boomers appeared first on Sequenza21.
items._cn_summary: 文章报道了2026年坦格尔伍德当代音乐节闭幕音乐会，主题为"北欧婴儿潮"，聚焦五六十岁北欧作曲家群体。音乐总监萨洛宁策划的这场演出包含四部作品：林德伯格的《小夜曲》（2020）以强劲管弦乐配器为特征，内含贝多芬作品111的引用；阿布拉汉森的《让我告诉你》（2013）为女高音与乐队而作，歌词取自莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》中奥菲莉亚的台词，演唱技术难度极高；希尔博格的《康斯加变奏曲》（2006）以贝多芬钢琴奏鸣曲第三乐章为主题进行系列变奏，弦乐写作融合挪威民俗风格与多种现代手法；萨洛宁本人的《大提琴协奏曲》（2016）使用电子音效与海鸥滑音循环，展现了作者对乐队音响的精妙掌控力。整场演出呈现出北欧当代音乐对古典传统的引用与重构。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的乐评，而是关于一个名为"隐形学院"的影展与现场音乐活动在英国黑斯廷斯电子宫殿电影院开幕的预告。该项目由The Wire杂志的Joseph Stannard组织，作为其先前"外层教堂"项目的延续，将放映怪诞、神秘、超自然题材的实验电影，并配合美国电子艺术家Trigger Object和Dream Skills的现场表演。首期将放映Wire专栏作家Philip Brophy于1993年拍摄的Body Melt，并附有导演新录制的介绍。整体内容聚焦于实验影像与现场电子音乐的跨界结合，呈现出地下艺术场景中视听融合的策展思路，但文章信息较短，主要为活动新闻介绍。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Late Night Laments' is a 2020 studio album from Tim Bowness, and it follows up two really solidreleases of his - 'Lost In the Ghost Light' and 'Flowers at the Scene', both of which exhibited abeautifully nostalgic art rock dynamic, within which the haunting enunciated vocals of Bownessbecame one of the defining qualities of the albums. Now, the problem with 'Late Night Laments' isthat the music isn't really developed any further. In fact, this record barely distinguishes itselffrom its predecessors - it is mellow, laid-back, and dreamy, a kind of poppy singer-songwriterexperiment. Bowness is joined by keyboardist Brian Hulse, by the way, who is the primary albumcollaborator.The songs are textured and light, enveloped in a moody atmosphere with subtle ambient undertones.Furthermore, the use of electronic elements is also prevalent, which recalls some of the classic 90sNo-Man releases. I like how Bowness' voice is emphasized by the minimal instrumentation, as it makesfor a moving and effective delivery, but this aspect of the album might be deemed uninspiring bylisteners expecting something more upbeat and eclectic. Of the songs appearing on this LP, Idefinitely enjoyed 'I'm Better Now', 'Darkline', 'Never a Place', and 'Hidden Life' (which aresomewhat darker than the rest of the album). 'Late Night Laments' is a record that demands aparticular mood in order to be appreciated completely, as it leans a little too heavily on thedream-pop influence of its predecessors.
items._genre: art rock / dream pop / ambient electronic
items._cn_summary: 这是Tim Bowness 2020年的录音室专辑，作为他前两张作品的延续，依然保持着怀旧而忧郁的艺术摇滚基调。键盘手Brian Hulse作为主要合作者参与制作，音乐整体呈现出轻柔、慵懒、梦幻的气质，氛围化的环境电子元素贯穿其中，与90年代No-Man的某些作品有所呼应。极简化的器乐编排突出了人声的表达，使嗓音成为情感传递的核心。然而评论指出，这张专辑在风格上与前作缺乏明显区隔，延续性大于突破性，对期待更多变化和活力的听众来说可能显得缺乏新意。推荐曲目包括《I'm Better Now》《Darkline》《Never a Place》和《Hidden Life》，这些歌曲相较其他曲目更为暗色调。整张专辑需要在特定情绪下聆听，过度依赖梦流行的影响是其局限所在。

items.body:
Will Long dons his dancing slippers for another deep house sojourn on his Long Trax Productions, blowing kisses in the direction of Larry Heard, Ron Trent, DJ Sprinkles.

One decade since minting the ‘Long Trax’ series on Terre Thaemlitz’s label, Comatonse, Will Long slow cooks six new additions on his personal folio, taking all the time needed to get right into the groove. Trust there’s no fireworks or over-produced trickery, just hypnotic deep house that unfurls with a real sense of space, patience and deferred gratification.

Long in his element, following his nose to pair the barest ingredients in classic style and pattern, as with with the likes of ‘About Where It's At (Now You Went N' Did It mix)’, which takes over 4 mins happily swinging away before introducing its lonesome flute motif, or a standout ‘Have to Have Something’ lost in the flow, where the bassline only thickens as it goes along. 

We’re also partial to the square bass budge of ‘Have To Have Something (S' a Lotta Shade mix)’, and the mesmerising meld of creamy bass and piquant cowbell pinging on ‘The Problems’, also found warped with trippier effect on its Metallic Dub reshape.
items._genre: deep house / minimal house / hypnotic house
items._cn_summary: Will Long 在自家厂牌 Long Trax Productions 发行第六张该系列专辑，延续其十余年来对深度浩室风格的执着探索。整张作品采取慢炖式制作思路，六首曲目均以极简配料构建：先是长达四分多钟的律动铺垫，才让孤独的长笛旋律线浮现；贝斯线条随时间推移逐渐增厚；方波贝斯与牛铃的搭配形成催眠般的绵密质地。专辑明显受到 Larry Heard、Ron Trent、DJ Sprinkles 等前辈的影响，强调空间感、耐心与延迟满足，没有烟火气十足的过度制作。整体风格克制内敛，呈现典型的芝加哥/纽约式深度浩室美学，但实验性与突破性较为有限。

items.body:
Breezy new age house by an Antipodean artist with illustrious credits beside Michal Hutchence, Bono, Jamiroquai since the ‘80s, evened out with Kuniyuki and 451 remixes...

"Originally emerging from Melbourne’s post-punk and new wave underground in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Gus Till has spent more than four decades navigating a remarkably diverse musical path. From early electronic experimentation with Third Eye alongside Ollie Olsen, through a pivotal role in the formative years of the global psy-trance movement and collaborations with artists including Michael Hutchence, System 7, Manu Dibango, Todd Terry and Bim Sherman, Till’s work has consistently resisted easy categorisation, moving fluidly between ambient music, downtempo, house, trance and psychedelic electronica.

First released on Japan’s Dakini Records in 2006, ‘Rainsong’ captures many of these threads in a single expansive composition. Built around a pulsating bassline, layered live percussion and soaring vocal elements, the track sits comfortably between the dancefloor and more immersive listening environments. Unfolding patiently across nearly thirteen minutes, it combines hypnotic rhythmic momentum with a rich sense of atmosphere and musicality.

For the B-side, Kuniyuki Takahashi offers a distinct reinterpretation of the original. His remix gradually unfolds from a patient introduction into a deep and richly textured exploration of the track’s core themes. Subtle spatial processing, nuanced arrangement shifts and his unmistakable sense of atmosphere transform the source material while preserving its emotional core."
items._cn_summary: Gus Till 来自墨尔本，自1970年代末以来在电子、浩室、迷幻电子乐等多个领域间游走，与多位国际艺术家有过合作。2006年首次在日本小型厂牌发行的《Rainsong》是一首近十三分钟的扩展作品，以脉动低音线、层叠现场打击乐与高远人声元素为骨架，在舞曲律动与沉浸式聆听之间寻找平衡。Kuniyuki Takahashi 的B面混音版本则以从容的展开方式重新诠释原作，通过细腻的空间处理与编排变化，在保留情感内核的同时呈现出深沉的氛围感。两首作品共同展现了一种跨越流派界限的电子音乐美学。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — More than a catharsis, it feels like a descent into the depths, built upon guitar and bass, yet the Minimoog introduces a different sensation that gives the track lift and elevates the musical vision of "Catastasis," the opening song on Elder's seventh album.Two guitars. Two keyboards. A composition with an epic scope that differs radically from that of classic heavy metal. It leans closer to Rush, creating the impression that every head-banging, aggressive passage... culminates in another that tears open portals to a different dimension, prompting a different kind of head-nodding altogether. Next comes a chorus led by Behrang Alavi, followed by a succession of riffs that constantly outdo one another. It is orchestral heavy metal without an actual orchestra, a sound that is symphonic and grand, yet loses none of its power or even its aggressive edge."Endless Return" moves at a breakneck pace that offers no respite; Behrang Alavi handles the vocals here, while the two guitars display virtuosity, building a powerful, and highly original, melody in tandem with the drums. The track's progressive character is further enhanced when the Mellotron and bass kick in. Bass-driven instrumental sections featuring guitar runs evoke the best of Rush, yet the entry of the synthesizer rounds out the perfect sonic picture the band has crafted. It is evident that they prioritized not only playing with skill and intensity but also composing original, vibrant pieces."Coalescence" gives the impression that they can't quite contain the momentum they've unleashed?reminiscent of the opening of "Close to the Edge", but then a more meditative passage with Mellotron kicks in. Just as I'm reminded of King Crimson, a highly original section emerges that doesn't call to mind anyone else, only Elder themselves. It possesses a psychedelic and almost jazzy sensibility, without ever explicitly crossing into that genre, driven by a melody that instantly hooks you. It's as if they've captured the best of both worlds: harmony and power, plus that dash of surprise that keeps you glued to the music."Merged in Dreams - Ne Plus Ultra" has a drawn-out opening that almost lulls one into a state of lethargy... the album title, Innate Passage, reminded me of that Kafka story about the door made just for us, one we didn't dare step through, only to see it close as the end approached... leaving us to realize the truth too late. Everything lies within us, and sometimes something awakens it, acting as a catalyst; I like to think of the object on the cover as such a catalyst, something each of us can use for ourselves. In fact, the music itself is exactly that.Nicholas DiSalvo sings and plays guitar alongside drum breaks that recall the wilder moments of Gong's You, building a pyramid of distortion that suddenly collapses, as if made of sand, revealing that what we had been witnessing was merely a desert mirage. When the two guitars join forces, it feels like an explosive finale, with playing as rapid as Steve Howe's during his classic era.Then comes a keyboard sequence that feels almost electronic; when the guitar and drums kick in, it resembles a beating heart, racing at times. This leads into the closing track, "The Purpose," which revisits that electro-rock vibe, with notes that lend the song a sense of maturity. Innate Passage does not disappoint; instead, it fuels that inner fire, that light that never goes out.
items._genre: heavy prog / psychedelic prog / progressive metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以两把吉他与两台键盘构建出交响化的金属音景，乐句编排追求层次递进与段落张力。评论者将其与Rush、King Crimson等前卫摇滚标杆相比较，强调旋律与即兴段落的有机结合。Minimoog、Mellotron等复古键盘的运用扩展了传统重金属的音色边界，使作品在保持力量感的同时具备沉思与迷幻的维度。每首曲目都设计了多段落结构，从狂飙的器乐段落到冥想式的过渡层层推进。专辑通过金属编制实现了近似交响乐的宏伟感，歌词与概念围绕内在觉醒与转化展开，以封面意象作为触发觉醒的隐喻。整体制作追求乐器间的复杂对话与情感起伏的交替，但本质上仍属于以摇滚乐器编制为核心的前卫金属范畴。

items.body: Review by OlyaBeginner — Listening to this tribute album felt like walking through familiar landscapes that suddenly open in a new light. Each track keeps the spirit of Depeche Mode, but also brings its own emotional depth, hidden meanings, and soft discoveries. I let the sound guide me through feelings, as if I was travelling inside both the past and something renewed.But Not Tonight The atmosphere is gentle and heartfelt. From the very beginning, the melody breathes sincerity. It feels touching and emotional, as if light itself wants to comfort. There is a sense of development ? inspiration to move forward, to grow, to reach for something bright. The composition gives hope and tenderness at the same time.World Full of Nothing The entrance is very light, flowing like air. The vocal creates the sensation of flight, of being above everything ordinary. Then comes the acceleration ? like the process of reaching a goal or realization. Finally, calmness returns, a peaceful landing after movement. The track teaches to breathe again after striving.The Things You Said This version is more lyrical than the original. It feels deeply emotional and intimate. The voice sounds almost magical, creating the feeling of being submerged into someone's secret thoughts. It's like a quiet dialogue between hearts that once knew sorrow and still remember beauty.Blue Dress Here appears the image of the road, the path. The rhythm invites movement, but also reflection. The vocal creates a romantic atmosphere, full of warmth and longing. It's not about distance, but about closeness ? about walking together through the unknown.Sibeling A mysterious night sky opens above the listener. There are stars, strange signals, maybe echoes of something cosmic. A quiet unease lives inside the sound ? a feeling of something unresolved, of searching. Then comes realization, acceptance, and a decision to move on. The music calms down as if peace was finally found in the middle of mystery.Enjoy the Silence The atmosphere here is magical and light. The voice gives softness, almost like silk on the surface of air. Gradually the sound grows stronger, more intense ? as if emotions expand beyond control. Then the voice returns again to bring comfort, to balance. The ending carries the listener away into clouds, into quiet joy. It's the emotional peak of the album ? a nine-minute journey through dream, reflection, and inner freedom.Together these compositions reveal the hidden depths of the familiar songs. The band develops the melodic foundation of Depeche Mode into something renewed ? sensitive, emotional, and thoughtful. What once seemed simple now opens with unexpected power. This tribute doesn't imitate; it transforms. It reminds that music lives not only in sound, but also in our personal discoveries and inner movements.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张向Depeche Mode致敬的专辑，将原作的合成器流行基底重新演绎为前卫渐进风格。评论者强调每首曲目都保留了原作的精神内核，同时注入更深层的情感深度与隐喻意涵。从轻柔的旋律展开到情绪的逐步积累，再到九分钟长度的高潮段落，专辑在结构上展现出渐进摇滚特有的呼吸感与展开逻辑。声乐处理偏向抒情与亲密，与原版的工业感形成对比。整体呈现为对熟悉作品的情感重塑而非简单模仿，强调内省式的聆听体验。

items.body: Review by Archisorcerus — I discovered this obscure gem in the autumnal times of the year 2024, and got immediately hooked by the music here. This project has offered only this jewel as of yet, however its mastermind "Lord Vrajitor" (and more aliases with the word vrajitor) still seems busy with some other projects, most of which, methinks, are within the black metal domains. Don't get outright frightened, this album of him/theirs (theirs, because he is not the sole musician in the album) is pure prog rock. Or not so pure... At least, it has nothing to do with metal, let alone the notorious black metal. Or is there a sinister connection?.. Haha. Vrajitor means wizard/sorcerer in the Romanian language. Too romantic, isn't it. Ha-ha! - As you can guess from my username, I'm quite interested in such "names", and I already had learned what vrajitor means before even hearing about this band.Well... This is really a solid album, I think. Not too avant-garde, though, unlike its label suggests. Vrajitor seems like a young guy, and perhaps in time he can sharpen his blade and cut through the vines which can block the path to achieve some real authentic originality. This really requires some maturity in general. I didn't want to say that this album is not original, I just cannot hear anything that makes me say "Wow, I've never heard anything like this before!" - Yet, this is a really atmospheric output that has a great soul, besides its musical solidity; which is an invaluable asset. It can sound nostalgic, magickal, occultic (and so forth), and the record is really of high quality in general.Though there are some problems in it, if not major. Firstly, the "fade-out trick" was used thrice, two of which are not okay for me by any means. Secondly, in the 4th track's 0:28 second, I really hear a timing error in drums. No matter how many times I listen to the album (which as of yet should be 20-30 times), that timing inaccuracy still disturbs me, though slightly. Normally I could have overlooked it, but in the rest of the album we hear some flawless musicianship, so that little timing thing really disturbs me a bit. The crash hitting is a bit late there. Dunno if it is a deliberate artistic twist, which can be seen in prog rock, but I frankly get displeased by it. These 2 are all. I mean I have no other "complaints" concerning this truly impressive work.If Lord/Magus Vrajitor releases some other works with this band of his, I'd definitely get excited enough to check them out. His black metal stuff?.. I don't envision myself doing so. Mind you, I like me some black metal stuff, but they are really too scarce... Maybe this album of Vrajitor's Tenebrarium has no direct relation with black metal musically, but it seems to have an indirect one... This album is labeled as "dungeon funk" as well. I had never heard of such a genre before discovering this band/album. Presumably, it is kinda like the genre entitled dungeon synth, albeit not that dismal, conversely uplifting perhaps. Lord Vrajitor also has a dungeon synth past, as I read/know... Yeah, kinda the medievalesque "air" of dungeon synth is here, but without the toxic depressivity. Let the oceans of good spirits seep in! The connection here is that, dungeon synth has some ancient and very strong ties with black metal. In the genesis of the dungeon synth, there already was the nefarious black metal residing in the nightside of Eden, whispering some ominous incantations in dungeon synth's ears...4/5 stars. So, definitely recommended.
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / dungeon funk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由罗马尼亚音乐人Lord Vrajitor主导，虽以交响前卫摇滚为核心框架，却自称"地牢放克"这一冷门标签，暗示其试图融合氛围化的暗黑元素与前卫结构。乐评人认为专辑氛围感出色，具有怀旧、神秘、隐喻性的灵魂气质，整体演奏质量扎实。然而，专辑被认为缺乏真正令人惊叹的原创性，更像是一张扎实但尚未完全成熟的类型作品。具体问题包括：三处使用淡出手法其中两处显得生硬，以及第四轨0:28秒处鼓点时值存在偏差，在其他部分近乎完美的演奏水准映衬下尤为突兀。乐评人对创作者的未来发展抱有期待，认为其需要更多时间打磨才能形成真正独特的个人风格。

items.body: Melbourne-based gothic/darkwave/industrial duo Velatine has released the Dead Radio EP on July 28, 2026, available digitally via Bandcamp and streaming platforms including Spotify. The four-track EP centers on new versions of “Playing with the Orbits”, a song the band first released as a single earlier in 2026. Playing with the Orbits – Dead Radio EP by Velatine Tracklist for Velatine’s ‘Dead Radio EP’ The tracklist comprises “Dead Radio Remix”, “Late Night Club Mix”, “Dead Radio Remix (Extended)” and “Absinthe Remix”. The closing “Absinthe Remix” combines acoustic guitar, violin and industrial electronic elements with the duo’s established gothic and darkwave sound. “Playing with the Orbits” was written by Velatine member Loki Lockwood about the 2019 murder of Bianca Devins, an American teenager killed by a man she had met online, and the subsequent circulation of images from the crime scene on social media. The song had previously been released with a different vocalist; the “Dead Radio Remix” on this EP is presented as a reworked version that better reflects the project’s current direction, shaped by the band’s recent live performances. About Velatine Velatine is a gothic/darkwave duo from Melbourne, Australia, formed by Loki Lockwood and Maggie Alley in late 2021. Lockwood had previously been active as a producer in the projects The Drones and Spencer P. Jones before starting Velatine. The duo released its first seven-inch single, “Comic” / “No God”, in March 2022, followed by the industrial-leaning track “Deadly Requiem” that August and a second seven-inch, “Whisper Park” / “One and Only”, in November 2022, accompanied by a video directed by Mathew T Ellery. A remix of “No God”, paired with footage from the 1973 film “Frankenstein”, followed shortly after. In February 2023, Velatine released its debut album, “I Won’t Be Civilised”, on Spooky Records, preceded by the singles “No God”, “Comic” and “Whisper Park”. The band has continued to perform live regularly since, a period the duo credits with shaping the more industrial-leaning direction heard on the “Dead Radio EP”.

items.body: Industrial electronic artist Silent Impulse will release a new EP, “The Shape of Consequence,” on July 31, 2026, available exclusively via Bandcamp. The three-track EP opens with restrained, atmospheric compositions before giving way to heavier, rhythm-driven pieces that build steadily in intensity. “The Shape of Consequence” balances cinematic ambience with driving industrial percussion, tracing a progression from quiet tension to uncompromising momentum across its three tracks. New material builds on ‘Invasive Forms’ The EP follows Silent Impulse’s most recent album, “Invasive Forms,” released in March 2026 with four tracks ranging from 100 to 130 BPM that mix harsh percussive frameworks with melodic synths, heavy atmospheres and distorted textures. “The Shape of Consequence” continues that cold industrial approach while shifting the arc of the release toward a more deliberate build from calm to intensity. About Silent Impulse Silent Impulse is the industrial electronic project of Joe Abrescia, formed in 2024 in the United States. The project mixes electro-industrial elements, pairing melodic synth work with harsh percussive frameworks and distorted textures. Silent Impulse released the “Invasive Forms” album in March 2026, and follows it with “The Shape of Consequence,” a three-track EP due July 31, 2026, exclusively through Bandcamp.
items._cn_summary: 这篇来自Side-Line的报道并非原创乐评，而是一篇标准的新闻通稿，介绍了工业电子艺术家Silent Impulse即将于2026年7月底通过Bandcamp独家发行的三曲EP《The Shape of Consequence》。文章描述了EP的创作构思：从开篇克制、氛围化的音景铺垫，逐步过渡到节奏密集、强度递增的工业打击乐段落，在电影感氛围与强劲工业节拍之间寻求平衡。该EP延续了2026年3月发行的全长专辑《Invasive Forms》的冰冷工业美学，融合了硬朗的打击乐框架、旋律化合成器、厚重的氛围层次以及失真质感。作品以三首曲目构建了从安静张力到不妥协推进力的弧线，作为独立小厂牌发行的带状录音作品，整体延续了暗潮与工业电子交叉地带的声音语汇。

items.body: Finnish Gothic Rock act Hateful Chains will release a new single, “Entities,” on August 7, 2026. The song is the band’s first written fully collaboratively, combining a swing/shuffle beat with a 7/4 time signature. “Entities” grew out of an idea by guitarist Kimmo Laaksonen to pair the shuffle groove with the odd meter, with vocalist Flora Kok then contributing lyrics and a chorus. The band describes the track’s subject as things that always come back to haunt you: “the entities you thought you’d cast away have returned and they are waiting for an opportunity to take you back. In fact, they never left in the first place: they were lurking inside your walls all this time.” The imitating vocal lines and odd timing build a strange, eerie atmosphere, with elements of Southern Rock adding a threatening edge. First collaborative songwriting credit for the band “Entities” was written by Flora Kok and Kimmo Laaksonen together, with lyrics by Kok and arrangement credited to the full band. The single is released via Eight Floor Music (FI-KL5-26-00005). About Hateful Chains Hateful Chains was launched in Finland in 2018. The band combines the dark sounds and aesthetics of Goth with elements of Indie Rock and Metal. They signed with Danse Macabre Records in 2020 and released their debut album, “Invite,” in 2021, followed by a second album, “Lambs and Goats,” in 2025. In 2026 Hateful Chains made their first appearance at Wave Gotik Treffen. The band is Flora Kok on vocals, keyboards and acoustic guitars, Kimmo Laaksonen on guitars, Jani Ilander on bass and Jani Vilhunen on drums. “Entities” continues the band’s run of singles following “Lambs and Goats,” with the collaborative writing process marking a new step for the group.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰哥特摇滚乐队Hateful Chains将于2026年8月发布新单曲《Entities》，这是乐队首次完全协作创作的作品。吉他手Kimmo Laaksonen提出将摇摆/切分节奏与7/4拍复合节拍相结合的想法，主唱Flora Kok在此基础上完成歌词与副歌部分。歌曲主题围绕那些始终缠绕不去的事物展开——被以为已被驱逐的实体其实从未离开，一直潜伏在内心深处。模仿式的人声线条与奇数拍节奏共同营造出诡异不安的氛围，南方摇滚元素的融入增添了威胁感。乐队自2018年成立于芬兰，融合哥特美学与独立摇滚及金属元素，曾签约Danse Macabre Records，于2021年和2025年分别发行两张专辑，2026年首次亮相Wave Gotik Treffen音乐节。

items.body: Independent post-punk and shoegaze project The Faded Trees released a debut EP, “Strange Summer”, moving between post-punk tension and immersive shoegaze textures. Strange Summer by The Faded Trees The EP runs four tracks: “The Faded Trees,” “Vision Of Nothing,” “Strange Summer” and “Sometimes.” The project centers on dense, layered guitars, hypnotic bass lines and melancholic atmospheres, favoring intensity over immediacy. A DIY record built on contrast “Strange Summer” was born from a contrast between the surface light of summer and a quiet unease underneath, according to the project. The EP reflects a self-produced, DIY approach, with close attention paid to both sonic depth and visual identity. About The Faded Trees The Faded Trees is an independent post-punk and shoegaze project built around dense, layered guitar work and melancholic atmosphere. “Strange Summer” is the project’s debut release, a four-track EP self-produced and self-released via Bandcamp and streaming platforms.
items._cn_summary: The Faded Trees 首张 EP《Strange Summer》以四首曲目呈现后朋克与自赏派美学的融合。专辑围绕密集层叠的吉他、催眠式的贝斯线与忧郁氛围展开，强调强度而非即时感染力。创作理念源于夏日表面光明之下的不安情绪，通过自制的 DIY 制作方式完成，在声音深度与视觉呈现上均有所考量。四首曲目——同名曲、"Vision Of Nothing"、"Strange Summer" 和 "Sometimes"——构成短篇集式的结构，将后朋克的张力与沉浸式音墙质感并置。整体上，这是一张注重氛围营造与情绪表达的独立小品，风格内敛克制，适合偏好暗色调氛围音乐的听众深入聆听。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body: Review by D0BR0 — Flawless album. The lyrics and the album title make you think like good progressive rock does. Connecting with the powerfully deep, legend of Thor. Deep ideas about creation. As a child creates itself, real magic does occur as it is creating itself. Schizophrenia is also creation and the only way to "get to heaven now". Do not be afraid to add to, create and test your mind. The chosen become young again when they are altered but it is possible to rise from and funnel this lackadaisical play into more direct creative output. It is possible to become the bane of darkness mankind.After someone mentioned A Tab in the Ocean in a top prog list I was on the lookout for them. I was lucky enough to find Magic is a Child, A Tab in the Ocean and Remember the Future all on vinyl. Not too expensive at the time (Past 2005). I had Journey to the center to the Eye on cd. And would later buy Recycler brand new on cd.I remember hearing Magic is a Child in a certain altered state of mind in the morning. With all the things I think about, the lyrics just confirmed it for me and my mind was blown. Instant classic. I hung on every word. The same thing happened with Remember the Future as I aligned with my own narrative of what it meant to me based on my personal life. Easy to add new ideas when you were meant to discover something. The vocals took me awhile to get into but once I did he has a unique, kind of quavering voice. The musicianship is TIGHT on Magic is a Child. These guys are the best of the best.I recently picked up ...Sounds like This and Down to earth on MP3 cheap and it is like coming back home with all these extended jam sessions. Something very special about these guys. Contributed to who I am as I sift through things that may or may not directly speak to me.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张1977年的迷幻太空摇滚专辑，评论者描述了其在特定精神状态下的聆听体验。歌词围绕创造、心境突破与意识探索等主题展开，呼应北欧神话中关于索尔的传说意象。评论者强调专辑的演奏紧凑扎实，歌手的声线独特且略带颤抖，需要时间适应。整张作品被描述为充满深度歌词与概念性框架的前卫摇滚，倾向于通过长篇即兴段落和迷幻氛围营造沉浸感。然而，该评论更多停留在个人情感共鸣层面，缺乏对音乐结构、编曲细节或声音设计的具体分析，对专辑技术性维度的讨论较为有限。

Trisol releases “First Anthology” and “Second Anthology” as limited 3LP sets on 16 October 2026, each capped at 1,000 numbered copies. “First Anthology” was originally issued as a double CD in 2011, drawing on the band’s early years, its own label Candylan
items.body: Project Pitchfork, the German dark electro group fronted by Peter Spilles, gets a Project Pitchfork anthology vinyl release: two of its career-spanning compilations pressed to vinyl for the first time. Trisol releases “First Anthology” and “Second Anthology” as limited 3LP sets on 16 October 2026, each capped at 1,000 numbered copies. “First Anthology” was originally issued as a double CD in 2011, drawing on the band’s early years, its own label Candyland Entertainment and its later run on the major-label imprint EastWest. The new vinyl edition spreads 31 tracks across three 180g 12″ black vinyl records, a German audiophile pressing, and includes anthem tracks such as “Timekiller”, “Alpha Omega” and “I Live Your Dream”. The set comes in a gatefold sleeve with printed inner sleeves, and the artwork draws on photos from Peter Spilles’ private archive. “Second Anthology” followed in 2016 as a companion double CD covering the band’s catalogue from 2002 onward, built around the previously unreleased song “What Have We Done” and a remix, “Beholder (Puppet Master Mix)”. Its vinyl counterpart carries 30 tracks over three 180g 12″ records with the same gatefold, printed-inner-sleeve and archive-photo artwork treatment as its companion, and highlights key tracks “Rain”, “Acid Ocean” and “Beholder”. Both anthologies are limited to 1,000 numbered copies and are due through Trisol. Project Pitchfork anthology vinyl arrives ahead of anniversary tour The two anthology vinyls land in the same year Project Pitchfork mark their 35th anniversary. Side-Line previously reported on the band’s Dhyani 35th anniversary reissue, the 2LP deluxe edition of Entities, and the 35 Years in the Heart of Darkness anniversary tour running across Germany from October to December 2026 – the same window in which both anthology vinyls arrive. About Project Pitchfork Project Pitchfork was formed in Hamburg, Germany, by Peter Spilles and Dirk Scheuber, who met in late 1988 and began working together as Project Pitchfork the following year, picking the band’s name at random from a dictionary. The band played its first live show in Hamburg in February 1990 and released the demo “K.N.K.A.” that August. Debut album “Dhyani” followed in May 1991 on Hypnobeat, with second album “Lam-‘Bras” arriving in February 1992 and introducing Patricia Nigiani as a backing vocalist. Third album “Entities” followed six months later. A move to the Off Beat label produced 1994’s “Io,” which gave the band its first German chart entry via the singles “Renascence” and “Carrion,” followed by a lengthy tour. In 1995 Project Pitchfork founded their own label, Candyland Entertainment, releasing “Alpha Omega” the same year and touring in support of Rammstein. “¡Chakra:Red!” (1997) was the first album written as a full group effort and introduced Jürgen Jansen as a permanent member. The band then signed to major-label imprint EastWest for the concept album “Eon:Eon” (1998), whose singles “Steelrose,” “Carnival” and “I Live Your Dream” brought the band German music-TV airplay and an Echo Award nomination for the “Steelrose” video. Project Pitchfork released “Daimonion” (2001) and the “NUN” trilogy centered on “Inferno” (2002), then “Kaskade” (2005) and “Dream, Tiresias!” (2009). By 2011, having wound down Candyland, the band had moved to Trisol, releasing “Continuum Ride” (2010) and “Quantum Mechanics” (2011) – the same year Trisol issued the original “First Anthology” compilation. “Black” (2013) and “Blood” (2014) followed, and in 2016 Trisol released “Second Anthology,” built around the unreleased track “What Have We Done,” alongside 25th-anniversary album “Look Up, I’m Down There.” “Akkretion” (2018) and “Fragment” (2018) opened a further trilogy that closed with 2024’s “Elysium.” Co-founder Dirk Scheuber left the band in March 2021; the current lineup centers on Peter Spilles with Jürgen Jansen, alongside live drummers Achim Färber and Christian “Leo” Leonhardt. Trisol now brings both career-spanning anthologies to vinyl for the first time, due 16 October 2026 as limited, numbered 3LP editions.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Project Pitchfork两张精选专辑黑胶再版的新闻报道。该德国暗黑电子乐队由Peter Spilles于1990年代创立，融合EBM与工业电子元素，隶属于暗潮/工业音乐范畴。'First Anthology'收录乐队早期至EastWest厂牌时期的31首曲目，'Second Anthology'涵盖2002年后的30首作品，各限量1000套三碟180g黑胶发行。报道以厂牌信息、曲目列表和乐队历史年表为主，并未涉及音乐本身的声响分析、制作技法或艺术价值探讨。文章内容属于产品发布信息，缺乏对声音设计、编曲特点或创新性的评价。作为暗潮/EBM领域的再版资讯，对关注该类型的听众有一定参考价值，但文章本身深度有限。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — A radical shift awaited the Swedish band between their first album and this one, titled Tv�, which consists of just two lengthy tracks; the first, "G�ngl�t fr�n Vintergatan," lacks the complexity and density of its predecessor. It is only around the halfway mark that the organ introduces Eastern-tinged melodies with a 1960s psychedelic vibe; Celtic influences are present, as are echoes of Jethro Tull, evident not just in the flute work but in the composition itself.Midway through, the organ takes an even more prominent role, combining with the percussion to evoke the kind of soliloquies found in The Doors' music; however, the frenetic energy that linked the band's debut to the likes of Van der Graaf Generator or early Santana is missing here. Mikael �desj� delivers fine guitar work during a sort of jam session that nonetheless retains a distinctly Celtic feel."Kung Bores dans" is the album's second track, featuring organ work that, this time around, truly embarks on the anticipated journey, though it gives the impression of being a bit drawn-out without offering many fresh ideas. Instrumentally, it is flawless, and the transitions between sections are skillfully executed, handled with subtlety and shifting modos, at times even maintaining a tense, suspense-filled calm before the dramatic intrigue resumes. On this track, the guitar work is somewhat reminiscent of the Pink Floyd sound found on "Echoes" (from the album Meddle).Around the halfway mark, the organ and guitar take center stage, performing duets and sounding a bit like Camel on their debut album. Towards the end, the organ notes drop to a lower register, taking on a somewhat Canterbury-esque feel, and are impeccably accompanied by drummer Tim Wallander, who was making his debut on this record. The finale gains power and a certain darkness that suits it well, lending a depth that the Swedish forest setting had been lacking.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典乐队AGUSA发行，仅包含两首长篇曲目。第一首以东方色彩旋律开场，融合六十年代迷幻氛围、凯尔特元素与长笛演奏，带有Jethro Tull与The Doors的影子，但缺少前作那种与Van der Graaf Generator及早期Santana相连的狂热能量。吉他手Mikael Ådesjö在即兴段落中贡献了细腻的凯尔特风格演奏。第二首曲目的管风琴真正踏上了预期中的迷幻旅程，过渡段落处理巧妙，吉他音色令人联想到Pink Floyd《Echoes》，中段管风琴与吉他的二重奏带有Camel首张专辑的气质，尾声的低音管风琴与鼓手Tim Wallander的配合营造出Canterbury式的氛围，最终以黑暗有力的尾声收束。整体而言，这是一张器乐精湛、过渡细腻的迷幻/太空摇滚作品，但缺乏实验性突破。

items.body: Review by ianjferris@gmail.com — I will make no reference in this review to Volume One - The Shorts. That is for another time. This album, Volume Two of The Way We Walk - The Longs, is a very strong album. It packs some real power into its 70 minutes, with no weak moments. Now I know that some people will decry the fact that the older material (particularly the stuff from the "Peter Gabriel era") is stripped back to the bone and all included in a soft rock style medley of some nineteen and a half minutes. But lets face facts here. This older material comes from about 20 years previously. At the time this album was recorded in 1992, it was natural that Genesis (or any band still going strong after so many years) would cut back on the older stuff, in order to play their more contemporaneous material for that more modern crowd, a lot of whom may have still been in nappies (or diapers in the USA) or who may not have been born at all when the older material was first released! But what they do play here from the 1970's, in this 1992 live setting, is delivered with impressive power, with precision and not a little expertise. But it's not played in a "rough and raw" way. It's played with an air of accomplisment by the original authors/composers, who are now more accomplished musicians themselves. In fact, the original 1970's studio albums, absolutely brilliant as they are, just can't compete with this live delivery of the 1990's. The four long songs from the 1980's and 1990's - Driving The Last Spike, Domino, Fading Lights and Home By The Sea are also delivered with a lot more panache and power than their respective versions on the studio albums. These are the versions that define these Progressive Rock monsters for me. Yes, I do like the originals but these live renditions are my favourites.I saw Genesis playing live on the Duke Tour, as they were in the midst of transitioning from their 1970's Progressive Rock rooted style into their Art/Progressive Pop pomp of the 1980's and 1990's. They were magnificent back then, in 1980. unfortunately I just didn't get to see them on their The Way We Walk Tour in 1992. But based on this album, "The Longs" CD, I can only imagine that it must have been electrifying for the audience! I suppose that I really should now declare that I'm a committed and dedicated fan of Genesis, right through all phases and incarnations of the band. And thats why, even though this review is written fully in accordance with Progarchives Guidelines, I can't restrict my award for this album to 4 stars. I just can't do that. The album is too good for that. It's just as good as all their other live albums, from all the different eras over the decades. So I'm proceeding upwards and I'm giving the album the full 5 stars.
items._genre: symphonic prog / art rock / soft rock
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑收录Genesis 1992年巡演中的四首长篇作品，包括《Driving The Last Spike》《Domino》《Fading Lights》和《Home By The Sea》，以及一段约十九分半的1970年代旧作软摇滚风格串编。评论者认为乐队在现场演绎中表现出超越录音室版的力度与精准度，长篇曲目在编排上更具气势。作者承认自己是Genesis贯穿各时期的忠实粉丝，从个人经历出发比较了1980年Duke巡演与1992年现场的舞台表现差异，最终给出五星评价。整体观点集中在怀旧情怀与现场版本相比录音室版的优势比较上。
