items.body: Review by alainPP — 1. "It Takes a Woman's Love (To Make a Man)" kicks things off with thunderous keyboards and vocals?dating back to the days when Robby and Steve traded licks; an explosive, short track that sets the tone for their signature rock style, blending heavy and folk elements.2. "Two Cents Worth" offers a similar vibe?short and energetic?though it lacks any real progressive flair.3. "Icarus - Borne on Wings of Steel" raises the bar?thank goodness, because anyone listening only to the first two tracks (as is common today) would miss out on this gem. A hard-rocking riff and vintage keyboards (featuring revolutionary Moog synths) combine to create a sort of proto-prog-metal sound. In 1975, there weren't many other bands doing this. The track relies on vocal harmonies, instrumental jamming, and?above all?a folk-prog-metal hybrid that was ahead of its time; the finale is ecstatic and defies description.4. "All the World" keeps the momentum going; it features backing vocals and orchestration, followed by a keyboard workout over a gritty riff?dynamic yet fierce. That riff reminds me of punk rock thanks to its latent aggression, while the sublime violin interlude adds a special touch unique to this band. The finale features staccato violin backing vocals reminiscent of Queen?back when both bands were experimenting with prog in their own distinct ways.5. "Child of Innocence" offers a breather after the side flip; it's a transitional track?starting with the energy of a potential radio edit (hard folk-rock) before shifting into a frenetic instrumental section that enters the realm of prog, with a hint of Thin Lizzy.6. "It's You" features violin and piano alongside a frantic folk rhythm?almost like a *bourr�e*?making it an electric and innovative track for its time. It feels like dancing in a Scottish pub on a stormy night while waiting to set sail again.7. "Mysteries and Mayhem" follows the "Child" formula: long enough to develop a prog atmosphere, yet short enough to keep the listener engaged. For me, this is the weakest track?whereas their long songs were always excellent, the shorter ones sometimes struggle to hold a prog fan's attention.8. "The Pinnacle" kicks off with a symphonic intro?grandiloquent, folk-infused prog metal at its peak! The tone, the vocals, the surrounding keyboards, and that majestic quality that made Kansas a spearhead of the genre. Personally, I'd classify them more as prog metal than symphonic rock?or perhaps right on the border between the two. The bridge?featuring a melody that Dream Theater would revisit much later?arrives while I'm talking; it just goes to show what a rock-solid track this is. Kerry and Steve show off their inventive keyboard skills; the symphonic element is front and center. A lingering, atmospheric feel, and plenty of emotion?though the guitar solo feels a bit too isolated for my taste, given the prominent role of Robby's violin. Then again, that's Kansas for you! (3.5)
items._genre: symphonic prog / hard rock / folk rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1975年的专辑将键盘、小提琴与人声交织成美式前卫摇滚的图景，融合重金属、民间元素与交响化编曲，键盘与弦乐的对位构成核心动力。多首作品以硬摇滚riff推进，中段穿插提琴独奏与管弦乐段落，高潮部分以人声和声与器乐即兴叠加。整体制作偏向主流摇滚厂牌的商业取向，小提琴与键盘的融合虽具特色，但旋律结构相对传统，缺乏实验音乐的解构性与即兴自由。对于偏好前卫实验、爵士即兴与电子声响的听众而言，这张专辑的创作手法仍偏向保守的摇滚框架内探索，融合维度有限，未能触及更广阔的跨界领域。

items.body: Krieg-B will release a new album, “Concrete Dominion,” on October 24, 2026, the same date as the band’s performance at the 19th Elektrisch Festival at Club Seilerstraße in Zwickau, Germany. The album comes via Emmo.biz Records. The label describes “Concrete Dominion” as combining the raw energy of EBM, darkwave and industrial music with powerful rhythms, massive basslines and hypnotic sequences. The album is built on the tension between human impulse and the cold architecture of machines, aiming for a soundtrack of urban atmosphere, mechanical force and relentless movement, a dark and intense journey through concrete landscapes where rhythm becomes the driving force. Formats and festival tie-in “Concrete Dominion” will be available as a CD with twelve tracks and an LP with eight tracks across two sides. The CD track list runs “Bite,” “Machinehead,” “Kill The Light,” “Cold Fragments” (feat. Misty), “Perestroika,” “Locked,” “Blackout,” “Libera Nos A Malo,” “Par Dessus Les Cendres,” “Molotov,” “New Zone Of Terror” and “Signal Ahead.” The LP carries eight of those tracks: side one holds “Bite,” “Machinehead,” “Kill The Light” and “Cold Fragments” (feat. Misty), while side two holds “Locked,” “Libera Nos A Malo,” “Molotov” and “Signal Ahead.” Emmo.biz Records is also selling bundled sets tied to the Zwickau show. A “Supporter” set pairs the LP and CD with a 10″ festival sampler featuring an exclusive 12″ mix of “Kill The Light” plus a ticket to the 19th Elektrisch Festival, and a “Fan” set bundles the LP, CD and the 10″ sampler without the ticket. A standard “Combo” set with just the LP and CD is limited to 77 copies, with the vinyl pressed on red and black streaked wax. About Krieg-B Krieg-B is a French-Belgian duo formed in June 2023 by Dominique Lallement, also known for his work as Kriegbereit, Cobalt 60 and K Bereit, and Benoît Buyse, who records as Dreadfool, Anamorphosis and Nihiliste. Based in Reims, France, the pair build on decades of industrial, EBM and darkwave music. Krieg-B released its debut album, “War Drums’ Resonance,” in September 2024 through Emmo.biz Records, in a limited edition of 77 copies that paired the 11-track record with a bonus disc holding a cover of Cabaret Voltaire’s “Nag Nag Nag” and a T-shirt. The band was confirmed for the 19th Elektrisch Festival line-up in April 2026, alongside Portion Control, Escalator, Oszylator and Cyborg Projekt X. “Concrete Dominion” is the duo’s second full-length album.
items._cn_summary: 本文为专辑发布的纯新闻稿，介绍了Krieg-B第二张全长专辑《Concrete Dominion》的发行信息。该专辑由Emmo.biz Records发行，CD收录12首曲目，黑胶收录8首。该作品融合EBM、工业和暗潮元素，以强劲的贝斯线和催眠序列为基础，试图在人类冲动与冰冷机械架构之间构建张力，被定位为都市氛围与机械力量交织的声轨。文章还详细列出了多种捆绑销售方案，包括限量77张的红黑条纹黑胶套装。原文信息偏向唱片格式、曲目列表与发行细节，对音乐本体缺乏深入分析，无法判断作品的创新性与艺术价值。

The accompanying video contrasts postcard-perfect holiday imagery with the growing environmental crisis. “This song is about
items.body: The Noise Who Runs, the UK-France project of former Sneaker Pimps member Ian Pickering, shares a video for “The Summer Talking,” the third single taken from the “Re: GenX” album. The indie-pop track pairs shimmering hooks with lyrics about climate denial, political inaction and the stories people tell themselves to avoid uncomfortable truths. The accompanying video contrasts postcard-perfect holiday imagery with the growing environmental crisis. “This song is about love, memory and self-deception, but also about a culture that keeps choosing short-term comfort over uncomfortable truths. Whether it’s a relationship, a dream of somewhere better, or believing just one more summer holiday comes without consequence, we become very good at telling ourselves what we want to hear,” Pickering says. ‘The Summer Talking’ pairs romance with climate warning Built around the refrain “it’s just the summer talking,” the song follows dreams of escape and new beginnings as they reveal themselves to be fragile, seasonal illusions. On the video, Pickering explains: “The video isn’t against holidays or people wanting to escape. It’s about why governments still refuse to treat the climate crisis with the urgency it demands. Most people want meaningful action on climate change and inequality, yet the biggest polluters continue to behave as though different rules apply to them. If we’re serious about protecting the future, governments have to lead, and the super-rich can no longer be exempt from the sacrifices expected of everyone else.” The Summer Talking by The Noise Who Runs “The Summer Talking” opens the “Re: GenX” album, out now via TNWR Records, whose ten tracks also include “Bang Bang,” “Trust Me I’m A Psychopath,” “This Song Sucks (Mind The Gap),” “Just The English Way,” “The Bodies Are Under The Bus Again,” “Home Front Truths,” “We Are Breach,” “Commercial Road” and “All Assuming You.” The song was recorded, engineered and produced by The Noise Who Runs, with additional production, mixing and mastering by Colin Cameron at The Cell Studio. About The Noise Who Runs The Noise Who Runs is the songwriting project of Ian Pickering, previously known for co-writing songs including “Spin Spin Sugar,” “6 Underground” and “Tesko Suicide” with Sneaker Pimps, and for his work with Front Line Assembly. After relocating from Hartlepool in north-east England to Lille, France, Pickering released The Noise Who Runs’ “Preteretrospective” album in 2023, followed by the “Come and Join the Beautiful Army” EP in 2024. Side-Line has followed the project’s singles since 2023, including “Tune Out, Turn Off, Drop In,” “Bang Bang” and “Commercial Road.” “Re: GenX,” described by Pickering as addressing war, consumerism, inequality and the erosion of collective responsibility, is out now via TNWR Records, with “The Summer Talking” its third single.
items._genre: indie pop / electronic pop / synth pop
items._cn_summary: 这是Sneaker Pimps前成员Ian Pickering的个人项目The Noise Who Runs发布的单曲'The Summer Talking'及相关专辑'Re: GenX'的宣传报道。文章重点介绍了歌曲主题——将气候危机、政治不作为与自我欺骗并置，歌词围绕'只是夏天的低语'这一副歌展开，探讨逃避与幻觉之间的关系。MV以度假影像与环保危机形成视觉对比。制作上由Pickering本人录音与制作，Colin Cameron负责混音与母带。整体风格定位为indie-pop，带有shimmering hooks的电子流行质感。该文为典型新闻稿性质，缺乏对音乐本体（编曲结构、音色设计、声音层次）的深入评论，信息以宣传发布为主。

items.body: German EBM project Endzustand will release its second studio album, “Macht Gesellschaft”, on September 11, 2026, through Echozone. The project began as a one-man project and has since evolved into a duo. Echozone describes “Macht Gesellschaft” as combining hard EBM with socially critical lyrics, in line with its predecessor, but harder and more cynical. The album follows the July 2026 single “Maschinenangst,” which aimed its lyrics at artificial intelligence, social networks and the growing weight of technology on daily life. Second album continues Endzustand’s social critique The band mixes classic EBM rhythms with lyrics addressing technology, control and society. The band’s 1980s reference points include acts such as Nitzer Ebb, Die Krupps and DAF. “Macht Gesellschaft” carries that approach further, with Echozone describing the album’s tone as more cynical than its predecessor while keeping its focus on social criticism. About Endzustand Endzustand is the EBM project of Ralf Rönckendorf, a former German soldier who lost his eyesight and three comrades during a 2010 mission in Afghanistan. Rönckendorf built the project around classic electronic body music, using it to process his experience through bold lyrics and straightforward EBM rhythms. Endzustand released the single “Hass” in September 2020, followed by its debut studio album, “Werk des Krieges,” in October 2020 via Echozone, and the “Roter Freitag” EP in 2021. The project now records as a duo, with Rönckendorf joined by Rudi on drums. Endzustand returned in July 2026 with the single “Maschinenangst,” the opening preview of “Macht Gesellschaft,” the duo’s second studio album, due September 11, 2026.
items._cn_summary: Endzustand 是一支德国 EBM 双人项目，核心成员 Ralf Rönckendorf 曾在2010年阿富汗任务中负伤失明。新专辑「Macht Gesellschaft」由独立厂牌 Echozone 发行，以经典 EBM 节奏为骨架，融合 Nitzer Ebb、Die Krupps、DAF 等八十年代工业电子的血脉。歌词延续前作的社会批判路线，聚焦人工智能、社交网络与技术对日常生活的侵蚀，整体语气被厂牌形容为比首张专辑「Werk des Krieges」更为冷硬与愤世嫉俗。先行单曲「Maschinenangst」于2026年7月释出，Rudi 加盟负责鼓机部分后，二人编制带来比早期独奏时期更厚重的工业张力。对于偏好工业电子与暗潮的听众而言，这张专辑延续了欧陆 EBM 的传统脉络，但音乐本身并无实验性突破或跨类型融合倾向。

items.body: Synthwave act GUNSHIP have released an official music video for “Time After Time,” their cover of Cyndi Lauper’s song featured on the soundtrack of Corin Hardy’s 2026 supernatural horror film “Whistle.” Hardy directed the video himself, built around previously unseen footage from the film. The DVD and BluRay release of “Whistle” is set for August 28, 2026. The video revives the movie-and-music-video tie-in tradition of the MTV era, pairing the song with an extended sequence cut from the finished film. “Whistle” follows a group of high school students who discover a cursed Aztec death whistle, stars Dafne Keen, Sophie Nélisse, Sky Yang, Jhaleil Swaby, Ali Skovbye, Percy Hynes White and Nick Frost, and had reached the number one spot on Amazon Horror and on VOD charts in the US and UK following its February 2026 theatrical release. GUNSHIP and Hardy resurrect a lost sequence “Working with Corin is a total dream,” GUNSHIP stated. “He’s an old friend who we bonded with over our love for cinema and music, and we were honored to have our song featured in the film. After the Whistle premiere, we were chatting over a pint, and he told us about a beautiful pseudo ‘one shot’ sequence he was heartbroken to lose in the final film. We suggested resurrecting it and using it as a music video. Corin got it immediately and the result is perfect. It’s heartbreaking, haunting and pure 80s noir soaked.” Corin Hardy described the pairing in similar terms: “I wanted Whistle to feel like a horror movie I might have watched around the late 1980’s, alongside films like A Nightmare on Elm Street, The Lost Boys, and The Breakfast Club. Films steeped in teen-angst and heightened feelings. Music was such a huge part of creating the romance of those cinematic worlds. Gunship’s synth-drenched cover of Cyndi Lauper’s ‘Time After Time’ was always top of my list. Their unique heart-on-your-sleeve sound was the perfect choice for a key moment in the movie. To come together post-release and create this extended music video is simply the cherry on top. Dan, Al & Al (Gunship) have provided the film a real companion piece in the world of Whistle… it makes me want my MTV again!” The collaboration extends GUNSHIP’s history with Hardy, who previously contributed vocals to the band’s track “Cthulhu.” “Whistle” is produced by No Trace Camping and Wild Atlantic Pictures and distributed by IFC Films, Shudder and Black Bear. About GUNSHIP GUNSHIP is Dan Haigh, Alex Westaway and Alex Gingell. The band builds its sound with vintage analog synthesizers and retro electronic gear from the 1980s, combining sweeping synth lines with driving electric bass arpeggios. GUNSHIP released the album “Unicorn” across five formats in October 2023. The band’s track “Cthulhu” features guest vocals from Corin Hardy, a collaboration that grew out of the pair’s shared interest in horror and cinema. “Time After Time,” GUNSHIP’s cover of the 1984 Cyndi Lauper song, was placed on the soundtrack of Hardy’s film “Whistle,” and the new official video marks the latest chapter in the band and director’s ongoing work together.
items._cn_summary: GUNSHIP为Cyndi Lauper经典曲目《Time After Time》制作了合成器驱动的翻唱版本，搭载于Corin Hardy导演的2026年恐怖电影《Whistle》原声带中。乐队以八十年代模拟合成器和复古电子设备构建声音，融合扫弦合成器音色与电贝斯琶音，呈现出怀旧的暗潮质感。音乐视频由Hardy亲自执导，取自电影正片中删减的长镜头片段，复刻了MTV时代电影与音乐视频联动的传统。GUNSHIP与Hardy此前的合作可追溯至乐队曲目《Cthulhu》，双方因对电影与音乐的共同热爱而再次携手。该作品延续了八十年代青春恐怖片的视听美学，与《猛鬼街》《迷幻所》《早餐俱乐部》等经典作品形成跨时空呼应。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Karate Boogaloo have been playing together since they were schoolboys, in the same Melbourne high school maths class, which is the sort of fact most bands turn into a claim about chemistry. Ask what twenty years of it buys them and Henry Jenkins offers elbow grease and luck, and reckons anyone could do what they do. Except only they can… What they do is instrumental funk and soul: bass, drums, organ and guitar, cut to tape, with nobody singing over the top. It runs in both directions. Across three volumes of the KB’s Mixtapes series the four of them play by hand the records hip-hop producers sampled, and away from KB, they cut new library music as Frollen Music Library for producers to sample in turn, which is how their playing reached ScHoolboy Q‘s “Smile” and Leon Thomas’s Mutt. Access All Areas, out on 9 October, holds to that and clears out the rest. Eleven tracks, and as the release notes have it, “if a tune became convoluted, to the bin it went”. It comes through Colemine Records in Loveland, Ohio and College of Knowledge Records in Coburg, Melbourne, the second album the two labels have shared. For the first time the band handed the recording to someone else. Alex Bennett cut it at Sound Recordings in Castlemaine, on tape machines built between the 1950s and the 1980s, all of them kept running by his own hand. Jenkins plays bass, Hudson Whitlock drums, Callum Riley organ, Darvid Thor guitar. They got here the long way, first as the rhythm section of The Cactus Channel, then Hold Your Horses in 2024. With Access All Areas a few months out, we put a handful of questions to the band, and Jenkins answered for all four, correcting half the rules KB are known for, keeping Thor’s fugues off the record, and leaving the question of why Melbourne sounds like this to a local historian who does not yet exist… You’ve been playing together since you were preteens in the same high school maths class, and the new record marks nearly twenty years of that. What can four people who’ve known each other that long do musically that a newer band simply can’t fake? We’re afraid it’s difficult for us to make that claim, with a little bit of elbow grease anyone can do what we do. Luck has been the key ingredient, it has come careening our way on many occasions. It has to if you’re blessed to play music with your best mates for as long as we have. KB started as the rhythm section of The Cactus Channel and got described early on as a “side project”. At what point did it stop feeling like a side thing and become its own animal? We were originally a cover band and a cover band only. The Meters, Booker T & The MG’s, etc. Then one day we wrote a song called “Stay Healthy” and everything changed. We crossed the River Rubicon that day. The band famously imposes strict rules and guidelines on itself: tape only, no plug-ins, no edits, mono releases, four instruments and no vocalist. Where did that manifesto come from, and does the discipline ever feel like a cage rather than a tool? We’re suckers for strict rules but we’ll have to correct a few of those. We record to tape, however we do mix on the computer and we do use plug-ins. No weird plug-ins though, just Waves Doppler. The mixtapes are mono, the albums are stereo, and vocalists are expensive, rightly so. As all good manifestos are, ours is a work in process, and may it forever be. Some rules are carrots, some are sticks, KB needs both. The KB’s Mixtapes series flips hip-hop samples and film and TV themes back into instrumentals. Talk us through how you pick what to reinterpret, and how far you’ll twist something before it stops being recognisable. Imagine the film 12 Angry Men but with four guys arguing about which song to include on an obscure funk mixtape, now picture the exact opposite of that, it’s somewhere in between. When it comes to how far we’ll go, we’ll twist it until it breaks, put it back together, and then hit record. You’ve said the aim with a cover is to bend a well-known tune almost beyond recognition but not quite. Is there one you pushed too far, or one you couldn’t crack no matter how hard you tried? There’s a mountain of tunes we couldn’t crack, we can’t recall them all. We tried making an album called Come With Us, Let’s Terraform Venus and Mars, uncrackable. Access All Areas is out on 9 October through Colemine Records and College of Knowledge Records, and you’ve called it a haiku where Hold Your Horses was an epic. What made you want to strip things down this time, and what got binned in the process? All four of us were on the bus, the 504, and all of the people on the bus started singing “99 Bottles of Beer On The Wall”, we all locked eyes, inhaled, and in unison said: “Access”. Easiest decision we’ve ever made. You’ve said anything convoluted went in the bin and only tunes that could be hummed by anyone survived. What’s an example of something you loved but cut because it failed that test, and did any of you fight to keep it? Darvid composes fugues for fun, and they’re frighteningly beautiful. The world will be subjected to their majesty one day but not on this record. Darvid understands. Access All Areas is the first record you’ve made with an engineer outside the four of you, working with Alex Bennett at Sound Recordings in Castlemaine. What changes when you hand even a small part of the process to someone else? Of all Alex’s incredible traits, and there are many, perhaps the best is that from the first step into his building you feel like you’re at home and in a space you can be yourself in. It’s a wonderful studio and he’s a magnificent engineer. We could sing Alex’s praises all day. Beyond the obvious Booker T & The MG’s and The Meters lineage, there’s a lot of European film music and library music in your DNA. Which of those less-obvious influences do people miss, and who should they be digging into? A favourite at the moment is Jack Arel, a wonderful French composer who we can’t recommend enough. Melbourne’s instrumental soul world is unusually tight, bands sharing members, one studio ecosystem, College of Knowledge Records holding it together. Why do you think that particular sound took root in Melbourne specifically, rather than anywhere else? There are funky roots that go deep in this town, deeper than we know we’re sure. The answer to the question unfortunately evades us right now but something tells us there might be a lovely local historian on this very case! Eyes peeled everyone. For readers outside Australia who maybe only know KB, Surprise Chef and a few other acts, which up-and-coming Melbourne acts should they be paying attention to right now, in or out of your immediate circle? To name only the first that comes to mind, Kasinda Faase is a local legend, everyone must listen to Kasinda’s music or else. How would you describe the state of Melbourne’s music scene right now to someone who’s never been? And where in the city should they actually go to feel it? If Karate Boogaloo ran the world every record store owner and most live music venue proprietors would receive a wheelie bin full of Nobel Peace Prizes. Two bins for the places that do both! They’re the best and they’re the reason Melbourne feels great. If we listen to them we’ll all be swimming in non-stop good times. Forget the funk canon for a second. What have the four of you actually had on repeat this year, and would any of it surprise us? If we could forget it we would, trust us, it’s easier said than done. Just kidding, we don’t want to forget it at all! We love all kinds of music, the weirder the better. Except any music with even a skerrick of “A.I.” in it, that’s the other kind of weird. No thank ye. Twenty years in, with a new album about to land, what does the next 20 years have in store? If we play our cards right and we’re the recipients of even more luck that we don’t deserve, we might just get to do the same thing all over again. Hopefully we’ll all hear a voice from the sky bellow “pull it up!” We always close with a tricky one. In a few words, how would you introduce Karate Boogaloo to someone who’s never heard you before? Karate Boogaloo try to play stock standard instrumental funk music and miss spectacularly every time. Listen along as they work on their aim.   Access All Areas arrives on 9 October via Colemine Records and College of Knowledge Records The album is available to pre-order, alongside the rest of Karate Boogaloo's catalogue, on Bandcamp   The post Interview: Q&A with Karate Boogaloo – “Some Rules Are Carrots, Some Are Sticks” (July 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于墨尔本乐队Karate Boogaloo的Q&A采访式乐评。乐队由四人组成，自中学时期便在一起演奏，至今已有近二十年。他们演奏器乐放克与灵魂乐，使用贝斯、鼓、风琴和吉他，全程磁带录制，无人声演唱。文章介绍了乐队从The Cactus Channel节奏组起步的历史，以及他们为嘻哈制作人制作可采样的库音乐（Frollen Music Library）的工作，其演奏曾被ScHoolboy Q采样。新专辑《Access All Areas》由Colemine Records和College of Knowledge Records联合发行，强调简洁直接——'复杂的曲子直接丢弃'。这是该厂牌组合发行的第二张专辑，首次将录音交给外部工程师Alex Bennett，使用1950至1980年代的磁带设备完成。文章以问答形式展开，成员Henry Jenkins代表全队回答，探讨了乐队的'规则与准则'及其演变过程。

items.body: Rising Appalachia‘s “Chance at Wholesome” is a folk song about a specific type of man: the one who performs devotion and withholds it, who lights a fire and vanishes before it catches, who offers the shape of love without the substance. Leah Song and Chloe Smith sing him down in close harmony. The sisters were born in Atlanta and have long been based in Asheville, in the North Carolina mountains, where they took up clawhammer banjo and fiddle in their twenties after a childhood of classical piano and weekends at fiddle conventions across the Southeast. Twenty years of Rising Appalachia has carried them from busking in New Orleans to Red Rocks and NPR’s Tiny Desk, all of it self-managed and independently financed. The group runs on sibling harmony, banjo and fiddle over world percussion, with David Brown on upright bass and baritone guitar, Duncan Wickel on fiddle and cello and Biko Casini on drums. The same lineup plays “Chance at Wholesome”, the sisters’ harmony carrying the verses. “Chance at Wholesome” is the second single from Trade My Troubles, a sixteen-track album due on 2 October, bookended by a traditional Irish traveller song and an Appalachian fiddle tune. The US autumn tour opens with two nights at Pisgah Brewing in Black Mountain, the band’s annual Hurricane Helene commemoration shows, then runs through the Southeast to Moab Folk Festival before finishing in New York. Stream “Chance at Wholesome” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Rising Appalachia – Chance at Wholesome appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: Rising Appalachia由姐妹Leah Song和Chloe Smith组成，以班卓琴与提琴为核心，辅以世界打击乐、低音提琴和大提琴。这首《Chance at Wholesome》围绕一个虚假的虔诚者展开，姐妹的和声是歌曲的核心载体，乐器编制以原声民谣为主，歌词叙事聚焦于情感观察。新专辑《Trade My Troubles》共十六首曲目，以爱尔兰传统旅行者歌曲开篇，阿巴拉契亚提琴曲收尾，乐队独立经营、自筹资金，从新奥尔良街头演出逐步走向Red Rocks和NPR Tiny Desk舞台。文末附有秋季巡演日程与单曲试听链接。整体属于传统阿巴拉契亚民谣谱系，在用户关注的世界音乐范畴中处于偏边缘的位置，缺乏显著的跨类型融合与实验性元素。

items.body: Industrial rock act Celldweller has released a new single, “Respawn,” out now on FiXT. The track is the second single from Celldweller’s sixth studio album, “GOD MODE,” following the single “Fakebreaker” featuring SWARM and REEBZ. “Respawn” combines guitars, vocals and Klayton’s industrial production through a metal lens. The lyrics run: “I’ve died a thousand times, but I’m still here. Access has been denied, but I’m still here.” Gaming culture shapes ‘GOD MODE’ Klayton built “GOD MODE” around gaming and game culture across different eras. “Spending my formative years in the 1980’s, gaming systems like the ATARI 2600 (I had the Sears knockoff) and ColecoVision were important and iconic to me,” he stated. “Those memories sparked the concept for my new album GOD MODE, an album revolving around gaming and game culture across different eras, which makes the concept of my next single ‘Respawn’ self-explanatory. I was inspired to throw elements of metal, industrial and punk-rock into a blender to see what would spawn. Lyrically it’s a reminder to myself that even when things seem dire, hopeless, or fatal, I will respawn.” “Respawn” is available now on all major streaming platforms from FiXT. A “GOD MODE” Season Pass with bonus tracks and early access to upcoming singles is available exclusively through EVEN. About Celldweller Celldweller is the primary recording project of Klayton, who also records as Scandroid and produces under Circle of Dust and FreqGen. Klayton founded FiXT as an independent, artist-owned label in 2006 together with James Rhodes. Celldweller’s discography includes the self-titled debut album (2003), “Wish Upon a Blackstar” (2012), “End of an Empire” (2015), “End of an Empire – Chapter 3: Dreams”, “Offworld” (2017) and “Satellites” (2022). Klayton returned with the single “My Disintegration” in 2019, and FiXT’s roster has since grown to include acts such as Scandroid, The Browning and THE DEFECT. “GOD MODE,” Celldweller’s sixth studio album, is now underway, with “Respawn” following the album’s opening single “Fakebreaker.”

items.body: Chicago industrial and EBM act The Ineffectuals released “INFX: EP01” on July 22, 2026. The four-track EP is digital-only via Bandcamp and marks the first release in a planned series under the band’s INFX alias. The tracklist runs “Disinformation,” “Blow My Top,” “Ultramagnetic Field” and “Cloning Technique.” The release is the “first in a series of EPs under the INFX moniker.” INFX: EP01 by The Ineffectuals The INFX moniker returns The Ineffectuals first used the INFX name in 2022, for the all-electronic six-track release “Tempered Expectations,” made in the Pilsen neighborhood of Chicago between 2020 and 2022. “INFX: EP01” revives that alias for the band’s purely electronic material, separate from the guitar-and-bass lineup used on their full-length albums. About The Ineffectuals The Ineffectuals is the Chicago project of Jeremiah Meece and Tim Nordberg, based in the city’s Pilsen neighborhood. The two began by making electronic music together before expanding the sound for live performance with vocals and bass guitar. Their debut release, “Tempered Expectations,” came out on April 1, 2022 under the INFX name, running six tracks: “Poppers,” “German Cars,” “Unplanned Euthanasia,” “Venereal Horrors,” “Sybaris” and “Decomission.” The band’s first self-released full-length as The Ineffectuals, “First Offering,” followed on February 29, 2024, with ten tracks including “Son of C.H.U.D.,” “Ducktator” and “Gimme a Hit.” Reviewing the album in July 2024, I Die: You Die described it as a mix of “post-punk, synthpunk, and EBM.” A second album, “The Serious One,” arrived on November 1, 2025, with eleven tracks including “The Mimic,” “Birth” and “Infanticide.” “INFX: EP01” continues the project’s pattern of alternating full-band albums under The Ineffectuals name with shorter, more electronic-focused releases under the INFX alias, and opens a new series of EPs in that vein.

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: Bruckner began his Symphony No. 7 in September 1881, soon after finishing the Sixth, and completed the finale in the late summer of 1883. He was fifty-nine, and his symphonies were still meeting resistance in Vienna. This is the work that changed his fortunes, and it did so not at home but in Germany. Arthur Nikisch conducted the premiere in Leipzig in December 1884. The success was genuine, though not unanimous. Hermann Levi’s Munich performance ten weeks later settled the matter. The score asks for pairs of woodwinds, four horns, trumpets and trombones, a contrabass tuba, timpani and strings. The weight comes from the depth of the brass rather than sheer numbers. Four Wagner tubas supply the work’s unique color, utilized here for the first time in a symphony and featured only in the Adagio and the finale. The first movement opens with one of the longest melodies in the repertoire, an arch given to the horn and cellos over a hushed string tremolo. The finale closes by bringing that same theme back in its original solemn form. The Adagio was begun in the expectation of Wagner’s death and finished after the news came, and Bruckner described its closing pages as music of mourning for the master. The Adagio’s great climax carries a cymbal clash, a triangle and a timpani roll that were not in his first draft. They came from his conductor-disciples and were entered later on a slip pasted into the score in his own hand. Robert Haas struck them out in his 1944 edition, and Leopold Nowak restored them ten years later. Conductors have taken sides ever since, which is why the peak of the slow movement lands differently from one recording to the next. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the best recordings of Bruckner’s Symphony No. 7. Staatskapelle Dresden, Eugen Jochum Jochum’s Dresden Seventh is rightfully remembered for its extraordinary Adagio. The central movement glows from within, its long crescendo unfolding on brass tones that are simultaneously burnished and unmistakably human. What elevates this reading beyond a mere exercise in atmospheric beauty is the relentless architectural tension Jochum sustains across the entire canvas. The glorious Adagio never feels isolated, instead arriving as an inevitable emotional destination. He achieves this by subtly flexing the tempo to delineate each structural shift, an interpretive choice that has fascinated listeners for decades. This remains a definitive benchmark against which other interpretations are constantly judged. Jochum Amazon Presto Apple Berlin Philharmonic, Günter Wand Wand brought decades of hard-won Bruckner experience to his guest appearances in Berlin. That deep familiarity shines through in the sheer breadth of his phrasing. He allows every musical span to breathe fully without ever letting the underlying pulse sag. The orchestra retains an astonishing transparency even during the heaviest sections, ensuring quiet woodwind figures in the Scherzo hold their distinct place rather than vanishing. Opting for the edition that leaves the Adagio’s climax entirely to strings and brass, he builds the peak so convincingly that listeners miss no extra percussion. Only in the final bars does the texture slightly tilt as the trumpets surge forward. Wand Amazon Presto Apple Vienna Philharmonic, Herbert von Karajan Karajan recorded the Seventh three times in the studio. This Vienna account, taped in 1989, stands apart as a personal farewell. Where his earlier Berlin versions felt monumental and grand, this interpretation glows with a fragile grace. The Adagio expands into a sublime elegy that retains its pristine architectural form throughout. Bathed in the warm sheen of the Vienna strings, the sound offers remarkable clarity and depth. Some listeners find the finale slightly less cohesive than the preceding movements. Yet few recordings manage to hold raw symphonic power and delicate vulnerability in such exquisite equilibrium. Karajan Amazon Presto Apple Berlin Radio Symphony Orchestra, Riccardo Chailly Chailly favors broad tempos, yet he never allows the phrasing to go slack. A deep, steady momentum carries the first movement forward, giving even its most sprawling sections a clear sense of destination. This structural clarity is precisely what makes the recording so admired, alongside audio engineering that remains stunningly realistic. The dividing factor is the emotional temperature. Some find this studio account slightly reserved compared to the thrilling spontaneity Chailly often brings to the concert hall. Regardless of where you stand on that restraint, his grasp of the symphony’s architecture is never in question. Chailly Amazon Presto Apple Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Bernard Haitink Haitink’s second Amsterdam recording stands as a quiet masterpiece of the catalog. The Concertgebouw delivers an even, luminous warmth from the opening bar to the final chord. Haitink navigates Bruckner’s great sonic blocks so seamlessly that the symphony flows without ever feeling segmented. The Adagio alone justifies adding this album to any collection. Its towering climax, cymbals included, is balanced with rare taste and proportion. If you prize sheer lyrical beauty over thunderous theatricality, begin your journey here. Haitink Amazon Presto Apple Vienna Philharmonic, Nikolaus Harnoncourt Striking velocity defines Harnoncourt’s interpretive approach from the very first notes. He moves noticeably faster than most peers while shining a revealing spotlight on the orchestra’s inner voices. Consequently, the opening theme carries an unsettling edge rather than standard serene devotion. Clean audio engineering preserves a natural perspective, ensuring the strings never overwhelm subordinate details. The cymbal crash at the peak of the Adagio is omitted, but listeners receive wonderfully dark Wagner tubas and a fierce, driving Scherzo. The nimble finale sparkles, powered by triumphant brass playing. Harnoncourt Amazon Presto Apple Munich Philharmonic, Sergiu Celibidache Celibidache’s idiosyncratic style regularly polarizes critical opinion, but this live 1984 concert makes a compelling case for his unique artistic vision. Spanning roughly seventy-four minutes, the performance moves at a famously expansive pace yet miraculously maintains forward momentum. The conductor unfailingly understands the ultimate trajectory of every phrase, shaping lines with complete authority. Munich’s elite instrumentalists respond with flawless execution and immaculate orchestral balance. While this smooth sculpting may occasionally push legato phrasing further than purists prefer, the archival sound is remarkably clear. Even admirers of the slower remake he made a decade later often return to this leaner, earlier one. Celibidache Amazon Presto Apple Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra, Manfred Honeck Few modern releases match this performance for sheer sonic spectacle. Taped in 2022, the recording boasts an enormous dynamic range, keeping complex counterpoint wonderfully clear even during cataclysmic peaks. Honeck builds his climaxes with immense patience and care. In the Adagio, he highlights a recurring phrase echoing the Te Deum, investing each return with distinct character. A rustic, swinging lilt in the Scherzo successfully summons the country dance hidden beneath the score. Minor caveats include an opening movement that feels sluggish at first and a heavily stretched final chord that crosses into engineering excess. Still, it is a formidable state-of-the-art showcase. Sanderling strikes the ideal tempo right away and holds it steady throughout. The grave, unhurried Adagio allows the Wagner tubas to deliver a lament of heartbreaking emotional weight. The brilliantly handled finale sets this performance apart from rivals. Sanderling draws sharp contrasts between quick and slow episodes, capturing the movement’s perpetual shift between humor and solemnity. Orchestral balances are so finely judged that no single section swamps another, keeping the vital horn counterlines fully audible. The stunning coda transitions effortlessly from desolation to consolation. Tintner masterfully evades this trap by identifying the exact, natural tempo for every musical thought. The opening movement generates substantial power, ensuring the Adagio feels like a logical consequence rather than an abrupt shift in focus. Employing the score edition that strips away added percussion from the slow movement’s climax offers a clear window into an old musicological debate. Both outer movements land their final codas with unerring precision. This thoughtful reading remains exceptionally difficult to fault, offering endless rewards. items.body:
Singapore's beloved R&B trio brb. are coming home. The homegrown act have announced their biggest local headline show in recent years, bringing the half/lives Tour to *SCAPE Ground Theatre on 13 December. The concert follows a milestone period for the trio, who have spent the past few years expanding their reach across Asia and North America while evolving their signature blend of nostalgic R&B, soul, hip-hop, and electronic pop.

Formed in 2018 by Auzaie Zie (Zie), Clarence Liew Oliveiro (CLO), and Marc Lian, brb. have steadily established themselves as one of Singapore's defining contemporary acts. Their recent releases — the blueprint and the EP lucky — mark a new chapter for the trio, showcasing a richer, moodier, and more sonically expansive sound while retaining the chemistry that has become synonymous with the band.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Live Nation SG (@livenationsg)

The Singapore stop also arrives after an impressive run of international touring. Over the years, brb. have performed across Southeast Asia, East Asia, and North America, with shows in cities including Seoul, Tokyo, Bangkok, New York City, and Los Angeles. Now, the trio are set to bring everything they've learned on the road back to home soil with the half/lives Tour.

Ticket details:

Live Nation Presale: 30 July, 2 PM – 11:59 PM

General Sale: 31 July, 10 AM

Tickets: Ticketmaster Singapore

items.body:
After wrapping up a successful North American run, yung kai is heading back to the region this autumn with his biggest Asia tour to date. The stay with the ocean, i'll find you: Asia 2026 tour will see the Canadian indie-pop artist perform across nine cities, beginning in Shanghai before making stops in Bangkok, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Manila, Taipei, Hong Kong, Seoul, and Tokyo. Click here for ticketing details.

Asia 2026 tour dates

30 October — Shanghai, Star@ Culture Center

1 November — Bangkok, Sphere Hall

3 November — Singapore, Capitol Theatre

6 November — Kuala Lumpur, Zepp Kuala Lumpur

9 November — Manila, New Frontier Theater

11 November — Taipei, Zepp New Taipei

13 November — Hong Kong, TIDES

16 November — Seoul, Myunghwa Live Hall

19 November — Tokyo, Ebisu The Garden Hall

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by yung kai (@ykaizzk)

Returning to a region that embraced him during his sold-out 2025 tour, yung kai shared his excitement in a statement: "Asia don't you worry... yung kai is back!!!!!"

Known for his dreamy alternative indie-pop sound, yung kai draws from both his Chinese and Canadian heritage, blending Eastern and Western influences into emotionally rich songwriting. After debuting in 2022, he broke through globally with 'blue', which has amassed more than two billion streams and earned Gold certifications in both the US and Canada. He later released his debut album, stay with the ocean, i'll find you, and was nominated for the JUNO Breakthrough Artist of the Year award.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Live Nation SG (@livenationsg)

items.body:
Fans of Jujutsu Kaisen are about to step into the world of curses in an entirely new way. Jujutsu Kaisen in Concert is set to make its Singapore debut at the Esplanade Theatre on 31 October, bringing the hit anime's iconic soundtrack to life with a live band and cinematic visuals. Tickets are on sale now.

The concert promises an immersive audiovisual experience, pairing scenes from all three seasons of the anime on a giant HD cinema screen with live performances by a hybrid ensemble of classical and modern musicians. From Gojo's emotional backstory to the devastating events of the Shibuya Incident, the production aims to recreate the series' biggest moments in full cinematic sound.

"This concert brings those elements together in a live setting, combining an exceptional band with cinematic visuals to present the story in a way that is both faithful to the original work and elevated by the power of live performance," said Floris Douwes, Producer and Managing Director at GEA Live.

Produced by GEA Live and RoadCo Entertainment in partnership with TOHO Co., Ltd., Jujutsu Kaisen in Concert marks the first time fans will be able to experience the anime's acclaimed score in a dedicated live concert setting. Beyond the music, audiences can expect a synchronized visual presentation that follows the emotional highs, heartbreaking losses, and explosive battles that have made the franchise a global phenomenon.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by JUJUTSU KAISEN EN (@jujutsukaisen)

The anime has continued to dominate worldwide since its debut, becoming the first series to win Crunchyroll's Anime of the Year award twice. It has also earned recognition from the Tokyo Anime Award Festival and was named the world's most in-demand TV series and anime at the 2024 Global Demand Awards, cementing its place as one of the defining anime franchises of its generation.

items.body: ■ 1. 概念の基本情報バイオグラフィカル・ディスラプションは、イギリスの医療社会学者マイケル・バリーが、関節リウマチ患者への聞き取り調査をもとに1982年の論文で提示した概念です。出典は Bury, M. (1982) “Chronic illness as biographical disruption”, Sociology of Health and Illness, 4(2), 167-182。論文原文（アブストラクト・書誌情報）https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/1467-9566.ep11339939この論文でバリーは、慢性疾患を「破壊的な経験の一種」として概念化し、この破壊が個人の認知的・物質的資源、痛みや苦しみの説明様式、専門家の知と素人の知の連続性・非連続性、経験のばらつきの源泉などを浮き彫りにする、と述べています。1970年代後半のフィールドワークで、関節リウマチの診断が日常生活の構造そのものを崩すという洞察を得たことが出発点でした。■ 2. バリーが示した「破壊」の中身（3つの要素）複数の二次文献を総合すると、バリーが提示した破壊の要素は概ね次の3つに整理されます。1）当たり前とされていた前提や行動様式の破壊 それまで意識せずに機能していた身体（沈黙していた身体）が、痛みや不調として意識に上ってくる状態。研究者はこれを「身体の非‐現前化（corporeal dys-appearance）」とも呼びます。2）説明の枠組みの破壊 「なぜ自分が」「なぜ今なのか」という問いが生まれ、近代医療の枠内だけでは答えが見つからないため、当事者は自分なりに病の意味を編み直す「ナラティブの再構築（narrative reconstruction）」に向かわざるを得なくなる。3）資源の動員という反応 時間、エネルギー、経済力、家族・友人からの支援といった資源を再配分し、破壊に直面しながら「正常さ」を取り戻そうとする（バリー自身の言葉では ‘normalise in the face of disruption’）。この整理を扱った解説記事https://healthtopic.org/topics/biographical-disruption-and-chronic-illness-a-critical-reflection/■ 3. 理論的な位置づけ・同時代の隣接概念バリーの議論は孤立して生まれたわけではなく、同時代の複数の理論と響き合っています。・アンソニー・ギデンズの「決定的状況（critical situations）」論（1979年）・アンセルム・ストラウスとバーニー・グレイザーの慢性疾患論（1975年）・キャシー・シャーマズ（Kathy Charmaz）の「自己の喪失（loss of self）」論（1983年）・ゲレス・ウィリアムズ（Gareth Williams）の「ナラティブの再構築」論（1984年）これらをまとめて紹介している文献（Springer, Locock & Ziebland執筆の追悼的レビュー章）https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1057/9781137355621_37■ 4. 概念の発展・派生バリエーションバリー自身、および後続の研究者によって、オリジナルの「破壊」モデルは以下のように分岐・拡張されてきました。・バイオグラフィカル・リインフォースメント（biographical reinforcement：伝記的強化） Carricaburu, D. and Pierret, J. (1995) “From biographical disruption to biographical reinforcement: the case of HIV-positive men”, Sociology of Health and Illness, 17, 65-88。 同性愛や血友病を背景に持つHIV陽性男性44名への聞き取りから、感染がむしろ既存のアイデンティティ（同性愛者・血友病患者としての自己）を「強化」する側面があることを示し、破壊一辺倒のモデルを相対化しました。 https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1467-9566.ep10934486・バイオグラフィカル・フロー（biographical flow：伝記的連続性・流れ） Faircloth ら（2004年）が提唱。年齢や社会経済的困難などの文脈次第では、疾患は「破壊」ではなく「あらかじめ予期されたもの」として経験されうるという議論。脳卒中回復のナラティブへの応用例 https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8673288_Sudden_Illness_and_Biographical_Flow_in_Narratives_of_Stroke_Recovery・ノーマル・イルネス（normal illness：正常化された病）／バイオグラフィカル・コンティニュイティ（biographical continuity） ウィリアムズ（2000年、後述）が提示。先天性疾患や幼少期からの障害では「断裂」ではなく「連続性」が経験の核になるとする視点。・ナラティブズ・オブ・アンコンサーン（narratives of unconcern：無頓着のナラティブ） Harris, M. (2009) “Troubling biographical disruption: Narratives of unconcern about hepatitis C diagnosis”, Sociology of Health and Illness, 31(7), 1028-1042。C型肝炎診断者の一部が診断を「たいしたことではない」として語る現象を分析し、破壊モデルの普遍性に疑義を呈しました。・バイオグラフィカル・イルミネーション（biographical illumination：伝記的“照らし出し”） Tan, D. (2018) “‘I'm a normal autistic person, not an abnormal neurotypical’: Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis as biographical illumination”, Social Science & Medicine。成人期に自閉スペクトラム症の診断を受けた人々の経験は「破壊」というより、これまでの人生を新しい視点から「照らし出し」意味づけ直す経験だとして、破壊とは異なる方向の再構成を提示しました。 https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953617307384・バイオグラフィカル・ディアレクティクス（biographical dialectics）／エンボディド・ダイアレクティクス（embodied dialectics） Cluley らが人工透析患者の経験から提示した概念で、過去と現在の身体経験がせめぎ合う「生産的な緊張」を強調。脳卒中サバイバーへの応用（2024年の論文） https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12592587/・バイオグラフィカル・リペア（biographical repair：伝記的修復） 説明困難な身体症状（persistent physical symptoms）のクリニックで、症状に「説明」が与えられることが破壊された物語を修復する契機になるとする研究 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11195018/・ペアレンタル・バイオグラフィカル・スペクトラム（親の伝記的スペクトラム：断裂⇔結束） 子どもが自閉症と診断された親の経験を、断裂（grief）と結束・意味の一貫性（relief, cohesion）の両極からなるスペクトラムとして描いた研究 https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953619306689・バイオグラフィカル・リインベンション（biographical reinvention） インドネシアのHIV陽性男性を対象に、資産（asset）に基づくレジリエンス戦略として自己と将来像を「再発明」する過程を描いた2023年の研究 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10454460/■ 5. 批判・理論的な相対化概念の代表的な批判的検討は、ゲレス・ウィリアムズによる以下の論文です。Williams, S. (2000) “Chronic illness as biographical disruption or biographical disruption as chronic illness? Reflections on a core concept”, Sociology of Health and Illness, 22(1), 40-67。概要（Semantic Scholar）https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Chronic-illness-as-biographical-disruption-or-as-on-Williams/b532fdaf3ca0c6d662a895d2e5799a8fc089bcf6ウィリアムズが指摘した主な論点は以下の通りです。・概念が身体的経験そのものより、分析概念としての整合性を優先しすぎているという批判・「なぜ自分が」という驚きを前提にしているが、実際には人によって疾患は「予期されたもの」「不利の一形態にすぎないもの」「たまにしか破壊的にならないもの」など多様である・概念が「成人になってから発症する病」を暗黙のモデルにしており、出生時あるいは幼少期からの疾患・障害では、断裂ではなく連続性こそが経験の中心になりうる・タイミングと文脈（年齢、ライフステージ、社会経済的状況）の重要性・喪失だけでなく連続性の側面の重要性・そもそも「伝記的破壊」自体が病の発症要因になりうる（ストレスによる発症等）という逆方向の関係さらに障害学（disability studies）からは、次のような批判が寄せられています（英語版Wikipediaのまとめ）。https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bury 「病気や障害が自己意識やアイデンティティに与える影響を過度に強調する一方で、より広い社会構造の影響を探ることを犠牲にしてしまうリスクがある」同様の指摘はアバディーン大学のリポジトリ論文にも詳しく整理されています。https://abdn.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/biographical-disruption/ 同論文は、批判者たちが「一部の人は破壊を経験せず、病を人生の“普通の一部”として組み込んだり、単なる“もう一つの不利”として経験したり、断続的にしか破壊的でないと感じたりする」と論じていること、また「個人の感情的反応に焦点を当てすぎ、障害の影響を増幅・軽減する社会構造への注意が不足している」との指摘があることを紹介しています。年齢・エスニシティ・ジェンダーといった社会構造との交差を扱った実証研究の例（オーストラリアの難民家庭出身の23歳男性のライフヒストリー）https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31359462/■ 6. 各領域への応用例（分野別）がんサバイバーシップ言説における「生存」の意味づけを問い直す研究などで、実存的不安・自己喪失（Charmaz）・伝記的破壊（Bury, Williams）が併せて参照されています。https://www.researchgate.net/publication/227509837_Chronic_Illness_as_Biographical_Disruption_or_Biographical_Disruption_as_Chronic_Illness_Reflections_on_a_Core_ConceptHIV／エイズ前述のCarricaburu & Pierret (1995) が代表的研究。近年ではHIV診断が「破壊」と「強化」の両方を同時にもたらす複合的経験であることを示す研究も出ています。Wells, N. et al. (2023) “HIV Diagnosis as Both Biographical Disruption and Biographical Reinforcement”, Qualitative Health Research, 33, 165-175（上記の再発明論文の参考文献リストで確認可）自閉スペクトラム症（自閉症）成人期診断における「破壊」対「照らし出し（illumination）」の対比のほか、後年に診断を受けた高齢者を対象にした研究もあります。https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/21642850.2019.1684920自閉症の子を持つ母親の経験を扱った研究（Raymond-Barker et al., 2016, Journal of Intellectual and Developmental Disability）も参照されています。フレイル（虚弱・老年期の脆弱性）ケンブリッジ大学リポジトリの研究では、フレイルの診断における曖昧さが、関節リウマチにおける原因・治療の不確実性と同様に破壊経験を強めると論じられています。https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/bitstreams/f2d14bb2-e031-45b8-b0e3-e2ccaca6fc12/download臓器移植移植レシピエントの多様な身体的経験を通じて、概念の基盤である「身体性（embodiment）」を再検討した論文。https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953619300863脳卒中脳卒中サバイバーとその支援ネットワーク41名へのインタビューをもとに、身体性の理論と組み合わせた「エンボディド・ダイアレクティクス」概念を提示。https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12592587/複数疾患の併存（うつ病＋糖尿病）女性の糖尿病とうつ病の併存経験を扱い、「破壊」に加えて「再定義（redefinition）」「回復（recovery）」という新しい類型を提示。https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38069586/多発性硬化症・炎症性腸疾患（IBD）等の慢性疾患一般若年成人のIBD患者における「反復する伝記的破壊」を、過去・現在・予期される未来という時間軸から論じた研究がWiley Online Libraryの概説記事に紹介されています。https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/9781118410868.wbehibs1017顧みられない熱帯病（NTD）リベリアにおける熱帯病患者への語りの分析で、ジェンダー・世代・障害が交差しながら伝記的破壊を媒介することを示した研究。https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6750611/なお、英語版Wikipediaの記述によれば、この枠組みはがん、HIV、自閉症、フレイル、運動ニューロン疾患（ALS等）、孤独（loneliness）、メニエール病といった経験にも適用されてきたとされています（個別の論文タイトルまでは同ページに列挙されていません）。https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bury■ 7. バリー自身によるその後の展開バリーは1991年に “The sociology of chronic illness: a review of research and prospects” を発表し、概念の射程を再検討しています。また2001年には “Illness Narratives: Fact or Fiction?”（Sociology of Health and Illness, 23, 263-285）で、病の語り（illness narrative）そのものの地位を批判的に問い直しました。これらの流れは、前述の「ナラティブズ・オブ・アンコンサーン」のような、破壊を前提としない語りの発見にもつながっています。■ 8. 概念のインパクト・引用状況英語版Wikipediaによれば、1982年論文は掲載誌 Sociology of Health and Illness の歴史上もっとも被引用数の多い論文の一つとされ、2026年1月末時点で6576件の引用があるとされています。https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bury■ 9. マイケル・バリー本人についてマイケル・バリー（Mike Bury）は1945年生まれ、2025年7月22日に死去したイギリスの社会学者で、医療社会学・保健と病の社会学の分野で活躍しました。ケント州ロートン在住で、妻ジェニーとの間に娘2人がいたとされています。https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bury※注意：日本語検索では同名の投資家マイケル・バーリ（Michael Burry、映画「マネー・ショート」で知られる人物）の情報が混在しやすいですが、本稿で扱っているのは社会学者マイケル・バリーであり、別人です。■ 10. 主要文献リスト（一次・準一次資料）Bury, M. (1982) Chronic illness as biographical disruption. Sociology of Health and Illness, 4(2), 167-182.https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/1467-9566.ep11339939Williams, S. (2000) Chronic illness as biographical disruption or biographical disruption as chronic illness? Reflections on a core concept. Sociology of Health and Illness, 22(1), 40-67.https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Chronic-illness-as-biographical-disruption-or-as-on-Williams/b532fdaf3ca0c6d662a895d2e5799a8fc089bcf6Carricaburu, D. and Pierret, J. (1995) From biographical disruption to biographical reinforcement: the case of HIV-positive men. Sociology of Health and Illness, 17(1), 65-88.https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1467-9566.ep10934486Locock, L. and Ziebland, S. (2015) Mike Bury: Biographical disruption and long-term and other health conditions. In The Palgrave Handbook of Social Theory in Health, Illness and Medicine.https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1057/9781137355621_37Tan, D. (2018) “I'm a normal autistic person, not an abnormal neurotypical”: Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis as biographical illumination. Social Science & Medicine.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953617307384英語版Wikipedia「Michael Bury」（人物・概念双方の要約）https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_BuryPsychology Today によるコロナ禍とバイオグラフィカル・ディスラプションを重ねた一般向け解説https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/chronically-me/202405/chronic-illness-as-a-biographical-disruption続きをみる
items._cn_summary: 该文章并非音乐评论，而是关于英国医疗社会学者迈克尔·巴里提出的"传记断裂"概念的学术介绍。文章梳理了1982年原始论文的三个核心要素——预设行为的破坏、解释框架的破坏、资源动员反应，并梳理了同期吉登斯、斯特劳斯、查尔马兹、威廉斯等学者的关联理论。此外还介绍了后续学者对该模型的扩展，包括"传记强化""传记流动""正常化疾病""无谓叙事""传记照亮""传记辩证法"等变体概念。内容涉及大量社会学理论文献引用，与音乐完全无关，无法归入任何音乐风格类别。

items.body: ■はじめにアーヴィング・ゴフマン(1922-1982)は、カナダ出身の社会学者で、シンボリック相互作用論・ドラマトゥルギー理論の代表者として知られる。代表作『スティグマの社会学――烙印を押されたアイデンティティ』(原著 Stigma: Notes on the Management of Spoiled Identity, 1963)で展開したのが本稿の主題である「スティグマ」理論だ。この本は出版から60年以上経った今でも、社会学・心理学・福祉学・障害学・医療社会学・ジェンダー研究・広告研究など極めて広い分野で参照され続けている古典中の古典である。参考:誠信書房の解説書紹介ページでも「ゴフマンの生誕100年、没後40年が経った現在でも、ゴフマン社会学の理解は十分ではない」「難解で正体がつかめないと評される『スティグマ』は、謎めいた文章を意味するまさに『エニグマ』である」と評されている。https://www.seishinshobo.co.jp/book/b10024431.html松岡正剛の千夜千冊での紹介では、ゴフマンの経歴とスティグマ概念の射程が丁寧にまとめられている。https://1000ya.isis.ne.jp/1317.html■1. スティグマの語源スティグマ(stigma)はもともと古代ギリシャ語に由来する言葉で、奴隷・犯罪者・裏切り者であることを示すために身体に刻んだ焼き印や刺青を意味した。この印を持つ者は「穢れた者」として公共の場で避けられるべき存在とされた。その後キリスト教の文脈では、聖痕(聖なる印)という宗教的意味と、皮膚の病変という医学的意味の2層が加わり、現在ではもっぱら「不名誉の烙印」という比喩的な意味で使われている。出典(ワシントン大学の講読資料、ゴフマン原文の抜粋):http://courses.washington.edu/intro2ds/Readings/7_Goffman-stigma.doc日本語での語源解説はこちら(note記事):https://note.com/kotobakaisetsu/n/nf2be01df893a■2. スティグマの定義――「属性」ではなく「関係」ゴフマンの定義で最も重要なポイントは、スティグマを個人の固定的な「属性」としてではなく、「属性」と「ステレオタイプ」の間の特殊な関係、つまり相互行為の中で生まれる関係概念として捉えたことである。原文では次のように述べられている。「stigma、すなわち深く信用を失わせる属性を指す語として使うが、本当に必要なのは属性の言語ではなく関係の言語である」(Goffman, 1963, p.3)九州大学のガイドはこの点を非常にわかりやすくまとめている。「スティグマは属性ではなく関係を表現する言葉」であり、「常人」が他者の一面のみを見て判断するという日常のコミュニケーションによってスティグマは生まれる、としている。https://guides.lib.kyushu-u.ac.jp/c.php?g=775084&p=5559482■3. 「virtual social identity」と「actual social identity」ゴフマン理論のコアとなる概念装置が、この2つの社会的アイデンティティの区別である。・virtual social identity(見せかけの社会的アイデンティティ):見知らぬ人と出会ったとき、外見や第一印象から我々が「この人はこういう人だろう」と無意識に予期し、規範的な期待として押し付けるカテゴリーと属性。・actual social identity(実際の社会的アイデンティティ):その人が実際に持っている、証明可能なカテゴリーと属性。この2つの間に「特殊な食い違い(discrepancy)」が生じ、その人がより望ましくない種類の人物だと判明したとき、その人は「まるごとの、通常の人間」から「けがれた、値打ちを割り引かれた人間」へと私たちの心の中で縮減される。この属性がスティグマである。原文引用箇所はこちら:https://selfteachingresources.pbworks.com/f/Stigma+and+Identity+-+Goffman.pdf出版社(サイモン&シュスター)の書籍紹介ページにも同様の引用がある:https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Stigma/Erving-Goffman/9780671622442■4. スティグマの3類型ゴフマンはスティグマを大きく3つのタイプに分類した。①身体上の忌まわしさ(abominations of the body)身体的な奇形・障害・外見上の異常など、目に見える身体的差異。②個人の性格上の欠点(blemishes of individual character)意志薄弱と受け取られる性格上の欠陥。具体的には精神障害、収監歴、依存症(アルコール・薬物)、失業、自殺企図、急進的な政治的行動、同性愛などが含まれるとされる。③部族的スティグマ(tribal stigma)人種、民族、国籍、宗教など、血統を通じて世代を超えて伝わり、その血族全員を等しく「汚染」するとみなされるスティグマ。この3分類について詳しいのは以下:Sociology Guideのゴフマン解説ページhttps://www.sociologyguide.com/thinkers/erving-goffman.phpSpringerの事典項目(定義学術的に整理されている)https://link.springer.com/referenceworkentry/10.1007/978-0-387-71799-9_402UKEssaysの解説(HIVスティグマなど具体例つき)https://www.ukessays.com/essays/philosophy/the-types-and-definitions-of-stigma-philosophy-essay.php■5. 「discredited(信用を失った者)」と「discreditable(信用を失う可能性のある者)」ゴフマンはスティグマを抱える人を、スティグマが他人に「見えているか・知られているか」によって2つに区別した。・discredited(信用を失った者):スティグマがすでに可視的で、相互行為の相手に知られている状態。人種、身体障害、顔の傷など。・discreditable(信用を失う可能性のある者):スティグマがまだ知られておらず、隠すことが可能な状態。特定の性的指向、精神疾患の既往、犯罪歴、宗教など。ゴフマンはさらに踏み込んで「我々は皆、潜在的にdiscreditableである」と述べている。つまり、誰にでも「もし知られれば今のアイデンティティを台無しにするような何か」が存在するという射程の広い主張をしている。この区別を扱った学術論文(健康格差研究への応用):https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237014254_Discredited_Versus_Discreditable_Understanding_How_Shared_and_Unique_Stigma_Mechanisms_Affect_Psychological_and_Physical_Health_Disparities同論文のジャーナル版:https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01973533.2012.746612わかりやすい解説ブログ(How Communication Works):https://www.howcommunicationworks.com/blog/goffman-stigma-spoiled-identity-explainedサブカルチャー研究の文脈でのまとめ:https://haenfler.sites.grinnell.edu/subcultural-theory-and-theorists/stigma/■6. スティグマ管理の技法――passing / coveringdiscreditableな人がスティグマを隠して生活する技法が「passing(パッシング)」であり、これは「自己についての、開示されていない信用失墜情報の管理」と定義される。行動範囲を区切ったり、見せる相手(オーディエンス)を分離したり、印象操作を行ったりすることで、実際の社会的アイデンティティで分類されないよう工夫することを指す。一方、discredited(すでにスティグマが知られている)な人が用いる技法が「covering(カバーリング)」である。これはスティグマそのものを消すのではなく、そのスティグマが相手との相互行為の緊張や気詰まりを引き起こさないよう、目立たなくする・和らげる技法を指す。ただし、カバーリングによって常人に受け入れられたように見えても、それは「見せかけの受容」に過ぎないことをスティグマを持つ本人は自覚しているとゴフマンは指摘する。passingについて詳しい論文(黒人のパッシング史なども含む):https://scholarworks.wmich.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?httpsredir=1&article=2606&context=jssw原著の章立てを丁寧にまとめた書評サイト(stigma symbols, disidentifiersの概念も):https://www.morgan-klaus.com/readings/stigma.html日本語でのカバーリング/パッシングのわかりやすい解説:https://keny.jp/stigma/■7. モラル・キャリア(moral career)スティグマを持つ人が自分自身のアイデンティティについて学んでいく過程を、ゴフマンは「モラル・キャリア」と呼んだ。大きく2段階に分かれる。第1段階:何が「常人(normal)」の基準であるかを学び、その社会規範を内面化する段階。第2段階:自分自身がその基準に照らしてどの程度スティグマを負っているか、自分がどのような立場にあるのかを学ぶ段階。ゴフマンはさらに、スティグマの獲得のされ方によって複数のパターン(先天的スティグマ、人生の途中で獲得するスティグマ、後からスティグマを持つ集団に社会化されるケースなど)を区別している。詳しい解説:https://www.howcommunicationworks.com/blog/2020/12/31/goffman-stigma-spoiled-social-identity■8. 「the own」「the wise」「normals」――スティグマをめぐる3者関係ゴフマンはスティグマをめぐる相互行為の場に登場する人々を3つのカテゴリーに分けた。・the own(仲間):同じスティグマを共有する当事者同士。互いに慰め合い、独自の価値体系やサブカルチャーを形成し、連帯や実践的な対処法を提供し合う。・normals(常人):スティグマを持たない、いわゆる「普通の人々」。ただし、スティグマ者をどの程度否定的に見て、ラベル付けし、関わるかには濃淡がある。・the wise(事情通):スティグマを持たないが、家族や介護者、支援者など、当事者と近い関係にあることで内輪の事情に通じ、いわば「名誉会員」としての地位を得ている人々。ただしこの立場ゆえに、当事者と同様のスティグマが波及する「courtesy stigma(儀礼的スティグマ/巻き添えスティグマ)」を経験することもある。学術的な整理(2023年の経営学分野でのレビュー論文、非常に詳しい):https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/00076503221148441この3分類を実証的に検証した研究(潜在クラス分析):https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/segmenting-an-audience-into-the-own-the-wise-and-normals-a-latent/ブログでの平易な解説:https://soc331.wordpress.com/2013/12/09/goffman-on-stigma-own-vs-wise/原著の目次構成が確認できるアーカイブ(the own and the wise, moral career, passing, coveringなどの章立てを一覧できる):https://dokumen.pub/stigma-notes-on-the-management-of-spoiled-identity.html■9. 後続理論①:Link & Phelan(2001)によるスティグマの再概念化ゴフマンの定義は「個人志向的すぎる」「あいまいすぎる」という批判を受けてきた。これに応答したのが社会学者Bruce LinkとJo Phelanによる2001年の論文「Conceptualizing Stigma」(Annual Review of Sociology所収)である。彼らはスティグマを次の5要素の「共起」として再定義した。①ラベリング(labeling):人間の差異を区別し、ラベルを貼る②ステレオタイプ化(stereotyping):支配的な文化的信念が、ラベルを貼られた人々を望ましくない特徴と結びつける③分離(separation):ラベルを貼られた人々を「我々」と「彼ら」に分けるカテゴリーに配置する④地位の喪失と差別(status loss and discrimination):不平等な結果につながる地位喪失・差別を経験する⑤権力(power):以上のプロセスが成立するには、権力の行使が不可欠であるゴフマンの相互行為レベルの分析に対し、Link & Phelanは「権力」という構造的・マクロな次元を明示的に組み込んだ点が最大の理論的貢献とされる。原論文(Annual Reviews、有料だが要旨は無料閲覧可):https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev.soc.27.1.363Annual Review of Sociology公式ページ(別URL):https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.soc.27.1.363全文PDF(モンテフィオーレ・アインシュタイン医科大学ミラー):https://montefioreeinstein.org/documents/Original-Article-Conceptulalizing-Stigma.pdf論文の要点を整理した比較的新しい論考(2022年、定義論争を扱う):https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jep.13684Scribdで公開されている全文コピー:https://www.scribd.com/doc/215112454/Conceptualizing-Stigma-Bruce-Link-and-Jo-Phelan■10. 後続理論②:Scamblerの「felt stigma」と「enacted stigma」イギリスの医療社会学者Graham Scamblerは、1986年にてんかん患者の研究から、スティグマを2種類に区別する枠組み(hidden distress model=隠された苦悩モデル)を提示した。・enacted stigma(顕在化したスティグマ):実際に経験される差別行為そのもの。・felt stigma(感受されたスティグマ):enacted stigmaへの恐れと、それに伴う内面化された恥の感覚。実際に差別を受けていなくても生じる。Scamblerの重要な知見は、多くの慢性疾患患者にとって、実際に受ける差別(enacted stigma)よりも、差別されるかもしれないという恐れ・恥の感覚(felt stigma)の方が、当人の人生に対してより破壊的な影響を及ぼすというものだ。原論文(1986年、Sociology of Health & Illness):https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1467-9566.ep11346455てんかんとQOLについての続編論文:http://www.neurology-asia.org/articles/neuroasia-2011-16(s1)-035.pdfScambler自身による理論の概説(本人サイト、非常に読みやすい):https://www.grahamscambler.com/sociology-and-stigma-an-overview/felt/enacted区分の再検証研究:https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0277953694903964なお興味深いのは、Scambler自身が後年(2004, 2018)自分の初期理論を批判的に振り返り、「医学モデル的・欠損モデル的な障害観に加担していた」「ゴフマン的な個人主義的スティグマ観を超えて、権力構造の分析に向かうべきだ」と述べている点である。この自己批判を扱った論文:https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233712051_Re-Framing_Stigma_Felt_and_Enacted_Stigma_and_Challenges_to_the_Sociology_of_Chronic_and_Disabling_Conditions■11. ゴフマン理論への批判ゴフマン理論は影響力が大きい一方、以下のような批判も蓄積されている。①個人主義的・相互行為主義的すぎるという批判スティグマを個人間の相互行為レベルでのみ分析し、それを生み出す社会構造・権力関係(貧困、制度的差別、法制度など)への視座が弱いという批判。前述のLink & PhelanやScamblerの近年の自己批判もこの文脈にある。②スティグマを固定的な二項対立(「常人」vs「スティグマ者」)として描いてしまっているという批判北海道大学リポジトリに収録された宮内洋氏の論考「繋がらない個人のために――ゴフマン『スティグマの社会学』再考」では、ゴフマンが「差別する者」と「差別される者」という対立図式を前面に押し出したことで、逆にその図式に自ら身動きが取れなくなっている、という指摘がなされている。https://eprints.lib.hokudai.ac.jp/repo/huscap/all/29454/65_P233-244.pdf③「見せかけの受容(fictional acceptance)」の問題山口毅氏の論考「スティグマ再考――『見せかけの受容』とその回避をめぐって」は、従来のスティグマ論が「スティグマの介在する相互行為は通常の相互行為と異なる」という前提に立っていたために、ゴフマンが論じた「見せかけの受容」がもたらす問題(表面的には受け入れられていても、当人はそれが本物でないと知っている状態)を見落としてきたと指摘し、日常的でゆるやかなカミングアウトの実践を代替案として検討している。https://www.l.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~slogos/archive/27/yamaguchi2003.pdf④障害学・ラベリング理論との接続と緊張関係researchmapに公開されている論考「相互行為場面におけるスティグマ――排除と包摂をめぐる」は、ゴフマンのスティグマ論が社会学だけでなく社会心理学・社会福祉学・人類学・差別論・障害学・医療研究・エスニシティ研究・ジェンダー研究など多分野の鍵概念として使われてきた一方、当初は逸脱の社会学における「ラベリング理論」の一翼として扱われてきた経緯があり、権力関係(社会構造)とラベリングというモチーフの接続が十分検討されてこなかったと論じている。https://researchmap.jp/read0182984/misc/33299997/attachment_file.pdf⑤「感動ポルノ」的な支援のまなざしへの応用九州大学のガイドでは、あからさまな差別だけでなく「支援しようとする眼差し」自体もスティグマを固定化しうる例として、障害者を「困難にもめげずに頑張る、明るく純粋な存在」として消費する「感動ポルノ」現象を挙げ、ゴフマン理論の射程の広さを示している。https://guides.lib.kyushu-u.ac.jp/c.php?g=775084&p=5559482■12. 現代における応用分野ゴフマンのスティグマ概念は、以下のような極めて広範な分野で応用され続けている。・精神疾患スティグマ研究(public stigma / self-stigma / label avoidance / structural stigmaという類型化。Corrigan & Bink, 2016などに発展)・HIV/AIDSスティグマ研究・肥満・外見スティグマ研究・失業・生活保護スティグマ研究・LGBTQ+のカミングアウト研究(passingの概念が直接応用される)・人種スティグマ、パッシング(黒人がパッシングによって白人として生活する歴史的現象)・てんかん・慢性疾患スティグマ研究(Scamblerのfelt/enacted stigma)・経営学・組織論における「スティグマを負った組織/職業」研究(セックスワーク、ギャンブル産業など)これらの応用の広がりを概観できる論文:https://www.proquest.com/scholarly-journals/conceptualizing-stigma/docview/199727731/se-2文化とスティグマ、道徳的経験を接続する近年の理論的発展:https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953606005958高齢者のうつと自己スティグマについての実証研究例:https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/25/NCT06527625/Prot_SAP_000.pdf■13. 日本語での入門・解説リソースまとめ日本語で体系的にゴフマンのスティグマ論を学びたい場合、以下が特に有用。・九州大学附属図書館作成のガイド「アーヴィング・ゴフマンの社会学」(トップページ)https://guides.lib.kyushu-u.ac.jp/goffman・同ガイドの「スティグマ、全制的施設」ページhttps://guides.lib.kyushu-u.ac.jp/c.php?g=775084&p=5559482・松岡正剛「千夜千冊」第1317夜(ゴフマンの経歴とスティグマ論の背景を含む読み物として秀逸)https://1000ya.isis.ne.jp/1317.html・keny.jp「【社会学】ゴフマン『スティグマ』とは？」(要約が非常に整理されている)https://keny.jp/stigma/・誠信書房『スティグマ』というエニグマ(薄井明著の解説書紹介ページ)https://www.seishinshobo.co.jp/book/b10024431.html■まとめゴフマンのスティグマ理論の核心は、①スティグマを個人の属性ではなく「関係」として捉えたこと、②virtual/actual social identityという概念でその発生メカニズムを説明したこと、③discredited/discreditableという区分でスティグマの可視性による対処戦略の違いを描いたこと、④passing/coveringという具体的な管理技法を提示したこと、⑤the own/the wise/normalsという当事者を取り巻く関係構造を可視化したこと、の5点に集約できる。その後Link & Phelanが権力・構造的次元を補い、Scamblerがfelt/enacted stigmaという当事者の主観的経験の次元を掘り下げ、さらに障害学・当事者運動側からは「対立図式そのものを固定化してしまう」という批判が寄せられてきた。ゴフマン理論は完成された理論というより、60年間にわたり書き換えられ続けている「生きた理論」だと言える。続きをみる

items.album: 杉江あこ｜エットレ・ソットサス─魔法がはじまるとき、デザインは生まれる
items.tags: art sound art contemporary music improvisation
items.excerpt: 会期：2026/06/23～2026/10/04 会場：アーティゾン美術館［東京都］ 公式サイト：https://www.artizon.museum/exhibition_sp/sottsass2026/ 20世紀イタリアデザインの巨匠といわれるエットレ・ソットサスが、デザイナー集団「メンフィス」を結成してからもう40年以上が経つ。にもかかわらず、ポストモダンと評されたメンフィスが世界に与えた影響力は未だ計り知れず、これを超える思想性の高いデザイナーや集団は、その後も現われていない。むしろ、時代は再びモダンデザインという守りへ向かっているような気がしてならないのである。そうした意味で、本展はいまの世の中に対しても強烈なメッセージを残し得るに違いない。 「エットレ・ソットサス」展示風景 ©Yuya Furukawa 本展は日本初のソットサスの大規模回顧展であるとともに、アーティゾン美術館にとっては初のデザイン展として話題を集めている。同館を運営する公益財団法人石橋財団は、近年、デザイン分野の作品収集に注力し、中でもソットサスの初期から晩年におよぶコレクションを100点以上抱えるに至った
items.body: 会期：2026/06/23～2026/10/04 会場：アーティゾン美術館［東京都］ 公式サイト：https://www.artizon.museum/exhibition_sp/sottsass2026/ 20世紀イタリアデザインの巨匠といわれるエットレ・ソットサスが、デザイナー集団「メンフィス」を結成してからもう40年以上が経つ。にもかかわらず、ポストモダンと評されたメンフィスが世界に与えた影響力は未だ計り知れず、これを超える思想性の高いデザイナーや集団は、その後も現われていない。むしろ、時代は再びモダンデザインという守りへ向かっているような気がしてならないのである。そうした意味で、本展はいまの世の中に対しても強烈なメッセージを残し得るに違いない。 「エットレ・ソットサス」展示風景 ©Yuya Furukawa 本展は日本初のソットサスの大規模回顧展であるとともに、アーティゾン美術館にとっては初のデザイン展として話題を集めている。同館を運営する公益財団法人石橋財団は、近年、デザイン分野の作品収集に注力し、中でもソットサスの初期から晩年におよぶコレクションを100点以上抱えるに至ったという。幅広い分野の美術作品を所蔵する同館が、デザイン分野に目を向けた際、最も注目したのがソットサスの作品だったという点は興味深い。言い換えれば、美術の文脈でも十分に語れる作品だったということだろう。 「エットレ・ソットサス」展示風景 ©Yuya Furukawa 「エットレ・ソットサス」展示風景 ©Yuya Furukawa ソットサスがデザイナーとして歩んできた時代は、そのまま戦後のイタリア史および世界史と重なる。戦前にトリノ工科大学で学位を取得後、第二次世界大戦従軍を経て、1950年代からプロダクトや家具のデザインに本格的に携わるようになるからだ。彼の初期代表作は、何といってもオリベッティ社の真っ赤なタイプライター「ヴァレンタイン」である。本展は回顧展ということもあり、このように初期から晩年に向かってソットサスの来歴や作品を紹介する内容となっていた。インドを旅して影響を受けた東洋美術や、病床で描いた「トーテム」シリーズのドローイング、また数々のメタファーを表現したモノクロ写真シリーズなど、メンフィス結成に至るまでの経緯が手に取るようにわかり、彼の思想や作品に対する理解が進んだ。ソットサスからすればモダンデザインを考えることは容易いが、ポストモダン──すなわち「デザインとは何か」を哲学的に問い続けることほど難しいものはなかったのだろう。もちろん、デザインの基本姿勢は人々の暮らしや社会をより良くすることだ。しかし、その概念があまりに凝り固まってはいやしないか。ソットサスが生涯をかけて挑んだ活動にこそ、我々の頭を柔軟に解きほぐすヒントが隠れているように思う。 「エットレ・ソットサス」展示風景 ©Yuya Furukawa 鑑賞日：2026/06/30（火）
items._cn_summary: 该文章并非乐评，而是关于意大利后现代设计大师埃托雷·索特萨斯（Ettore Sottsass）在东京Artizon美术馆举办的回顾展评论。文章聚焦于索特萨斯的设计哲学、从早期奥利维蒂打字机到孟菲斯设计集团的历程，以及其对当代设计的影响。由于内容与音乐完全无关，无法从中提取音乐风格或进行音乐品味的匹配评估，属于非音乐领域的艺术展览评论，信息与用户关注的音乐类型无任何关联。
